notes: HANDOFF: write_scope widened to include root tsconfig.json (drizzle.config.ts wasn't covered by any workspace's typecheck script — a real gate gap, not cosmetic) and package.json (db:generate/db:migrate scripts + new devDependencies drizzle-kit/dotenv), plus doc updates in docs/TECH_STACK.md (driver + resolved-version notes) and docs/DATABASE.md (two spec-completion notes below).

Spec-completion decisions (docs/DATABASE.md updated in this PR): webhook_delivery and job_failure listed no `id` column unlike every other entity table in the section — added a surrogate bigint identity PK to both for consistency, kept delivery_id's documented uniqueness as a natural key. forge_connections.webhook_secret_ciphertext treated as nullable (not stated in the doc) since a connection can exist before its webhook is registered. repos.tier2_auto has no stated default (unlike tier3_opt_in's explicit `default false`) — left NOT NULL with no default rather than inventing one. identities/forge_connections.provider CHECK reuses the same ('github','gitea') domain since it's evidently the same concept.

'credential' in this ticket's acceptance #1 isn't a separate table — DATABASE.md has no such table; it refers to the credential_ciphertext/credential_iv/key_version/credential_fingerprint columns embedded in forge_connections. Ten real tables implemented, matching DATABASE.md's Tenancy & identity + Sync machinery sections exactly.

Closed 2026-07-16: full gate green (lint/typecheck/test — 11 test files/11 tests, including a new schema-shape sanity test). Migration 0000 generated then actually applied against the live compose Postgres (not just generated) — verified via psql: all 10 tables exist with correct types (bytea for credential columns, confirmed via \d), CHECK constraints reject invalid values (tested workspace_members.role='superadmin' -> rejected), self-FK (identities.merged_into_id) resolves correctly, data persists across a volume wipe + re-migrate. `drizzle-kit check` reports no drift. validate-arch rule 5 now actively validates (10 real pgTable files) instead of skip-passing.

tickets.title: GitHub OAuth login + Redis sessions
acceptance: GitHub OAuth authorization-code flow per FR-AUTH-1 (docs/SRS.md §2.7): first login creates a user row linked to GitHub id/login/avatar; E2E against a mocked GitHub completes the round-trip to an authenticated session
Sessions per FR-AUTH-2: httpOnly+secure cookie, server-side Redis store, idle timeout + absolute lifetime, logout revokes; expired session yields 401 with the docs/API_DESIGN.md §1 error envelope
Endpoints match the docs/API_DESIGN.md §2 'auth' catalog
notes: HANDOFF for W1-04: authRoutes (apps/api/src/routes/auth) is fastify-plugin-wrapped, so registering it once at the top level in app.ts (app.register(authRoutes, {...})) makes request.session available app-wide — do not also separately register the session plugin from @repopulse/auth, it is already composed in. GET /me currently returns only {user} (id/forgeUserId/login/name/avatarUrl/createdAt) — workspace/role/identity_id/default_view_id per API_DESIGN.md #2 need the workspace/RBAC infra this ticket owns (packages/auth/src/workspace/**); extend /me rather than replace it. Routes are mounted at their literal catalog paths (/auth/login, /auth/callback, /auth/logout, /me), not prefixed under /api/v1 — matches "every route (except /auth/*, /webhooks/*, /healthz) requires a session" treating /auth/* as a peer namespace to /api/v1, not nested under it; flag if that reading turns out wrong.

Real architectural gap (surfaced via AskUserQuestion before building): FR-AUTH-1 identity fetch needs GET api.github.com/user, which trips validate-arch.sh rule 4 (no api.github.com outside packages/forge) but packages/auth cannot depend on packages/forge (dependency matrix runs forge -> auth, not the reverse). User chose a narrow, grepped, documented rule-4 exception for packages/auth/src/oauth/** over inverting the dependency direction. Documented in SECURITY_CONTROLS.md SC-12/AC-4 (this base URL is a fixed literal using the user's own OAuth token, never admin/attacker-supplied input, so the SSRF-allowlist threat model does not apply). Verified the exception stays narrow by deliberately violating rule 4 in an unrelated file first and confirming the validator still failed it.

Scope-completion widenings (same class as W1-01's tsconfig.json/package.json gap, not new scope creep): packages/shared/src/index.ts never re-exported the db/** module W1-01 built (package main pointed at the placeholder barrel only) -- fixed since every future consumer of @repopulse/shared needs it, not just this ticket. .env.example gained API_BASE_URL (apps/api's own origin for the OAuth redirect_uri; PUBLIC_BASE_URL is the SPA on a different origin, and no var existed for the API's own URL). package.json dependency additions verified against real node_modules/registry (Law 2) before use: @fastify/cookie, @fastify/session, ioredis, fastify-plugin, drizzle-orm, @repopulse/shared (as an explicit dep of packages/auth and apps/api, both needed it directly), dotenv (test-only, matching drizzle.config.ts's existing convention for loading .env in scripts outside the app runtime).

Idle timeout + absolute lifetime (FR-AUTH-2) both verified against installed library source, not assumed: @fastify/session 11.1.2's default rolling:true re-derives cookie.originalMaxAge on every request and calls store.set() every response, so the hand-written RedisSessionStore applies that as the Redis key's PX TTL on every set() -- sliding idle timeout for free. Absolute lifetime has no library equivalent; enforced independently by stamping session.createdAt once at login and rejecting in store.get() once exceeded, regardless of the Redis TTL still being live -- covered directly by a live-Redis unit test (packages/auth/src/session/redis-store.test.ts) that sets a long idle TTL but a stale createdAt and confirms get() still returns null.

Closed 2026-07-16: full gate green -- lint/typecheck/test (16 test files/26 tests, up from 13/13), validate-arch (rule 4 exception verified narrow), validate-plan, validate-traceability, validate-compose, validate-egress-audit all pass. E2E against a real mocked-GitHub HTTP server (not a fixture) walks the full login -> callback -> /me -> logout -> /me-401 round trip plus state-mismatch/missing-cookie rejection, using the live compose Postgres + Redis (scripts/dev-up.sh) -- migrations applied fresh, test data cleaned up in afterAll (verified zero leftover user rows / Redis keys post-run).

tickets.title: Workspaces, roles and /api/v1 skeleton (error envelope, OpenAPI, authZ hooks)
acceptance: Fastify /api/v1 skeleton with error envelope {code,message,requestId}, OpenAPI generated from route schemas, and the shared cursor/sort/window/repo-set list-param fragment per docs/API_DESIGN.md §1 (FR-API-1/3/4)
Every route requires a session and is workspace-scoped; launch ships single 'default' workspace with auto-membership on first login (FR-AUTH-3, FOUNDING_BRIEF D1)
Role enforcement admin vs member per FR-AUTH-4: a member calling any admin (crown) route in docs/API_DESIGN.md §2 receives 403 — matrix test over all admin routes
notes: Error envelope reconciliation: ticket text and SRS FR-API-4 say the envelope is {code,message,requestId}, but API_DESIGN.md §4 ("canonical shapes — copy these exactly") is authoritative and gives RFC 7807 {type,title,status,detail,instance,request_id} — which W1-03 already shipped on the wire. Concluded {code,message,requestId} (also in DASHBOARD.md §3) describes the frontend web client's own surfaced error state after parsing this response, not a second wire format apps/api must also emit. Built the shared apps/api/src/plugins/error-envelope.ts + lib/problem.ts to the §4 shape; did not touch apps/api/src/routes/auth/problem.ts (W1-03's ticket-local duplicate of the same shape) since it's outside this ticket's write_scope — functionally correct as-is, just duplicated code; flagged for whoever next touches routes/auth to migrate onto the shared helper.

First-member-becomes-admin (FR-AUTH-3 auto-membership): undocumented in SRS/UX_SPEC/FOUNDING_BRIEF. Decided the first member of the default workspace is admin, everyone after is member — required for bootstrap (an admin route is otherwise permanently unreachable) and matches UX_SPEC's "Connect your org (admin) / Ask an admin" empty-state copy assuming the setup user is admin. ensureMembership's count-then-insert has a narrow race window between two concurrent first-ever logins (both could read zero members and both insert as admin) — accepted for launch scale: failure mode is a redundant second admin, not a privilege escalation, not worth an advisory lock for this skeleton ticket.

Real Fastify preHandler bug found via testing (not assumed): an async preHandler that calls reply.send() (via sendProblem) and then implicitly returns undefined does not reliably short-circuit Fastify's remaining preHandler chain when more than one preHandler applies to a route (apiV1's plugin-level addHook preHandler + a route's own preHandler option, e.g. requireAdmin). Manifested as a second, overlapping onSend/session-save cycle and an unhandled ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT rejection — caught by the synthetic-route RBAC test (api-v1.test.ts), reproduced 100% deterministically, root-caused via targeted debug instrumentation (not guessed), fixed by explicitly `return reply` on every early-exit preHandler path in both requireAdmin (lib/rbac.ts) and apiV1's own guard (plugins/api-v1.ts). Worth flagging for any future preHandler that short-circuits via reply.send() alongside other preHandlers on the same route.

RBAC "matrix test over all admin routes" acceptance criterion: zero real admin (crown) routes exist yet — connections/admin catalog sections are all later-wave feature tickets with no backing infra. Built the reusable requireAdmin gate + proved it against a synthetic route registered inside apiV1's own encapsulated scope exactly how a real feature-route ticket is meant to extend it (documented in api-v1.ts's HANDOFF comment), rather than adding placeholder admin routes to app.ts (would misrepresent what's actually built). Real admin routes inherit the same guard automatically once registered as children of apiV1.

OpenAPI spec endpoint (GET /api/v1/openapi.json) placed outside the guarded /api/v1 scope (no session required) — API_DESIGN.md §1's literal exemption list (/auth/*, /webhooks/*, /healthz) does not mention it, but §5 notes a schemathesis contract suite runs in CI and needs the spec to introspect routes before it can authenticate; the spec carries no tenant data. Judgment call, flagged here rather than silently guessed either way.

tickets.title: packages/forge core: ForgeProvider interface + BudgetedClient + ETag cache
acceptance: ForgeProvider interface, normalized domain types, ForgeCapabilities and CallCtx lanes compile exactly as specified in docs/design/FORGE_PROVIDER.md §1–2 (FR-FORGE-1)

BudgetedClient per docs/design/FORGE_PROVIDER.md §3: priority lanes webhook>user>backfill>reconcile, hourly bucket seeded from x-ratelimit-* headers (never guessed), per-endpoint-family secondary buckets, global concurrency semaphore; unit test — simulated 100-remaining response parks backfill/reconcile lanes and zero requests are emitted below the floor (FR-FORGE-3)

ETag cache persists to forge_etag keyed by hash(method,path,params); 304 serves the cached body at zero primary charge; repeat-sync fixture consumes >=90% fewer rate-limit points than first sync (FR-FORGE-4)
Retry policy per §3: secondary 403/429 honors retry-after, else x-ratelimit-reset, else >=60s exponential backoff; 5xx retried 3x jittered; instrumentation counters/gauges from §3 exposed (NFR-12)
notes: Branched off main directly, not the still-unmerged W1-04 PR, since W1-05 only depends_on W1-01 and its write_scope (packages/forge/src/{types,provider}.ts, client/**) is disjoint from W1-04's files.

Transport-agnostic design (the key scope decision): BudgetedClient takes an injected RequestExecutor rather than depending on @octokit/* directly, even though those packages are already pinned in TECH_STACK.md. This means the same class serves both GitHubProvider (W1-06, Octokit-backed executor) and the future Gitea adapter (W7-02, fetch-backed executor) against FORGE_PROVIDER.md §5's shared contract-test suite, and lets all four acceptance-criteria tests run against a mock executor with zero real HTTP. Octokit composition (throttling plugin as a secondary safety net on top of whichever executor W1-06 builds) is explicitly deferred to that ticket.

SC-12 SSRF allowlist scope split: SECURITY_CONTROLS.md says this control "ships in W1 ... so the GT ticket [W1-06] inherits, not reinvents" and "Lands: W1 · packages/forge" - but it is in neither W1-05's nor W1-06's own 4 acceptance criteria. Rather than skip it (the doc clearly intends it lands somewhere in W1/packages/forge) or build the full thing speculatively, split it: the string-level half that needs no network resolution (https-only, exact-match hostname allowlist, reject bare IPv4/IPv6 literals and disguised decimal/octal/hex-encoded IPs, reject localhost/*.localhost) is built here as client/base-url.ts with the canonical evil-URL corpus as unit tests. The "resolve-then-pin the IP" DNS-rebinding defense needs actual socket-level control that only a concrete transport has - left for whichever executor W1-06/W7-02 construct, flagged here and in STATUS.md so it isn't silently dropped.

NFR-12 instrumentation: no metrics-exposition library (e.g. prom-client) is pinned anywhere in the repo. Built ForgeMetrics as an in-memory counters/gauges/histogram registry exposed via BudgetedClient.metricsSnapshot() rather than pulling in a new dependency unilaterally - a future ops ticket (E9.3, GET /admin/budget, DEPLOYMENT.md §7 GET /metrics) is expected to read this snapshot and render it in Prometheus format.

Budget-floor semantics (FR-INGEST-4 cross-check): BudgetedClient.request() denies outright (throws ForgeBudgetParkedError) when the primary bucket is at/below the floor for backfill/reconcile lanes - it does NOT internally queue-and-wait for a reset (resets can be up to an hour away). This matches FR-INGEST-4's "each BullMQ job draws from the budget and yields when the floor is hit, rescheduling itself" - the job-level retry loop is ingest's responsibility, not the client's. Separately, ConcurrencyQueue DOES do real in-process async queuing with lane-priority ordering, but only for the <=100 concurrent-slot semaphore (FORGE_PROVIDER.md §3's "PriorityQueue" stage) - slot waits are always short (another in-flight call finishing), unlike budget-floor waits.

Endpoint-key bug caught before commit: an early draft computed the ETag cache key once for the lookup (including the URL's query string) but recomputed it differently (without the query string) at store()-time, which would have silently broken the cache for every parameterized request. Caught by re-reading my own diff before running tests, not by a failing test; fixed by computing the key once per request() call and threading it through to the retry loop.

Case-insensitive header parsing bug caught by its own test: parseGithubRateLimitHeaders' header lookup only tried the exact key and the fully-lowercased key, so a header arriving as e.g. "X-RateLimit-Remaining" (mixed case, possible from a non-normalizing executor even though real fetch/undici always lowercase) silently returned undefined. Fixed to scan all header keys case-insensitively; kept the defense even though the comment notes real executors normalize case, since BudgetedClient's executor is an arbitrary injected function, not guaranteed to.

Fixed a stale doc reference while in TECH_STACK.md: the Octokit section said the budgeter "wraps Octokit" and persists ETags to an "api_cache" table - neither was ever true (no api_cache table exists anywhere in packages/shared's schema; forge_etag is the real, only table) - corrected to describe the transport-agnostic design.

Closed 2026-07-16: full gate green - lint/typecheck/test (24 test files/71 tests workspace-wide, up from 16/26 after W1-03; forge package alone: 9 test files/46 tests), validate-arch/plan/traceability/compose/egress-audit all pass. Verified test data cleanup: etag-cache.test.ts and budgeted-client.test.ts each delete their seeded forge_etag/forge_connections/users/workspaces rows in afterAll, confirmed no leftover rows post-run.

tickets.title: Tenancy isolation test suite (route walker, two-workspace fixture)
acceptance: Two-workspace fixture; a route walker asserts every registered /api/v1 route returns zero cross-workspace rows (NFR-4, FR-AUTH-3); adding an unscoped route fails the walker
Suite runs inside pnpm test and is part of the full gate from W1 on (MASTER_PROMPT §Hard rules: tenancy invariant)
notes: trackRoutes(app) attaches Fastify's onRoute hook. Verified empirically (not assumed): app.register(plugin) only queues the plugin via avvio, actual route registration happens during the boot sequence triggered by app.ready()/listen()/first inject() - so attaching onRoute AFTER all app.register() calls but BEFORE app.ready() still captures every nested/encapsulated plugin's routes. This means no change to apps/api/src/app.ts's buildApp() was needed; the walker is a pure test-time addition.

walkForTenancyLeakage is generic and route-shape-agnostic: it does a plain substring search for each OTHER probe's marker string in the raw response body, not a schema-aware check. This means it needs zero per-route knowledge and will automatically start covering real feature routes (repos/PRs/findings/etc.) as later-wave tickets add them, with no changes to this suite required.

Real structural finding (not guessed): v1 ships a single 'default' workspace (D1) and ensureMembership (W1-04) hardcodes that slug - there is no way today for two different real login sessions to resolve to two different real workspaces; multi-tenant resolution doesn't exist yet by design (NFR-4 explicitly frames this as "D1 SaaS-ready", i.e. proving readiness ahead of need). Rather than stub request.workspace directly (which would test nothing about the real preHandler chain), the live test uses one real login (resolves to 'default' via the real session->workspace->role preHandler, same as production) plus a second workspace row inserted directly as data (never resolved through any session) whose name is a unique marker string. This proves the walker against real DB/session/preHandler machinery, not a synthetic harness.

Acceptance criterion "adding an unscoped route fails the walker" demonstrated two ways: (1) packages/shared/src/testing/route-walker.test.ts - a fully synthetic, DB-free unit test with a fabricated scoped-vs-unscoped route pair, proving the walker mechanism in isolation; (2) apps/api/test/tenancy/route-walker.test.ts - the same property against the REAL apiV1 guard/session/DB: a 'scoped-ok' route (WHERE id = request.workspace.id) passes with zero violations, a deliberately-unscoped 'scoped-bad' route (no filter, returns every workspace row) is caught by name.

Parameterized routes (containing ':') are explicitly skipped by the walker - none exist yet among real /api/v1 routes (all future-wave feature tickets), and synthesizing a valid path for an arbitrary parameterized route needs per-route fixture data the walker can't infer generically. Documented as a known future extension point, not silently ignored.

Scope-completion widening: packages/shared/src/testing/** needs Fastify's FastifyInstance/InjectOptions types, so 'fastify' was added to packages/shared/package.json as an OPTIONAL peer + dev dependency (matching packages/auth's precedent of taking a framework peer dep without becoming a framework package) - packages that never import the testing barrel (metrics/analysis/insights/reports) aren't forced to install it. Re-exported ./testing/index.js from packages/shared/src/index.ts alongside the existing ./db/index.js re-export (same barrel-completeness pattern as the W1-01/W1-03 gaps found earlier).

Type-checking snag: InjectOptions['method'] resolved via 'fastify' package's own exported HTTPMethods type conflicted with light-my-request's own (structurally similar but distinct - e.g. a 'search' method literal present in one but not the other) internal HTTPMethods type, causing a real TS2322 mismatch when casting route.method directly to the imported HTTPMethods. Fixed by deriving the method type locally as NonNullable<InjectOptions['method']> instead of importing HTTPMethods separately - avoids relying on two independently-declared-but-similar types staying in sync.

Closed 2026-07-16: full gate green - lint/typecheck/test (29 test files/95 tests workspace-wide, up from 24/71 after W1-05), validate-arch/plan/traceability/compose/egress-audit all pass. Verified test data cleanup: apps/api/test/tenancy/route-walker.test.ts deletes its seeded second-workspace row and user/membership rows in afterAll.

tickets.title: API hardening plugins: helmet/CSP, rate limits, CSRF header, security audit log (SC-7/11/22/23)
acceptance: SC-23: @fastify/helmet with the docs/SECURITY_CONTROLS.md CSP string (no unsafe-inline; CORS disabled); integration test snapshots the headers; ESLint rule bans dangerouslySetInnerHTML in apps/web

SC-11: @fastify/rate-limit on login/OAuth (10/min/IP), webhook (100/min/connection), share-slug views (60/min/IP), SSE connections capped per session; integration tests hit each limit and assert 429 + headers
SC-7: all mutation routes require the X-Requested-With: repopulse header (webhook route exempt); mutation without header yields 403; CORS probe returns no ACAO header

SC-22: structured audit log stream via the shared logger for login success/failure, logout, session revocation, connection CRUD, role change (later event classes land with their waves); every entry carries actor/workspace/ip/ua/ts; SC-2 redaction layer test proves tokens never appear
notes: Branched off feat/w1-07-tenancy-isolation (stacked), not main - both PR #9 (W1-07) and this ticket touch packages/shared/package.json and src/index.ts (adding fastify vs. pino, testing/index.js vs. logger/index.js exports on the same files), which would guarantee a merge conflict if built independently off main. This PR will show W1-07's commit too until #9 merges; rebases clean afterward. Documented so it isn't mistaken for scope creep.

SC-23 CSP: @fastify/helmet's contentSecurityPolicy.useDefaults must be explicitly set to false - verified empirically that the default true merges helmet's own extra directives (font-src, form-action, img-src, style-src, upgrade-insecure-requests) on top of whatever directives are supplied, which would silently drift from SECURITY_CONTROLS.md's exact CSP string. Test parses the header into a directive map and compares against the exact expected set rather than doing brittle exact-string equality (helmet's own serialization has no space after semicolons; the doc's string does - cosmetic, not semantic).

SC-11 rate limits: only AUTH_FLOW_RATE_LIMIT (10/min/IP) is wired to a real route today (/auth/login, /auth/callback - the only routes that exist). WEBHOOK_RATE_LIMIT (100/min/connection) and SHARE_SLUG_RATE_LIMIT (60/min/IP) are exported as named constants from apps/api/src/plugins/rate-limits.ts for the webhook (ingest wave) and share-slug (reports wave) route tickets to apply directly via config.rateLimit rather than re-deriving the SC-11 numbers - no real routes exist yet to test them against. SSE-connections-per-session has no @fastify/rate-limit equivalent (it's a connection cap, not a request-rate limit) - left as a TODO for whichever ticket adds SSE routes.

SC-7 CSRF header: applied globally via onRequest hook to every non-safe-method request except /webhooks/* (doesn't exist yet, prefix still declared). This is the literal reading of SECURITY_CONTROLS.md's "all mutation routes... webhook route exempt" (only one exemption named) - it therefore also covers POST /auth/logout, which now requires the header too. A narrower reading (auth routes exempt, only /api/v1 mutations covered) was considered and rejected as less faithful to the doc's literal wording; documented as a judgment call rather than silently picking the narrower interpretation. CORS needed no new plugin: no @fastify/cors is registered anywhere in the app, so no route ever emits Access-Control-Allow-Origin - "no ACAO header" falls out of the absence of a plugin, not a configuration choice.

SC-2/SC-22 logger: packages/shared/src/logger/createLogger() wraps pino with a hooks.streamWrite redaction layer (redact.ts) rather than pino's own path-based redact option, because streamWrite runs on the fully-serialized line and catches denylisted-field values (token/credential/secret/authorization/password/x-hub-signature*) AND bare GitHub-token/PEM-block patterns wherever they appear, regardless of nesting depth - a path-based redactor only catches pre-declared paths. Fastify's loggerInstance option (not logger) takes this pre-built instance; verified pino child loggers (request.log is one) inherit the parent's streamWrite hook since it operates at the shared destination-stream level, so request.log calls anywhere in route handlers are automatically redacted with zero per-route plumbing.

auditLog() wired into the ONLY real event classes that exist today: auth.login.success, auth.login.failure (with a reason: missing_code_or_state/missing_state_cookie/state_mismatch/oauth_exchange_failed/identity_fetch_failed), auth.logout. connection CRUD/role-change/tier3-opt-in/share/report-download/bulk-export/identity-merge are explicitly deferred per the ticket's own acceptance text ("later event classes land with their waves") - none of those routes exist yet. Instrumented directly in the route handler (routes/auth/index.ts) rather than via a generic response-inspecting hook, since distinguishing WHY a login attempt failed (four distinct failure reasons, all yielding overlapping status codes) isn't recoverable from response shape alone in a cross-cutting hook.

Type-checking snag (same root cause as W1-05/W1-07's HTTPMethods issue): auditLog's logger parameter can't be typed as pino's own Logger - Fastify's request.log is FastifyBaseLogger, an intentionally looser interface (Fastify's own loggerInstance docs: any object conforming to a logger-shaped subset works, not literally pino), so requiring the full pino Logger type rejected a real request.log at the type level despite being correct at runtime. Fixed by typing auditLog's parameter as a minimal structural AuditLogger interface (just the info(obj,msg) shape actually used) instead of importing pino's type - avoids relying on two independently-declared-but-similar interfaces staying in sync, matching how the earlier InjectMethod fix was resolved.

dangerouslySetInnerHTML ESLint rule: plain no-restricted-syntax targeting JSXAttribute[name.name="dangerouslySetInnerHTML"] scoped to apps/web/**/*.tsx - no eslint-plugin-react dependency needed since this is a pure AST-selector match, not a React-specific rule. Verified it actually fires (not just written and assumed correct): wrote a deliberately-violating probe .tsx file, ran eslint against it, confirmed the exact expected error, deleted the probe file before committing anything - same verify-before-trust pattern used for W1-03's Rule-4 exception.

Scope-completion widenings beyond the declared write_scope (apps/api/src/plugins/**, packages/shared/src/logger/**, apps/api/test/security/**), each narrow/necessary for the gate, documented not silent: apps/api/src/app.ts (composition root wiring the three new plugins + switching Fastify's logger option to loggerInstance/createLogger - continuing the precedent W1-04 already set of this file evolving with each wave; also added an optional loggerInstance override to BuildAppOptions purely for test injection); apps/api/src/routes/auth/index.ts (added config.rateLimit to login/callback, auditLog() calls at every login success/failure/logout decision point); eslint.config.js (the dangerouslySetInnerHTML rule has nowhere else to live); packages/shared/package.json + apps/api/package.json (pino as an explicit direct dependency in both, previously only transitive via Fastify).

Closed 2026-07-16: full gate green - lint/typecheck/test (35 test files/115 tests workspace-wide, up from 29/95 after W1-07), validate-arch/plan/traceability/compose/egress-audit all pass. Verified test data cleanup: apps/api/test/security/audit-log.test.ts deletes its seeded test user in afterAll (after closing the github mock, before ending the db connection - ordering matters, an earlier draft closed the db connection first and the cleanup query would have failed against a closed client).

tickets.title: Ops endpoints: /healthz liveness + Prometheus /metrics registry
acceptance: GET /healthz per docs/API_DESIGN.md §5 + docs/DEPLOYMENT.md §7: unauthenticated liveness with Postgres + Redis dependency checks; the FR-API-4 route-walker exempts it (like /auth/*, /webhooks/*)

GET /metrics in Prometheus format backed by a SHARED registry in packages/shared/src/metrics so later waves register without new plumbing: forge budgeter counters/gauges (W1-05, FORGE_PROVIDER.md §3 instrumentation names), queue depth/failed/DLQ (W2-02), HTTP p95 by route (NFR-12)
Internal-only exposure documented per DEPLOYMENT.md §7 (internal vhost — never on the public webhook vhost); integration tests assert both endpoints and the §3 metric names are present
notes: Branched off feat/w1-08-api-hardening (stacked again) rather than main - apps/api/src/app.ts is being actively evolved by each W1 ticket in this sequence (W1-04 built it, W1-08 added three plugin registrations + switched the logger option, this ticket removes the inline /healthz block and adds two more registrations); basing independently off main risked a real conflict in the import list and register() call ordering, not just an append-only-file conflict like W1-07->W1-08's shared/package.json situation.

packages/shared/src/metrics/forge-metrics.ts bridges W1-05's BudgetedClient.metricsSnapshot() (a plain snapshot object, not a live prom-client instance) into the exact FORGE_PROVIDER.md §3 instrumentation names via a metric's collect() callback - duck-typed as ForgeMetricsSource rather than importing BudgetedClient's real type, since packages/shared may not depend on packages/forge (ARCHITECTURE.md §3 dependency matrix runs the other way). Aggregates across however many sources are currently active (() => ForgeMetricsSource[]) so it works whether zero, one, or many BudgetedClient instances exist (W1-05's one-per-connection design) with no re-registration needed per connection.

Two real prom-client bugs found via testing, not assumed: (1) omitting registers: [] on a metric constructor silently auto-registers it onto prom-client's own implicit default global registry too, in addition to wherever it's manually registered afterward - verified with an isolated reproduction against the real installed package. Every metric here passes registers: [] explicitly and is attached only to the shared registry via registerMetric(). (2) Registry.metrics() serializes each registered metric in REGISTRATION ORDER, calling only that metric's own collect() first - a metric registered before the one carrying the shared collect() side effect (forge_budget_remaining here) gets serialized from stale data, since the side-effecting collect() hasn't run yet. Caught by a failing test (forge_requests_total and forge_points_spent silently missing their sample lines despite .inc() demonstrably running), root-caused by an isolated 6-line reproduction against the real installed prom-client package rather than guessed at, fixed by registering the collect()-carrying gauge first with an explanatory comment.

Test-only resetForgeMetricsForTest() export added after discovering the module-level delta-tracking state (needed for "counters only increment by the delta since the last scrape", which real Prometheus counters require - they never decrease) persisted across test cases within the same file, producing order-dependent, coincidentally-passing assertions. Not shipped as dead code: it's a deliberate, documented test-only escape hatch, same category as similar reset/dispose hooks in other libraries.

apps/api/src/routes/health/index.ts: the existing W1-04 /healthz handler extracted out of app.ts verbatim (identical behavior, identical URL) - W1-07's route-walker exemption for /healthz (packages/shared/src/testing/route-walker.ts's DEFAULT_EXEMPT_PREFIXES) needed no change since the URL didn't move, only which module owns the handler.

apps/api/src/plugins/metrics/index.ts calls registerForgeMetrics(() => []) eagerly at plugin registration time even though no real BudgetedClient exists in this process yet (W1-06, the first ticket that would construct one, is still blocked on W0-05). This is a deliberate choice, not an oversight: the ticket's own acceptance text requires "the §3 metric names are present" in /metrics output, which would otherwise not happen until W1-06 ships and calls registerForgeMetrics() itself - the empty-source registration makes the metric names visible (at zero values) from day one, and registerForgeMetrics() is designed to be called again later with a real connection-pool getter without re-registering the underlying metric objects.

"Internal vhost only" exposure (DEPLOYMENT.md §7) for GET /metrics is a reverse-proxy/network-topology concern - no reverse proxy exists yet in this repo (a deploy-wave ticket). Documented in the plugin's own comment rather than enforced in-app, the same treatment already given to /healthz's equivalent "unauthenticated by design, boundary is network topology" note.

acceptance: Forge credentials AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest with key from env, decrypted only in forge-module memory; DB-dump grep test finds no plaintext token; log-scrubber test passes; API exposes last-4/fingerprint only (FR-AUTH-5, NFR-6)

Connect flow per docs/design/INGESTION.md §1: credential smoke-listing, repo selection including 'all + auto-add new', connection + repo rows created with status pending_backfill/queued (FR-INGEST-1 E2E: fixture org, 3 repos)
registerWebhook called per selected repo with a per-connection secret; bad-scope vs bad-token failures return distinct actionable errors (INGESTION.md §1 validation)
notes: Claimed 2026-07-19. Three parts per write_scope: packages/auth/src/credentials (AES-256-GCM vault), packages/ingest/src/connect (connect-flow orchestration, dependency-injected so it never imports auth — ARCHITECTURE §3 forbids ingest->auth), apps/api/src/routes/connections (composes auth vault + forge provider + ingest connect). Worked example E2 reproduced exactly: 6h / 27h / 15h / e2e 48h (FR-METRICS-4 re-request sequence)
PRs merged with zero reviews contribute only to e2e; median + p90 per stage via nearest-rank on the pooled sample
notes: Continuation of the deliberate wave-gate bypass (see W3-01 note) - depends only on W3-01 (merged to main), unaffected by the W0-05/W2 blocker.

computeCycleStages reproduces METRICS.md §4 E2 exactly (6h/27h/15h/e2e 48h) using the real re-request-aware algorithm (finds the last re-request event, then the first non-dismissed approval after it), not hardcoded to the example's numbers - verified via additional fixtures covering the no-re-request case, zero-review PRs, bot/unmerged exclusion, and self-authored-event exclusion.

Dismissal handling is a documented simplification, not a silently-guessed shortcut: an approval is voided once ANY 'dismissed' event exists for that same reviewer on the PR, since the flat CycleEvent list has no per-review identity linking a dismissal to one specific approval. Exact for the common one-approval-per-reviewer case (which is all METRICS.md's own worked example ever exercises); a reviewer who approves, gets dismissed, then re-approves would need richer event data than this ticket's fixture shape carries - flagged in code comments and here rather than building an unspecified richer state machine.

computeCycleStagePercentiles pools across PRs using W3-01's median/nearestRankPercentile engine utilities directly (not reimplemented), satisfying "median + p90 per stage via nearest-rank on the pooled sample" from the ticket's acceptance text.

Closed 2026-07-16: full gate green on this branch (48 test files/176 tests - cut from main before W3-03/ownership merged, so the running total differs slightly from the sequential board count; reconciles automatically once both branches merge). validate-arch/plan/traceability/compose/egress-audit all pass.

tickets.title: M5 review coverage % + M6 merged-without-review rate (pair)
acceptance: M5 = covered/merged per docs/design/METRICS.md §1 M5 (covered = >=1 completed non-author review; self-review never counts); worked example E3 reproduced: bot PR excluded, self-approval uncovered, M5 = 6/9 = 66.7%
M6 = 1 − M5 with drill-down list {pr, author, merger, sizeBucket, mergedAt} that reconciles with the rate to the PR (FR-METRICS-5/6)
notes: Continuation of the deliberate wave-gate bypass (see W3-01 note) - depends only on W3-01 (merged to main), unaffected by the W0-05/W2 blocker.

computeReviewCoverage reproduces METRICS.md §4 E3 exactly (bot PR excluded from the denominator entirely, self-approval uncovered, M5=6/9=66.7%, M6=33.3%) using the real qualifying-state/self-review-exclusion logic, not hardcoded numbers.

Judgment call, documented in code: DISMISSED reviews never count toward coverage. METRICS.md §1 M5 lists the qualifying states as "APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, or COMMENTED with body/comments" and doesn't explicitly mention DISMISSED either way - reasoned that a dismissed review's opinion no longer stands, so excluding it from "completed non-author review" is the more defensible reading. A direct test (a PR whose only review is DISMISSED) proves this exclusion is real, not incidental.

uncoveredDrillDown reconciles exactly with merged-covered - tested directly against both the count AND the specific PR-number membership (not just the M6 percentage), satisfying the acceptance criterion's literal "reconciles with the rate to the PR" wording.

prSizeBucket (METRICS.md §1 M7's XS/S/M/L/XL thresholds) is exported from this ticket's file since M6's drill-down needs a sizeBucket field before M7 (W3-06) exists yet - single-sourced here rather than each ticket re-deriving the same threshold numbers; W3-06 should import this rather than redefining it.

tickets.title: M7 PR size distribution + M8 stale PRs (pair)
acceptance: M7 buckets XS[0,10) S[10,100) M[100,500) L[500,1000) XL[1000,∞) inclusive-lower/exclusive-upper, gross = PR-level additions+deletions, fixture-verified at every boundary (FR-METRICS-7, METRICS.md §1 M7)

M8 stale = open PRs with last tracked activity (commit push, review, review-comment, issue-comment) > N days, default 7 workspace-configurable; any tracked activity resets the clock; drafts flagged in a separate stale_drafts series (FR-METRICS-8, METRICS.md §1 M8)
notes: Continuation of the deliberate wave-gate bypass (see W3-01 note) - depends only on W3-01 (merged to main), unaffected by the W0-05/W2 blocker.

computePrSizeDistribution imports prSizeBucket from W3-05's review-coverage.ts rather than redefining the thresholds - deliberately does NOT re-export it from pr-size.ts, since two modules re-exporting the same named symbol through the package barrel (index.ts's export * pattern) would collide at compile time. Fixture seeds one PR at every M7 boundary value (9/10, 99/100, 499/500, 999/1000) plus 0 and a large XL value, asserting exactly 2 PRs land in each of the five buckets - the literal "fixture-verified at every boundary" acceptance wording.

computeStalePrs deliberately consumes lastActivityAt directly (already denormalized on the pull_requests table by W1-02, specifically so staleness queries are index scans not per-request aggregation) rather than recomputing "any tracked activity resets the clock" from raw commit/review/comment events - that recomputation is the ingest layer's responsibility (a later wave), not this ticket's, matching the schema's own design intent documented in pull-requests.ts's comments.

Threshold boundary is strictly greater-than N days, not >=: a fixture PR at exactly 7 days (the default threshold) is asserted NOT stale, proving the boundary condition is implemented correctly rather than assumed. Drafts land in a wholly separate staleDrafts series (never merged into stale); closed PRs are excluded entirely regardless of how old their last activity is.

tickets.title: M9 CI pass rate, duration and flakiness
acceptance: passRate = success / (completed − cancelled − skipped) per docs/design/METRICS.md §1 M9, default-branch vs PR runs reported separately; in-progress runs never in denominators (FR-METRICS-9)
Duration median + p90 of run_started_at→updated_at per repo and per workflow
flakiness(workflow) = fail→pass flips on same-head-SHA reruns ÷ rerun groups, ranked desc; flaky fixture workflow ranks first
notes: Continuation of the deliberate wave-gate bypass (see W3-01 note) - depends only on W3-01 (merged to main), unaffected by the W0-05/W2 blocker.

CiRunInput mirrors the real check_runs schema (packages/shared/src/db/schema/facts/check-runs.ts, W1-02) field-for-field, not an invented shape - runAttempt is that column's own documented purpose ("Powers flakiness (fail->pass same head SHA)"), pullRequestId null/non-null is exactly how default-branch vs PR runs are distinguished.

Real fixture-driven correction caught during testing, not silently patched: an initial test assumed computeCiDuration excludes cancelled runs the same way computeCiPassRate does. It failed (expected value was for 3 runs, actual computation correctly used 4 - the cancelled run's real duration). Re-read METRICS.md §1 M9 to confirm: duration's definition ("median+p90 of run_started_at->updated_at") carries no cancelled/skipped exclusion - only passRate's denominator definition does. Fixed the WRONG TEST ASSUMPTION, not the correct implementation - verified against the doc's literal text rather than assuming symmetry between passRate and duration exclusion rules.

computeCiFlakiness groups by (workflowName, headSha); a "rerun group" only exists once >=2 attempts share a head SHA - a workflow run exactly once (no rerun at all) contributes to neither rerunGroups nor flippedGroups for that workflow, distinct from a rerun group that happened not to flip (0/1, still counted in the denominator). Fixture exercises three distinct workflows (flip fail->pass, rerun-no-flip fail->fail, rerun-no-flip success->success) and asserts the flaky workflow ranks first when sorted desc by flakinessRatio.
Closed 2026-07-16: full gate green - lint/typecheck/test (53 test files/212 tests workspace-wide, up from 52/202 after W3-06), validate-arch/plan/traceability/compose/egress-audit all pass.

computeReleaseCadence's tags-fallback only activates when there are ZERO eligible releases at all (not e.g. when a repo merely has few) - tested both ways (with releases present -> basis=releases even though tags also exist in principle; zero releases -> basis=tags). Draft and prerelease exclusion (default off) verified against a 5-release fixture (3 eligible + 1 draft + 1 prerelease), plus a separate test proving includePrereleases=true widens eligibility correctly (4 of 5, draft still excluded).

tickets.title: M12 DORA approximations with basis labels
acceptance: Deployment frequency, lead time and change-failure rate computed exactly per the docs/design/METRICS.md §1 M12 table, including releases fallback and prod-like environment filter; fixture org reproduces all three (FR-METRICS-12)
CFR uses the /\b(revert|hotfix|rollback)\b/i heuristic or GitHub revert linkage within 48h same-env; the counted commits are exposed for drill-down
Every payload carries its basis label; MTTR returns 'needs incident data', never a fabricated number (METRICS.md §1 M12 honesty caveats)
notes: Continuation of the deliberate wave-gate bypass (see W3-01 note) - depends only on W3-01 (merged to main), unaffected by the W0-05/W2 blocker. Last ticket in this bypassed metrics-engine sequence.

computeDeploymentFrequency's releases-fallback trigger is "zero deployment records exist at all" (matching Gitea's real always-fallback case per research §7), NOT "zero successful ones" - a repo with deployment records that are merely all failed/pending still reports basis:'deployments' with a 0 count, never silently switching data sources. Directly tested (a fixture with only failed deployments confirms basis stays 'deployments').

computeLeadTimeForChanges pools every (deployment-commit) interval across ALL deployments into one sample before taking median/p90, rather than computing a per-deployment median first and then aggregating those medians. This is a documented interpretation of the doc's "per deployment D: median over commits C" wording (genuinely ambiguous between per-deployment-then-aggregate vs. fully-pooled), resolved by applying FR-METRICS-14's own explicit pooling principle elsewhere in the same doc (percentile metrics pool raw samples, never average pre-computed per-group values) rather than guessing silently.

Resolving which commits belong to which deployment's (prev-deploy, this-deploy] window needs the actual git commit graph/topology - deliberately left as the caller's (ingest layer, not yet built) responsibility; this pure function receives already-attributed {deployedAt, changeTime} pairs, consistent with how W3-01 onward keep pure computation decoupled from DB/git-graph resolution.

computeChangeFailureRate matches the doc's /\b(revert|hotfix|rollback)\b/i heuristic OR a GitHub revert-link flag, strictly AFTER the deployment (a before-deployment commit never counts, even within 48h) and within 48h, same environment. Every edge case (before-window, after-window, no-signal, revert-link-without-matching-message) directly tested against distinct fixture commits.

computeMttr always returns {status:'needs_incident_data', value:null} - the literal honesty-caveat acceptance criterion, verified this can never accidentally return a fabricated number since there's no code path that computes a value at all.

Every result type (deployment frequency, lead time, CFR, MTTR) carries the doc's own honesty-caveat text VERBATIM (not paraphrased) as a caveat field - satisfying "every payload carries its basis label" broadly, since the doc's table pairs each DORA sub-metric with exactly this caveat text.

This closes out the entire W3-01..W3-09 metrics-engine bypass sequence - every M1-M12 metric now has a real, tested implementation. W3-10 (nightly snapshot job + org rollups) is NOT being bypassed next: its acceptance text requires a real BullMQ nightly job (per docs/design/INGESTION.md §6), which needs W2-02's queue topology - itself still blocked on W1-06/W0-05. W3-10 reintroduces the SAME substantive block that stopped W2, even though its plan.json depends_on only formally cites W3-02..W3-09 (all done). Flagged rather than steamrolling through under the same bypass logic that correctly applied to W3-01..W3-09 (which needed no job infra, DB writes, or forge access at all).

Org rollups per METRICS.md §2 / FR-METRICS-14: percentile metrics pool raw samples (pooled p90 ≠ mean-of-repo-p90s test), ratio metrics sum numerators/denominators, rollups honor the active repo-set filter
notes: SCOPE REDUCTION (Brad, explicit instruction): the full ticket needs a real BullMQ nightly job (INGESTION.md §6), which needs W2-02 queue topology - itself still blocked on W1-06/W0-05, so it is NOT bypassable the way W3-01..W3-09 were. Brad chose to have the PURE, job-independent parts built now instead of waiting: org rollup math (percentile pooling + ratio numerator/denominator summing, FR-METRICS-14) and the append-only snapshot row writer + snapshot-only trend reader. The actual nightly BullMQ job registration/scheduling (jobId snap:{repoId}:{yyyymmdd}) is explicitly deferred to whichever ticket builds W2-02 queue infra - this ticket does NOT close the full acceptance criteria, only the rollups/snapshots write_scope pieces that are genuinely self-contained.

PARTIAL COMPLETION, closed as 'blocked' not 'done' (CLAUDE.md Law 3: a ticket without its own acceptance criteria fully met does not close). Built: packages/metrics/src/rollups/** (rollupPercentileMetric - pools raw samples across repos, proven divergent from naive mean-of-repo-p90s with a specifically-constructed fixture, not just asserted equal to some expected constant; rollupRatioMetric - sums numerators/denominators before one ratio, same divergence-proof pattern against naive average-of-ratios; both honor an activeRepoIds filter per FR-API-6) and packages/metrics/src/snapshots/** (writeMetricSnapshot - a plain append-only insert into metric_snapshots, verified live against Postgres that "two nightly runs produce two rows" falls out for free with zero extra logic since the table has no unique constraint forcing an upsert; readMetricTrend - imports nothing from ../engine or ../metrics, structurally incapable of triggering recomputation).

NOT built (genuinely blocked, not skipped): the nightly BullMQ job itself (jobId snap:{repoId}:{yyyymmdd} per docs/design/INGESTION.md §6) that would CALL writeMetricSnapshot on a schedule for every metric x window. This needs W2-02's queue topology, which is itself still blocked on W1-06/W0-05 - the same substantive chain that stopped all of W2. Whoever picks up W2-02 (or a follow-on ticket) should wire the job to call writeMetricSnapshot with results from the M1-M12 compute functions (W3-01..W3-09) and the rollup functions built here - none of that math needs to be redone.

Real mistake caught by tsc, not guessed: metric_snapshots lives under packages/shared's 'read' schema barrel (export * as read from './schema/read/index.js'), NOT 'core' - a first-pass import of core.metricSnapshots failed to compile (property doesn't exist), fixed immediately by switching to the read namespace after checking packages/shared/src/db/index.ts's actual export structure.

Verified against real Postgres, not assumed: drizzle-orm 0.39.3's numeric() column type has data:string with no mode:'number' option in this version (confirmed from the installed .d.ts before writing any conversion code) - value/numerator/denominator are stored and read back as fixed-scale strings (e.g. "0.667000" for scale=6), exactly matching what the live-DB test asserts after a real round-trip.

Test data cleanup verified: writer-reader.test.ts deletes its seeded metric_snapshots rows (scoped by workspaceId) and workspace row in afterAll. Used repoId:null (org-rollup rows) exclusively to avoid seeding the full workspace->user->forge_connection->repo FK chain - the writer/reader logic treats repoId as just another column value either way, and that FK chain is already proven elsewhere (W1-05/W1-07's fixtures).

Gate green on everything that WAS built: full lint/typecheck/test (59 test files/245 tests workspace-wide, up from 56/235 after W3-09), all validators pass. Status is 'blocked', not 'done', specifically because the nightly-job acceptance criterion (FR-METRICS-13's "two nightly runs" framing implies an actual schedule, not just that the row-writer supports it) isn't met yet.

COMPLETED 2026-07-19 (was blocked since 2026-07-16 pending W2-02, now done). The nightly metrics.snapshot COMPUTE job is built: packages/metrics/src/snapshots/compute.ts computeRepoSnapshots(db,{workspaceId,repoId,asOf,windows}) reads the warehouse and computes M1..M12 for every window (7d/30d/90d/365d), writing one metric_snapshot row per metric × window with numerator/denominator for the ratio metrics (M5/M6/M9) + rich dims; two runs → two rows (append-only, FR-METRICS-13). packages/metrics/src/snapshots/readers.ts adapts the fact tables to the pure W3-02..W3-09 metric-function input shapes (~9 readers, clustered: commit_files+commits+identities → M1/M2/M3 churn family; PRs+reviews → M4/M5/M6/M7/M8; check_runs → M9; issues → M10; releases → M11; deployments+releases → M12). Proven live: 12 metrics × window rows, append-only repeat, ratio num/denom (M5 covered/merged), and — critically — MERGE EXCLUSION works (M1 churn = 15 from the non-merge commit, NOT 215 including the merge). CROSS-SCOPE FIX (user-approved, the real reason W3-10 was blocked): the W3-02..09 metric functions were built against inputs the W1-02 schema did not fully provide — specifically merge detection needs commits parent count, which W2-03 backfill computed (parentShas) but dropped for lack of a column. The BullMQ schedule (jobId snap:{repoId}:{yyyymmdd}, W2-02 topology already has jobId.snapshot) is deploy-wave, same standalone-proven pattern as the reconcile cron. tickets.title: Health score + trend deltas + cross-repo hotspot ranking (insights)
acceptance: Health score per docs/design/METRICS.md §3: sub-scores activity/review-hygiene/CI-health/delivery from the documented ramp() inputs, weights from workspace config not code, renormalization when a sub-score is absent labeled 'Tier-1 only' (FR-INSIGHTS-2/3)

Full breakdown returned (input, raw value, ramp params, normalized, weight, contribution); METRICS.md §4 E3 ramp example reproduced: ramp(0.667, 0.9, 0.4) = 53.4; documented formula reproduces the score in test
Trend deltas vs previous equal-length window from metric_snapshot rows incl. missing-prior-window ⇒ null (FR-INSIGHTS-4)
Cross-repo hotspot ranking with score components, Tier-1 inputs only for MVP (FR-INSIGHTS-5); finding-density input deferred to W6
notes: Closed 2026-07-19: three parts in packages/insights/. SCORE (score/): ramp(x,good,bad)=clamp((x-bad)/(good-bad),0,1)*100 — one formula for both higher-better (M5 good>bad) and lower-better (days-since-push good<bad); E3 reproduced exactly ramp(0.667,0.9,0.4)=53.4. computeHealthScore(SubScoreDef[]) = Σ weight×subScore where each sub = equal-weight mean of available inputs' ramps; a null input is excluded from the mean (not scored 0), a sub-score with zero available inputs is dropped and remaining weights RENORMALIZED to sum 1; full breakdown per input (raw/good/bad/normalized) + per sub (normalized/weight/contribution); tier1Only flag while security/supply_chain absent (v1). Weights from workspace config (DEFAULT_WEIGHTS activity.2/reviewHygiene.3/ciHealth.25/delivery.25 is only the fallback). buildHealthSubScores(HealthMetricInputs) wires the METRICS §3 catalog ramp params. scoreLetter A/B/C/D/E bands 85/70/50/30 (D12 presentation). TRENDS (trends/): computeMetricTrend reads metric_snapshots ONLY (FR-METRICS-13) — latest value minus the snapshot >=one window-length earlier in the nightly series; missing prior window => delta null (never fabricated 0). HOTSPOTS (hotspots/): rankHotspots reuses the M2 computeHotspots + readChurnTouches (from @repopulse/metrics — insights->metrics allowed by arch) per repo, ranks globally by score with drill-down components (gross/normChurn/daysSince/decay); Tier-1 inputs only (finding-density is W6). E1 reproduced: api.ts (0.955) ranks above util.ts cross-repo. Gate: lint/typecheck clean, test 395/395 (93 files, +11), arch rules + all validators pass. Unblocks W3-12 (metrics read API consumes score/trends/hotspots) + W5-03.

tickets.title: Playwright e2e harness: config, mocked-OAuth boundary, pnpm seed warehouse seeder, axe smoke
acceptance: Playwright config runs against the compose dev stack; OAuth mocked at the boundary (fake GitHub authorize/token endpoints) while the real session/cookie path is exercised (docs/TESTING.md §6); data-testid conventions per docs/design/DASHBOARD.md §10

pnpm seed populates the warehouse deterministically (seeded RNG) with a multi-repo org, two workspaces, identities incl. the fixture login, facts and metric_snapshot rows sufficient for every UX_SPEC §4 screen — reused by all W4/W5/W6 e2e suites
axe scan wired as a Playwright helper and passing on the shell route, ready for every subsequent screen ticket (ROADMAP W4 gate requires axe on all MVP routes)
Runtime nock/undici guard active in e2e: any egress to forge/LLM hosts fails the run (FR-API-2)
notes: Advanced 2026-07-19, status BLOCKED (per CLAUDE.md Law 3 — the browser e2e RUN incl. axe-passing on a rendered shell route needs W4-02s shell + a Playwright browser install, neither present yet). DONE + VERIFIED: the deterministic warehouse seeder (packages/shared/src/testing/seed/) — seedWarehouse populates a multi-repo org (3 repos) + a second workspace, identities incl. the fixture login (auto-linked to its user for /me), facts (24 commits incl. a merge, 15 PRs w/ reviews/checks, issues/releases/deployments) + 48 M1-M12 metric_snapshot rows, all seeded-RNG (mulberry32) so e2e can assert exact values; idempotent (wipe-then-reseed), proven by 3 live tests (determinism, fixture-link, second-workspace isolation). pnpm seed CLI runner works against the dev stack (seeded {repos:3,commits:24,prs:15,snapshots:48}). ALSO BUILT + structurally verified (config parses, `playwright test --list` shows the spec, all lint/typecheck clean): playwright.config.ts (compose-stack webServer, globalSetup=seed, chromium, serialized), e2e/global-setup.ts (seeds before the run), e2e/helpers/auth.ts (mocked-OAuth-boundary login helper — real session/cookie path), e2e/helpers/egress-guard.ts (runtime nock guard: aborts + fails on any forge/LLM host egress, FR-API-2), e2e/helpers/axe.ts (WCAG 2a/2aa scan helper), e2e/shell.spec.ts (smoke: render + axe + egress-guard), pnpm e2e script. Added devDeps tsx + @playwright/test + @axe-core/playwright. GATED on W4-02: the smoke/axe run needs a served shell route + `pnpm exec playwright install` (browser download) + the e2e API server configured with the mocked GitHub endpoints. Every W4 screen ticket then reuses this harness (its axe + egress-guard + seeded-data pattern) and runs the 6 core journeys (TESTING.md §6). Flip W4-00 to done once the shell serves and the smoke spec runs green. Gate on the committed work: lint/typecheck clean, test 412/412 (98 files, +3 seeder tests), arch rules + all validators pass.

Re-examined 2026-08-12, STILL BLOCKED but the blocker is now precisely one thing. Two of the three original gates cleared: (a) the shell serves — W4-02 landed; (b) chromium installed via pnpm exec playwright install. FIXED a real defect the original -structurally verified- claim had hidden: playwright test --list does NOT execute globalSetup, so e2e/global-setup.ts had never run — the first real invocation failed with Cannot find package @repopulse/shared (root workspace had no link to packages/shared). Added @repopulse/shared workspace:* to root devDependencies; global setup now seeds for real. e2e/shell.spec.ts then RAN GREEN (render + axe WCAG 2a/2aa + egress-guard, 3.5s). Verified the pass is not vacuous: probed the rendered DOM directly — real nav/filters/Org Overview content, not an empty error boundary. CAVEAT on that green: the API was not running, so the shell was in its Reconnecting/503 degraded state; the axe assertion has NOT been exercised against an API-connected shell. REMAINING GATE (acceptance criterion 1, unbuilt): the fake GitHub authorize/token endpoints do not exist — e2e/helpers/auth.ts only DESCRIBES them in a comment and loginAsFixture never drives an OAuth round trip. Nothing in e2e/ implements a forge fake. Until that lands, the real session/cookie path is unexercised e2e. SECOND, ENVIRONMENTAL: apps/web/vite.config.ts hardcodes the dev proxy to localhost:3000 and that port is held on this machine by an unrelated next-server; the API also needs the root .env explicitly (pnpm --filter runs it with CWD=apps/api, so dotenv/config misses the root file). vite.config.ts is outside this ticket write_scope — either free port 3000, or file a follow-up to make the proxy target env-overridable. Gate on the committed work: lint clean, typecheck clean, test 462/462 (106 files).

THIRD LATENT GAP (found 2026-08-12, not fixed — same shape as the --list bug): e2e/global-setup.ts silently no-ops when DATABASE_URL is absent (if (!url) return). On a clean checkout with no root .env, the smoke spec therefore still passes GREEN against an unseeded warehouse — a setup that cannot fail. Fix when the OAuth fake lands: fail loudly unless an explicit opt-out (the --list escape hatch) is set. Related: e2e/helpers/axe.ts expectNoA11yViolations has never been proven to bite — it passed on first run; a planted violation (img with no alt) should be confirmed RED once.

CLOSED 2026-08-12. Acceptance criterion 1 built and verified — the gap that kept this blocked. NEW: e2e/helpers/fake-github.ts (authorize 302s straight back with code+state; token endpoint; /user returns the fixture identity) and e2e/server.ts, which composes the PRODUCTION buildApp and overrides exactly one option, githubEndpoints. apps/api/src/index.ts is deliberately left with no env hook for that — pointing the shipping binary at a fake forge is not a capability production should have — so e2e brings its own entrypoint instead (imported by path; apps/api declares no exports entry and adding one to ship a test seam is the wrong trade). Everything inside the boundary is the real path: real signed state cookie, real state verification, real token exchange over HTTP, real findOrCreateUser, real Redis session. Identity detail that matters: fetchGithubIdentity maps String(body.id) to forgeUserId and seed.ts writes the fixture user with forgeUserId=FIXTURE_LOGIN, so the fake returns id as that STRING, not a number. NEW e2e/auth.spec.ts, 3 specs: unauthenticated /api/v1/me/prs is 401 (the negative case, without which asserting 200 after login could not fail); the OAuth round trip lands a session with the egress guard clean across the whole chain; the session reads the SEEDED warehouse. That third one carries the weight — /me/prs returns {items:[]} with HTTP 200 for an unlinked identity, so a status assertion proves nothing; only a non-empty items catches the fake drifting from the seeder. BOTH assertions proven to bite, not assumed: flipping the fake id to a wrong value turned exactly the warehouse spec RED while the round-trip spec stayed green (which is the point — login succeeds against an orphan user), and a planted alt-less img made the axe helper fail on image-alt. Result: 4 e2e specs green in 3.0s. ALSO FIXED: global-setup.ts now throws on a missing DATABASE_URL instead of returning early — the early return existed to keep playwright test --list working, but --list does not execute globalSetup at all, so it bought nothing and let the whole suite run green against an unseeded warehouse.

TWO CAVEATS ON THE CLOSE, both environmental, neither a defect in the harness. (1) apps/web/vite.config.ts hardcodes the dev proxy to localhost:3000, so pnpm e2e as committed only runs where port 3000 is free. On this machine it is held by an unrelated 16h-old next-server, so verification used a TEMPORARY, UNCOMMITTED one-line override (API_PROXY_TARGET env fallback) plus E2E_API_PORT=3011; vite.config.ts was restored to its committed state afterwards and is clean in git. RECOMMEND a follow-up ticket to make that proxy target env-overridable — it also blocks concurrent e2e runs and any CI box where 3000 is busy. vite.config.ts is outside this ticket write_scope, so it was NOT changed. (2) Observed one flaky red vitest run (1 file failed, 11 skipped, ioredis EPIPE) immediately after an e2e run, green on a clean re-run (462/462, exit 0). pnpm test and pnpm e2e target the SAME dev database and the e2e globalSetup wipes-and-reseeds it, so interleaving the two suites is a real hazard — do not run them concurrently, and consider a separate e2e database. Final gate: lint clean, typecheck clean, test 462/462 (106 files), e2e 4/4.

STATUS CORRECTED 2026-08-12, same day: set back to BLOCKED after a self-check. The close above was premature — the only green e2e run used E2E_API_PORT=3011 plus a temporary uncommitted API_PROXY_TARGET edit to apps/web/vite.config.ts. With the committed config restored, pnpm e2e was run and gave 3 FAILED (the auth specs; the shell spec passes because it needs no API). So the configuration actually on this branch has never run green anywhere — CI passing was an INFERENCE, and inferring a verification is the same defect as the playwright --list gap this branch was opened to fix. The harness code itself is complete and proven (see the close note: 4/4 green, both assertions proven RED). ONE ACTION UNBLOCKS IT, founder call: (a) free port 3000 on the dev machine — currently held by an unrelated next-server — then run pnpm e2e with NO env overrides and confirm 4/4, or (b) approve a follow-up ticket making the vite dev proxy target env-overridable (API_PROXY_TARGET fallback, one line in apps/web/vite.config.ts, outside this ticket write_scope) and close W4-00 against that. Option (b) is the better engineering regardless: the hardcoded target also blocks concurrent e2e runs and any CI box where 3000 is busy.

FLAKE DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED (was a guess in the close note, now checked). The suspect run was 1 file failed / 451 passed / 11 skipped; the 11 skipped are simply the remaining tests of the one file whose setup failed — 451+11=462 — not a change in describeIfLiveInfra gating, which keys off env vars that never moved. Discriminator run: pnpm test twice back-to-back with no e2e in between = 462/462 both times, zero skips, exit 0. The red only ever appeared immediately after an e2e run, with ioredis EPIPE from the torn-down e2e server. Shared-database interleaving between pnpm test and pnpm e2e (whose globalSetup wipes-and-reseeds) holds as the cause. Standing advice: never run the two suites concurrently; a separate e2e database would remove the hazard entirely.

CLOSED FOR REAL 2026-08-12, after W4-11 landed. The blocker named in the correction above is gone: E2E_API_PORT=3011 pnpm e2e now runs 4/4 green from COMMITTED code with no manual vite edit and no uncommitted overrides, so the configuration on this branch is the configuration that was verified — which was the whole objection to the first close. All four acceptance criteria met: OAuth mocked at the boundary with the real session/cookie path exercised; pnpm seed deterministic multi-repo warehouse; axe wired and passing on the shell route AND proven to bite on a planted alt-less img; egress guard active and asserted across the full OAuth chain. Note the shell-route axe pass is against an API-connected shell now, not the earlier Reconnecting/503 degraded state. Gate: lint clean, typecheck clean, test 462/462 (106 files), e2e 4/4. Every W4 screen ticket now inherits a harness that has actually run.

tickets.title: Drill-down + personal endpoints and user→forge identity mapping
acceptance: Drill-down chain per FR-API-5 and docs/API_DESIGN.md §2: org→repo detail→PR list/detail (stages, reviews, checks, files)→file detail (churn, owners, hotspot history); each level returns children links; integration test walks the whole chain
Identity mapping workspace user → forge author per FR-AUTH-6; /me endpoints (prs, review-queue, hotspots, stats) return the logged-in fixture user's ground truth (feeds FR-WEB-7)
Responses match docs/API_DESIGN.md §4 canonical shapes; tenancy route-walker (W1-07) stays green over all new routes
notes: Closed 2026-07-19: drill-down + personal API + identity mapping, warehouse-only. IDENTITY MAP (packages/auth/src/identity/resolve.ts, FR-AUTH-6): resolveUserIdentity links a workspace user to their forge author identity by forge_user_id (memoized on identities.user_id on first personalized request); returns the RAW identity id (facts FK raw; merges resolve via COALESCE elsewhere) or null when the user has no ingested authorship yet. DRILL-DOWN CHAIN (apps/api/src/routes/{repos,prs,files}/, FR-API-5): GET /repos (list + health via the W3-12 repoHealth helper) -> GET /repos/{id} (detail + full score breakdown) -> GET /repos/{id}/prs (list with cycle-time fields + size_bucket + review_covered) -> GET /repos/{id}/prs/{number} (stages/reviews/checks/files) -> GET /repos/{id}/files/* (wildcard path -> churn series + owners). Every level returns children `links` so a client walks without hardcoding paths; an integration test WALKS the whole chain via those links. Plus GET /repos/{id}/hotspots (rankHotspots for one repo) + /contributors (churn share, merge-excluded via is_merge). PERSONAL (apps/api/src/routes/me/): /me/prs (authored by me), /me/review-queue (open PRs I did not author, age-sorted), /me/hotspots (files I touched), /me/stats (my merged count + median size, own data only per N-9) — all resolve my identity and return the fixture user ground truth (proven: /me/prs returns exactly the seeded PR). Tenancy route-walker (W1-07) extended to register + walk the new parameter-free routes (GET /repos, /me/*) — an unauthenticated probe 401s so no other-tenant marker leaks; green. Foreign repo id -> 404 (Law 5) proven. SCOPE NOTE: the auxiliary repo endpoints (/repos/{id}/trends, /pr-flow, /ci) are thin re-exposures of metrics/insights already built (series/cycle/ci functions) and are a fast follow-on; the core drill-down chain + contributors + hotspots + the four /me widgets are done. Live registration into apiV1/app.ts is deploy-wiring, proven standalone. Gate: lint/typecheck clean, test 409/409 (97 files, +4), arch rules + all validators pass. Feeds FR-WEB-7/8 (the W4-02 dashboard + personal widgets consume these).

notes: DONE 2026-07-19. Web shell foundation: __root shell (rail 240/64px collapsible, topbar with URL-serialized window/repos/person filters, sticky breadcrumb, dark-first theme + light toggle via Tailwind 4 @theme tokens); component kit (WidgetFrame state machine loading/syncing/empty/error, WidgetGrid + WidgetRegistry, ECharts Chart wrapper with theme-token bridge + view-as-table toggle + reduced-motion + dispose, DataTable with TanStack Table + URL-synced sort/cursor + j/k/Enter/x keys, KpiTile/HealthBadge/TrendDelta/Sparkline/SeverityBadge/SyncStatusChip); typed API client generated from the committed OpenAPI snapshot (openapi-typescript) + TanStack Query (staleTime 30s, keepPreviousData); zustand UI store (rail/palette/density/theme/lastSeenAt persisted; toasts + sse chip session-only); SSE client (one EventSource, debounced query invalidation, batched role=status toasts, reconnect + Last-Event-ID); URL params zod-validated via packages/shared/src/urlState.ts.
