tickets.title: Org Overview screen
acceptance: Screen per docs/UX_SPEC.md §4.a: 5 KPI tiles with sparkline + TrendDelta, repo health tile grid (click → repo), cross-repo hotspot leaderboard (click → file drill-down), attention feed computed vs last_seen_at, org sync banner
Playwright: landing renders tiles + sparklines from the fixture warehouse (FR-WEB-1 acceptance); every number click lands on its evidence (UX_SPEC §1.3)
States per UX_SPEC §4.a: first-run empty shows role-appropriate connect CTA; backfilling repos render syncing chips with %, never zeros (UX_SPEC §8)
notes: ROUTING (from W4-02): the shell bootstraps CODE-BASED routing in apps/web/src/main.tsx (root route + placeholder index + not-found). DASHBOARD §1 + TECH_STACK specify FILE-BASED routes (@tanstack/router-plugin, routes/ dir, routeTree.gen.ts). First step of this ticket: decide — migrate to file-based (add the Vite router plugin + move HomePlaceholder to routes/index.tsx) OR keep code-based and add a line to DASHBOARD §1 blessing it. Do not diverge silently. createRootRouteWithContext (already used) is compatible with both.

WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-12 before any code was written, because the acceptance was not reachable from the original scope (apps/web/src/routes/index.tsx + widgets/org/**). Acceptance 2 is a Playwright assertion and needs e2e/**. The index route is currently HomePlaceholder defined inline in main.tsx, so main.tsx changes under EITHER routing choice. File-based routing needs the Vite plugin (apps/web/vite.config.ts) and a direct devDependency (apps/web/package.json), plus routes/** rather than the single routes/index.tsx. Widening scope so stated acceptance becomes reachable; acceptance itself is UNCHANGED and nothing was narrowed — narrowing would be a founder call.

ROUTING DECIDED: FILE-BASED, and it was not a judgment call. docs/TECH_STACK.md:136 records TanStack Router 1.x file-based as BRIEF-FIXED, and FOUNDING_BRIEF decisions are marked do-not-relitigate; TECH_STACK:186-189 further specify routes/ + generated routeTree.gen.ts (commit it, never hand-edit) +  file naming + @tanstack/router-plugin, warning that omitting the plugin causes stale trees and route-not-found confusion. W4-02 code-based bootstrap was the divergence, so the ticket note framing (decide, or bless code-based in DASHBOARD §1) resolves to migrate. Migrating now is also cheapest it will ever be — only two routes exist — and eight more screen tickets inherit the choice.

DATA CHECK before building: all four endpoints acceptance 1 needs already exist — GET /org/summary, /org/health-tiles, /org/attention (?since=<iso>) and /hotspots. lastSeenAt is CLIENT state (zustand persist, localStorage, apps/web/src/components/store/uiStore.ts:43) fed to /org/attention as ?since, per DASHBOARD §60-61 — not a DB column on a user row. So no acceptance clause is unbuildable and nothing needs narrowing.

LAYOUT DIVERGENCE FLAGGED, not silently established: write_scope puts these under apps/web/src/widgets/org/**, a new top-level dir parallel to src/components/, which already holds components/widget/ (WidgetGrid, WidgetFrame). Following write_scope since Law 1 makes it authoritative, but a later ticket should either fold widgets/ into components/ or add a line to DASHBOARD §1 blessing the split — two homes for widget code will confuse every subsequent screen ticket.

SCREEN BUILT AND GREEN, ticket BLOCKED on W4-13 (fixture), 2026-08-12. Shipped: file-based routing migration (routeTree.gen.ts generated + committed, plugin ordered before plugin-react, test files excluded from route generation) and widgets/org/{OrgOverview,KpiRow,HealthTileGrid,HotspotLeaderboard,AttentionFeed,contracts}. Each widget owns its query/loading/error state so one failing endpoint degrades a card, not the dashboard. Gate green: lint, typecheck, test 462/462, e2e 7/7. WHAT IS NOT MET is acceptance 2s -renders tiles + sparklines from the fixture warehouse-, and the reason is fixture data, not screen code — see W4-13 for the three measured gaps. HONESTY NOTE ON THE TEST: my first version asserted the KPI row innerText was non-empty after stripping em dashes. It PASSED while all five tiles rendered nothing but em dashes, because the tile LABELS are innerText too — a test that could not fail. Caught by probing the rendered DOM rather than trusting green. The vacuous assertion was removed rather than weakened, and the real value+sparkline assertion is now W4-13 acceptance, to be written where it can actually pass. The two shipped e2e specs assert DOORS (href target + filter preservation through the hop), which is genuine W4-03 behaviour and independent of fixture richness.

ROLE GAP (needs a founder call, do not narrow silently): acceptance 3 wants a role-appropriate first-run CTA — admin -Connect your org- vs member -Ask an admin-. No endpoint exposes the callers role: apps/api/src/plugins/api-v1.ts:53 sets request.role server-side and never returns it, and /me is the minimal {user} shape (its own comment says workspace/role/identity_id need infra deferred from W1-03). Implemented the member-safe copy as the single variant, because showing admin copy to a member is a dead end for someone who cannot act on it while the reverse is merely less direct. Either add role to a /me-shaped response in an API ticket, or ratify the single-variant copy.

CLOSED 2026-08-12 once W4-13 landed. Acceptance 2 now met at the DEFAULT window, not a widened workaround: KPI tiles carry real values (review coverage 90%, CI pass rate 100%, cycle time 134h, churn 142 lines, throughput 116) with trend deltas, 5 sparklines render, 3 health tiles, 9 hotspot rows; door specs assert href target + filter preservation through the hop, pinned to a NON-default window on purpose since serializeGlobalSearch omits defaults and a default value cannot prove a filter survived. BUG FOUND AND FIXED BY PROBING THE RENDERED SCREEN, not by a failing test: ratio metrics (M5/M6/M9) are stored 0..1, so review coverage rendered -0.9 %- and a perfect CI pass rate rendered -1 %-. Both read as catastrophic rather than good — an outage, not 100%. formatKpi now scales by unit. Green e2e did not catch it because no assertion read the value text; only looking at the screen did. Acceptance 3 role-branching remains the one open item, carried on its own note as a founder call (no endpoint exposes the callers role).
W4-03 acceptance 3 CLOSED by W4-14 (2026-08-12): the role-branching first-run CTA is live; the single member-safe variant noted above was the interim, not the final state.

tickets.title: Repo Detail screen (Pulse / Hotspots / PR Flow / CI tabs)
acceptance: Tabbed screen per docs/UX_SPEC.md §4.b with each tab a routed URL per docs/design/DASHBOARD.md §1; Findings tab renders the pre-v1.x teaser
'why?' health-score popover shows the full formula breakdown + basis label from the score endpoint (FR-INSIGHTS-2/3, UX_SPEC §1.4)

Visualizations per FR-WEB-3: hotspot directory treemap (dir zoom, file click → drill-down) with side top-N list showing churn × recency components and bus-factor flags; PR Flow funnel + review-load matrix + XS–XL histogram; CI pass/duration trends + flaky ranking — all from fixtures, each chart with table toggle (NFR-5)
Playwright walks org→repo→tab by clicks AND by direct URL paste (FR-WEB-2)
notes: DONE 2026-08-12. Tabs are ROUTES, not local state (DASHBOARD 1): /repos/$repoId/{,hotspots,pr-flow,ci,findings} plus a /repos list so a pasted /repos URL is not a dead end. Shipped: Pulse (4 repo-scoped trend charts), Hotspots (ECharts treemap with native directory zoom + top-N table linking to W4-06 file drill-down), PR Flow (opened→reviewed→merged funnel + XS-XL histogram in METRICS M7 order, never alphabetical), CI (M9 pass-rate trend scaled to percent), Findings teaser, and the health "why?" popover showing basis label + per-axis normalized x weight = contribution so the arithmetic is checkable rather than asserted. Every chart carries tableData — NFR-5 treats a chart with no text equivalent as inaccessible, not merely unpolished.

THREE BUGS, each found by looking rather than by a green test. (1) ECHARTS SERIES NOT REGISTERED: echarts.ts registers only Line and Bar, and its comment claimed "line + bar cover trend/histogram/funnel" — they do not. An unregistered series type fails at RUNTIME with a console error and draws NOTHING, so the Hotspots and PR Flow tabs rendered empty boxes that still passed a toBeVisible assertion. Registered Treemap + Funnel and corrected the comment. (2) RELATIVE TAB LINKS COMPOUNDED: to="hotspots" resolves against the CURRENT route, so once on /hotspots the link became /repos/N/hotspots/hotspots. Caught by the deep-link spec — a click-through walk would have kept passing. Switched to absolute /repos/$repoId/... paths. (3) BREAKDOWN CONTRACT WRONG: I typed health.breakdown as Record<string,number>; it is an ARRAY of {key, normalized, weight, contribution}. Would have rendered a silently blank popover.

TEST-QUALITY NOTE. My first specs asserted panel testids were visible — but those testids sit on ALWAYS-rendered containers, so they passed while a probe showed the screen still loading and every chart empty. Same vacuous shape as the W4-03 KPI assertion. Strengthened to assert resolved content: repo-name contains "/" (only true after /repos/{id} returns), Pulse draws exactly 4 canvases, each tab draws at least one, the treemap is visible, and the popover has real <dt> rows. RED-checked by removing TreemapChart — the hotspots canvas assertion fails, which is what proves it bites. ALSO fixed a harness limit surfaced by the suite growing to 15 specs: SC-11 caps the auth flow at 10 requests/minute, so a login per spec exhausted it and surfaced as an unrelated-looking waitForURL timeout rather than a 429. globalSetup now logs in ONCE and saves storageState; the anonymous specs opt out explicitly and one spec still drives the full OAuth chain. Suite went 25.2s → 5.3s, three consecutive clean runs. Gate: lint clean, typecheck clean, test 462/462, e2e 15/15.

NOT BUILT, filed as W4-15: the PR Flow review-load matrix and the CI duration/flaky ranking. None are reachable from the current API — the PR list has no per-reviewer counts and metric_snapshots stores one scalar per metric, so M9 arrives as pass-rate only. The CI tab carries an explicit empty state naming W4-15 instead of a proxy chart: a review-load matrix built from author data would look plausible and answer a different question, on a screen whose entire job is evidence.

tickets.title: PR list + PR Detail screen

TIMELINE DESIGN DETAIL worth keeping: a missing milestone renders as an em dash, never 0h. A PR merged with no review has an ABSENT review stage, and "0h to first review" would read as an instantaneous review rather than none at all — the opposite conclusion from the same data. BOTH load-bearing assertions RED-checked, not assumed. Dropping `state` from the query (filter rides the URL but never reaches the API) turns the filter spec red with Expected 3 / Received 5. Forcing toStages down the merged branch turns the open-PR spec red with Expected 1 / Received 0 — and the merged-PR spec asserts the elapsed stage is ABSENT, so the pair proves the function branches on merged_at rather than always producing one shape. Fanning out one request per repo from the browser would be an N+1 against the NFR-3 p95 budget that degrades silently as repo count grows, so /pull-requests lists repos and routes into each repo list instead. tickets.title: File drill-down screen
acceptance: Screen per docs/UX_SPEC.md §4.d: 52-week stacked churn bars (gross/net/rework), owners list with top-author-share >=80% flag, recent-PRs table → PR detail, hotspot-score history sparkline, file-scoped findings list placeholder

notes: DONE 2026-08-12. Splat route /repos/$repoId/files/$ so a file path keeps its slashes in the URL instead of being flattened into one segment (FR-WEB-2). Shipped: 52-week churn bars (gross + net) aggregated client-side from the per-commit series, owners table, and the M3 single-owner flag at top-author-share >=0.80. The hotspot-leaderboard link has existed since W4-03 but pointed at a route that did not exist until now — the click-through is the acceptance path and is asserted.

DESIGN DECISION, verified rather than assumed: EVERY week in the 52-week window is emitted, including empty ones. Measured the alternative — filtering empty buckets renders this fixture file in 5 bars instead of 52, drawing a file touched in a few bursts as if it were touched steadily. The quiet periods are the signal, so the spec now asserts toHaveCount(52) on the table fallback. Commits older than the window are dropped rather than clamped into the first bucket, which would invent a spike that never happened.

NOT BUILT, filed as W4-17 and named in a visible empty state rather than omitted: rework component, hotspot-score history, per-file PR list, and the deleted/renamed banner with its rename chain. None are in the endpoint payload. Drawing gross churn labelled "rework" would misstate a defined metric (M1 scopes rework to a prior non-bot touch <21d earlier); a flat line labelled "hotspot history" would invent a trend from one current value. Gate: lint clean, typecheck clean, test 462/462, e2e 24/24.

A TEST DEFECT THAT LOOKED LIKE A DATA-ISOLATION BUG. My first review-queue spec compared the RENDERED row text of my PRs against the queue and found an overlap. The API was correct: the seeder gives every repo identical PR titles, so -#4 feature 4- exists in all three repos and a text comparison reports a false collision. Checked the actual identities before touching any code — zero overlap by repo_id + number. The spec now compares identities, and was RED-checked by removing the author filter from the query, which makes it fail for the real reason. tickets.title: Admin screens: Connections, Sync (DLQ ops), Members
acceptance: Tabs per docs/UX_SPEC.md §4.i: Connections (credential fingerprint/last-4, repo picker, pause/remove with optional purge per FR-INGEST-9), Sync (per-repo phase/%/budget gauge/lag/last-webhook + DLQ list with replay button per NFR-11), Members (admin/member role assignment)
Admin API routes per docs/API_DESIGN.md §2 'admin' with role guard; member hitting /admin gets the 403 page with 'ask an admin' copy (FR-AUTH-4, DASHBOARD.md §1 admin/route.tsx)
Failing-webhook repo row flagged crit with remediation hint; forge budget gauge + sync lag surfaced so 'is ingest healthy' is answerable from this page (NFR-12)
notes: DONE 2026-08-13. Admin is a tabbed route set like the repo screen: /admin (Connections), /admin/sync, /admin/members. Connections is the screen docs/INSTALL.md sends operators to and the only way to connect an organisation — a create form plus the connection list showing provider, auth kind, credential last-4, status and repo count. Sync shows the org aggregate plus a per-repo table with phase, progress, rate-limit budget remaining, lag and last error; budget is on screen because Law 7 makes it law and an operator needs to see it BEFORE a repo goes paused_budget, not after. The role gate on the layout is presentation only — the API enforces admin independently with a 403 (FR-AUTH-4).

FOUND BEFORE WRITING ANY UI: the API requires x-requested-with: repopulse on every mutating verb (SC-7 CSRF) and the web client never sent it, so every write from the SPA would have returned 403 with no hint — a Connect button that looks inert. Added the header to apiFetch (a simple header, so no CORS preflight) plus a useApiMutation hook that invalidates the query keys a caller names.

A TEST THAT COULD NOT FAIL, caught and fixed in the same sitting. The credential spec asserted only that AN error appeared after submitting — but a CSRF 403 and a rejected-credential 400 both render an error, so the spec passed with the client header DELETED. That is exactly how a silently-403ing Connect button ships. The assertion now requires the error to be about the CREDENTIAL, proving the write reached the handler; RED-checked by deleting the header again, which now fails with "Missing or invalid X-Requested-With header".

Also corrected my own over-strict assertion rather than the code: I first asserted the credential never appears in the DOM at all, which failed because a FAILED connect deliberately keeps the value so the operator can fix a typo — it is a password input. Probing showed the credential appears in exactly one place, its own input, and nowhere else: not echoed by the API, not in the error envelope, not in the list. The spec now states that property precisely. Gate (checked on exit codes, not summary lines): lint 0, typecheck 0, test 0 with 463/463, e2e 0 with 30/30.

FOLLOW-UP 2026-08-13: added the REPO PICKER, which W4-08 had shipped without. Creating a connection only stores a credential — POST /connections/{id}/repos is what creates repo rows, registers webhooks and enqueues the backfill plans. Without a picker an operator could connect and then had no way to start collecting anything, so docs/INSTALL.md 4 ('connect your organisation, backfill starts immediately') was not achievable from the UI. Caught the request-body key by reading the zod schema rather than assuming: it is repo_forge_ids, not forge_repo_ids, and my first version would have 400d.

Also decoupled a cross-spec assertion I had made brittle: org-overview asserted EXACTLY 3 health tiles as a stand-in for tenancy, but the new ingest specs legitimately add repos to the same workspace, so the count depended on spec order and failed intermittently (one run 35.2s with a failure, then clean). Replaced with >=3 plus a direct assertion that the second seeded workspace never appears — which is what the exact count was really standing in for (NFR-4). Three consecutive clean runs at 39/39.

tickets.title: Workspace settings API + admin Settings tab (score weights, bot list, stale-N, budget share)
acceptance: GET/PATCH /admin/workspace per docs/API_DESIGN.md §2 'admin': health-score weights (validated to sum semantics of METRICS.md §3), bot-login glob list, stale-PR N days, forge budget share/floor — zod-validated, admin-only 403 for members (FR-AUTH-4), every change audit-logged (SC-22)

Admin → Settings tab renders current values with the METRICS.md §3 defaults labeled; editing the bot list or stale-N is reflected in the next metric recompute/snapshot (integration test); weights change is reflected in the health-score breakdown endpoint

LLM-related settings (LM host list, concurrency cap, T3 monthly USD cap) render as disabled placeholders with 'lands with analysis wave' copy — schema columns exist from W1 (DATABASE.md workspaces.settings), UI activates in W6/W7
Tenancy walker + axe green over the new route
notes: WRITE_SCOPE AMENDED 2026-08-15, before any code, because as filed it could not satisfy its own acceptance 2 — and widening it silently is the thing MASTER_PROMPT rule 3 exists to prevent. Acceptance 2 requires an edited bot list or stale-N to reach 'the next metric recompute/snapshot' and an edited weight to reach 'the health-score breakdown endpoint'. Neither surface is inside apps/api/src/routes/admin/** or apps/web/**: snapshots are computed in apps/api/src/workers/processors.ts and the breakdown is built in apps/api/src/routes/org/health.ts. Added file-by-file rather than as a glob: lib/workspace-settings.ts (the zod schema + reader, needed by BOTH the route and the worker, so it cannot live under routes/), plugins/api-v1.ts (mounting — five built-but-never-mounted defects in this project so far, so registration is part of the work, not an afterthought), packages/shared/src/logger/audit.ts (acceptance 1's SC-22 audit event class; the AuditEvent union is a closed type that grows per wave by design), routes/admin/route.tsx (a tab nobody can navigate to is the same defect in the UI), and e2e/** (acceptance 4 wants axe green over the new route).

FOUND WHILE READING, not part of this ticket: apps/api/src/workers/processors.ts:368 passes `botGlobs: []` to computeRepoSnapshots. Empty array is NOT 'use the defaults' — isBotLogin does `globs.some(...)`, so [] means NOTHING is a bot and METRICS.md §0's shared rule ('exclude bot activity from every human-flow metric') has never held in production. DEFAULT_BOT_LOGIN_GLOBS exists and is passed by nobody. Every churn, hotspot and ownership number computed from real ingestion counts dependabot as a human. Fixed as part of this ticket since acceptance 2 puts the settings-derived bot list through exactly this call, but worth recording separately: it is a data-correctness bug, not a settings feature.

DONE 2026-08-15. All four criteria met. GET/PATCH /admin/workspace are zod-validated, admin-only (a member gets 403 on BOTH verbs, asserted), and every PATCH writes an SC-22 audit entry naming the CHANGED KEYS and not their values — the LM host list lands in this same object in W6, and an audit stream is not where a credential should surface. PATCH MERGES rather than replaces, for the same reason: a `.set({settings: body})` would delete the W6/W7 keys the moment an admin saved a weight.

THE WEIGHT TEST IS THE ONE THAT EARNS ITS SETUP COST. buildHealthSubScores looks weights up as `weights.reviewHygiene ?? DEFAULT_WEIGHTS.reviewHygiene`, so a renamed key or an unwired call does not fail — it silently scores exactly as before. The test therefore reads the breakdown endpoint's own numbers with TWO sub-scores present (M5 + M9): with one, computeHealthScore renormalizes its weight to 1.0 and every possible weight config produces identical output, so the test would have passed against a completely unwired endpoint. M9 is seeded at 0.8 rather than 0.5 for the same class of reason — 0.5 clamps ramp(0.95,0.6) to zero and every contribution becomes 0 x weight, which compares equal regardless. The schema also rejects snake_case weight keys, since those would fall through to defaults silently rather than erroring.

SUM SEMANTICS, read rather than assumed: METRICS.md §3's four Tier-1 weights sum to 1.00, and security (+0.20) / supply chain (+0.10) are added ON TOP and renormalized. So the refinement checks the four, and deliberately does not check a total that includes the two sub-scores that do not exist yet. The check is not arithmetic necessity — computeHealthScore renormalizes by the present weights, so a set summing to 4.0 yields identical numbers — it is so a stored config means what §3's table says when a human reads it back.

THE BOT-LIST BUG IS FIXED, and it was the real find. processors.ts passed a literal `botGlobs: []`, which reads as 'no override' but means 'nothing is a bot' (isBotLogin does globs.some over an empty array), so METRICS.md §0's exclusion rule had never held for any number computed from real ingestion. The settings reader returns DEFAULT_BOT_LOGIN_GLOBS when unset and an empty array only when an admin chose one, and `??` is used rather than `||` throughout so an emptied list survives. Pinned by unit tests on both states. The Settings screen says out loud what an empty box does ('dependabot then counts as a contributor') instead of letting it read as unset.

HANDOFF for W4-20 (closed, not reopened here): its PATCH /admin/members/:userId is NOT audit-logged, though SC-22 names 'admin role change' explicitly. The pieces are in place — auditLog is imported one file away and the AuditEvent union now grows per wave by design — but SC-22's verify clause wants an integration test per event class, so it is not a two-line change, and satisfying a closed ticket's acceptance from inside a different ticket would make the board stop meaning anything. Founder call.

Gate: lint 0, typecheck 0, 562 unit tests (was 543), 44 e2e + 1 skipped (was 42), validate-arch/plan/traceability all exit 0. Unit suite run TWICE to prove teardown is clean — the first run of the new suite left a second admin in the shared `default` workspace and broke W4-20's last-admin assertion in a file this ticket never touched. e2e must be run as `E2E_API_PORT=3010 pnpm e2e` on this machine: a compose dev stack holds port 3000, which is exactly what W4-11 shipped the override for.

tickets.title: Journey pack: persona picker, onboarding checklist, first-insight toast, rail badges, visual deltas
acceptance: Persona picker at first login per docs/UX_SPEC.md §6 (D9/R-A2): one question, stored users.persona (migration + rollback note), changeable in user menu; routes P1→Org Overview, P2→My Focus, P3→Findings, P4→Exec view (E2E per persona)

Onboarding checklist card on Org Overview until dismissed — admin variant (connect ✓ → bot list → roles → starter views → first report) and member variant (choose focus → guided drill-down); state persisted, no new tables beyond users.persona
First-insight toast: when a repo's 30d coverage completes (per-entity sync phase already tracked), SSE-driven toast 'last 30 days ready for {repo}' (docs/work/UX_AGENTS_IMPROVEMENT_PLANS.md R-A3)

notes: SPLIT PROPOSED 2026-08-15, before writing code, after reading each criterion against the code rather than after discovering it mid-implementation. Three of the five cannot be satisfied inside this ticket, for three DIFFERENT reasons, so they are filed rather than faked. (3) first-insight toast: there is no producer — see W4-22, publishSyncEvent has ZERO production callers, so no SSE event of any kind is ever published and a 30d-coverage event does not exist to filter. (4) findings half of the rail badges: Findings Explorer ships in MVP as a teaser shell, there are no findings rows and no lastSeenAt, and a badge that renders 0 forever is indistinguishable from a working one. (5) hero tiles: WidgetGrid ALREADY supports per-widget w/h, but OrgOverview.tsx never uses WidgetGrid — it is hand-composed flex/grid — so the criterion is already true of the engine and false of the screen, and converting the MVP-gate landing screen (four e2e specs point at it) is a rewrite, not a journey-pack delta.

LANDED HERE: acceptance 1 (persona picker + migration) and 2 (onboarding checklist), the review-queue half of 4, and the R-D1 half of 5. REMAINDER filed as W4-21 (toast, findings badge, bento) which depends on W4-22 (the missing event producer). Left in_progress rather than closed: re-scoping acceptance is a founder call, the same principle applied to W12-03 and W12-05. This ticket blocks the W4 gate until Brad rules on the split, which is the honest state — the gate genuinely is not reached while a criterion is unmet.

LANDED 2026-08-15 — acceptance 1 and 2 in full, plus the reachable halves of 4 and 5. Migration 0006 adds users.persona (NULL = never asked, which is what opens the picker — distinct from any value, so nobody is asked twice) and users.prefs jsonb, with a rollback note. prefs is on `users` and NOT workspaces.settings deliberately: the checklist has a member variant, and workspace-scoped state would let one member's dismissal hide it for everyone. PATCH /me/prefs merges, like the W4-09 settings PATCH, since the column will hold more than one preference. The persona->home mapping lives in the API and the picker routes from the API's own answer, so the browser carries no second copy to drift.

THE CHECKLIST DOES NOT PRETEND TO TRACK PROGRESS. Steps are links, not checkboxes; only 'connect your organisation' shows as done, because the health-tiles response the screen already fetched genuinely answers it. A checkbox that never ticks itself implies the app is watching progress it is not watching.

FOUND AND FIXED, a latent race this ticket happened to trip: playwright.config.ts set `fullyParallel: false` with the comment 'shared seeded warehouse — serialize like the vitest suite', but that flag only serializes tests WITHIN a file. The suite was running 49 tests across 9 workers against ONE seeded warehouse and one fixture user. Nulling the fixture's persona to test the first-login picker made six unrelated specs in other files time out behind a modal that appeared over their screens — any spec mutating shared state would have done the same, and the next one might have corrupted data instead of blocking a click. `workers: 1` is what the comment always meant. It is also FASTER: 38s -> 21s, because the parallel run was spending its time on 30s timeouts.

Gate: lint 0, typecheck 0, 565 unit tests (was 562), 48 e2e + 1 skipped (was 44), validate-arch/plan/traceability exit 0. The seeder now gives the fixture user a persona so the picker does not cover every other spec; journey.spec.ts clears the column and restores it, so the picker is still tested against a genuinely null value rather than a mocked store write.

STILL IN_PROGRESS, deliberately. Acceptance 3 (first-insight toast), the findings half of 4, and the bento half of 5 are filed as W4-21 (blocked on W4-22, the missing SSE producer). W4-10 as written cannot close, and re-scoping acceptance is a founder call — the same principle applied to W12-03 and W12-05. RECOMMEND closing W4-10 with criteria 3/4b/5b superseded by W4-21, which is the only thing standing between this board and the W4 MVP gate.

CLOSED 2026-08-17 on the founder's instruction to proceed, after the split was put to Brad twice with the remainder and the reasoning laid out. Criteria 3 (first-insight toast), the findings half of 4, and the bento half of 5 are SUPERSEDED BY W4-21, which now carries them with the blockers named. Recorded here rather than assumed: this ticket did not meet its acceptance as written, and the board should say so plainly rather than showing a clean `done` that implies otherwise.

tickets.title: Journey pack remainder: first-insight toast, findings rail badge, Org Overview bento
acceptance: First-insight toast: when a repo’s 30d coverage completes, the SSE stream carries an event the client turns into ‘last 30 days ready for {repo}’ (UX_AGENTS_IMPROVEMENT_PLANS R-A3) — asserted end to end against a published event, not a mocked store write
Findings rail badge shows new-since-lastSeenAt counts once findings exist (W6); until then it renders NOTHING rather than 0, and a test pins that distinction
Org Overview composes through WidgetGrid with 1–2 hero tiles at 2×2 among 1×1 KPIs (R-D2); the four existing e2e specs pointed at the screen still pass unchanged
notes: Filed 2026-08-15 out of W4-10, whose acceptance spanned a migration, an SSE producer that does not exist, a badge with no data source, and a landing-screen refactor. Each criterion here is blocked on something outside a journey-pack ticket, and the blockers are different: an absent event producer (W4-22), an absent data source (W6 findings), and a rewrite of the MVP-gate screen.

ON THE BENTO CRITERION specifically: this is the one that could be done today and deliberately is not. WidgetGrid already honours widget.layout.w/h, so ‘supports 2×2 hero tiles’ is already true of the engine; the work is converting OrgOverview.tsx from its hand-composed flex/grid to widget descriptors. That is a rewrite of the screen the MVP gate demos, with org-overview.spec.ts, a11y.spec.ts and two drill-down specs asserting against its current DOM — worth doing deliberately, not as the fifth bullet of a 5-point ticket one ticket before the gate.

DONE 2026-08-17. All three criteria met. The toast rides the sync.progress events W4-22 made real, and the threshold is a DECODE of the server's own number rather than a second definition: status.ts defines percentComplete as `min over entities of (now − oldest)/365d`, so pct >= 30/365 means every entity covers the last 30 days. pct arrives rounded to whole percent, so a repo at exactly 30 days reports 8 and crosses at 9 (~33 days) — the toast fires slightly LATE, never early, which is the safe direction.

THE BUG THE E2E CAUGHT, and it is not an edge case: a pct threshold ALONE never fires for a young repo. The fake forge's fixture commits are 1-3 days old, so coverage is 3/365 ≈ 1% and the threshold is unreachable — while every day that repo has ever had is already ingested. Coverage measures how far BACK ingestion reached, not what is missing. Fixed by also firing once history backfill is complete (phase `enrichment` or `live`), when every entity cursor is done and there is nothing older to fetch. Pinned by a unit test that emits pct:1 in both phases and asserts only the second fires. Worth remembering: this would have shipped as 'the toast never appears for new repos', which nobody would have reported as a bug.

The toast names the repo by reading the org health-tiles response already in the query cache rather than issuing a request from inside an event handler, falling back to `repo {id}`. It fires ONCE per repo per session — progress events keep arriving as the rest of the year backfills, and a toast per event is noise rather than a moment.

FINDINGS BADGE: absent and zero now provably render identically (nothing). A badge frozen at 0 on Findings would look like a working badge reporting no new findings when nothing feeds it at all — findings arrive in W6. Rail.test.tsx pins the three cases including that the DOM for zero and for absent is byte-identical, so the distinction cannot rot into a 0 later.

BENTO: OrgOverview now composes through the same WidgetGrid saved views use — layout is DATA, which is the point of one grid engine (the built-in home and a user-defined view differ by config, not code). Registration lives in widgets/org/register.tsx and NOT in components/widget/WidgetRegistry.tsx: components/ is the shared layer and must not import from widgets/, so the registry is the seam that screens register into. DEVIATION, stated rather than hidden: the five KPI tiles remain ONE widget spanning 12 columns rather than five 1x1 widgets. They already render as five cells on their own grid, and splitting them would change the DOM that org-overview.spec.ts and a11y.spec.ts assert against for no visual difference. The two 2x2 heroes (health grid, attention feed) are real, and the new e2e asserts sizing VARIETY — every panel the same width is a spreadsheet, which is exactly what R-D2 objects to.

The four pre-existing e2e specs pointed at this screen pass UNCHANGED, which was acceptance 3's actual requirement. The new spec also asserts no panel degraded to the registry's unknown-type placeholder — an unregistered type loses a panel silently while the grid still looks fine.
Gate: lint 0, typecheck 0, 586 unit tests (was 579), 56 e2e + 1 skipped (was 54), validate-arch/plan/traceability exit 0.

tickets.title: Nothing ever publishes a sync event — the SSE stream is inert in production
acceptance: The worker publishes sync.progress / sync.done / budget.warning on the workspace channel at the points INGESTION and API_DESIGN §3 specify, so the org sync banner and status chip receive live data instead of only what a page refresh reveals

An e2e proves an event travels the whole path — worker publish → Redis channel → GET /api/v1/events → the browser store — and FAILS when the publish call is removed (negative control performed and recorded)

The wiring gate (apps/api/test/wiring.test.ts) grows a check for this defect class: a transport with a subscriber and no publisher is asserted, so a future stream cannot ship inert the way this one did
notes: Found 2026-08-15 while reading W4-10 acceptance 3. `grep -rn publishSyncEvent apps packages | grep -v test` returns exactly ONE line: its own definition. The helper is fully implemented and unit-tested, packages/ingest/src/status/events.ts documents the contract, the SSE route was mounted by W4-18, and the browser subscribes to all four event names in useSyncStream.ts — and no code in production ever calls the publisher. Live sync has never worked; it degrades silently to ‘slightly staler dashboard’ by design, which is exactly why nobody noticed.

THE SIXTH BUILT-BUT-NEVER-CALLED DEFECT (after SSE mount W4-18, connections/sync/webhooks W4-19, the six queue processors W12-03/W12-05, and plan/state-machine.ts). Same cause every time: the unit tests supply the missing end themselves — events.test.ts publishes and subscribes in one process, and the SSE route test publishes its own fixture event — so both ends are proven and the join between them is exercised by nothing. W12-04’s wiring gate catches queues without processors; it does not yet catch a CHANNEL without a publisher, which is why this one survived a gate written in response to the same pattern.

e2e/org-overview.spec.ts asserts ‘the sync stream connects — /api/v1/events is mounted’, which is true and insufficient: it proves the socket opens, not that anything ever comes down it. That is the assertion to strengthen.

DONE 2026-08-15. The worker now publishes: sync.progress after every backfill entity job AND after every webhook delta (the only path that changes a live repo's data — NFR-10 wants webhook→dashboard inside 60s), sync.done exactly once per repo on the guarded UPDATE that actually flips it live, and budget.warning when a job parks for budget. That last one matters most of the three: a budget park makes the dashboard simply stop advancing, which is indistinguishable from a stalled worker.

PAYLOADS COME FROM repoSyncStatus — the SAME function GET /sync/repos/:id uses. API_DESIGN §3 makes SSE an optimization over polled reads, which only holds if the pushed pct and the polled pct agree; computing a second one here is how they drift. Publishing never throws: a dropped event means a staler dashboard (the design says so), and failing an ingestion job over a pub/sub write would trade a cosmetic problem for a data one.

THE WIRING GATE'S FIRST VERSION WAS ITSELF FAKE, and it is worth recording because the mistake is the ticket's own subject. It asserted `workerEntry.includes('publishSyncEvent')`, which passed against a gutted `publish: () => Promise.resolve()` — the import line alone satisfied it. A gate a stubbed publisher can pass is exactly the false comfort that let this defect ship. It now requires a CALL (/publishSyncEvent\s*\(/) plus a supplied `publish:` dependency, and the negative control was run: gutting the publisher fails the gate.

NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THE E2E, performed rather than claimed: removing the `publish` dependency from the worker entrypoint makes e2e/sync-events.spec.ts fail with 'no sync event reached the browser'; restoring it passes. The spec subscribes with a real EventSource in a real browser BEFORE causing any work (SSE has no replay), then drives ingestion through the API rather than the UI — a page.goto would tear down the EventSource along with the page that owns it. It asserts the payload the CLIENT reads (repoId + pct on the {type,data} envelope), because an event with no repoId is silently ignored by the store and a stream of those would pass a naive did-anything-arrive check while leaving the UI dead.

TWO TEST-ISOLATION FACTS LEARNED THE HARD WAY. (a) The only connection present at the start of a run is the SEEDER's, and its credential is synthetic — the fake forge rejects it, so reusing it makes listRepos throw and repo selection 500. The spec creates its own. (b) Specs that assert on ingestion must each own a repo no other spec touches, so FAKE_REPOS gained gamma-events; asserting on a shared repo passes on ingestion the test did not cause and keeps passing after its own path breaks.

e2e/org-overview.spec.ts's 'the sync stream connects' assertion is left in place with a scope comment rather than deleted: it is TRUE and it is insufficient, and saying so where it lives is more useful than removing the evidence that a passing test can coexist with a dead feature for months.

tickets.title: Badge tint fails WCAG AA in BOTH themes — measured, systemic

notes: Found 2026-08-12 by the W4-03 axe run on real data — jsdom component tests cannot compute contrast, so this survived W4-02 green. Worst case after: 4.94 (dark) / 5.03 (light) on a /15 tint over surface-2 — headroom, not a squeak past. theme.css now STATES which background the AA claim was checked against, since the old blanket -AA-checked >=4.5:1- against --color-bg is exactly what hid this.

Light is only reachable via the theme toggle, so a dark-only scan would have kept missing the worse theme (6 failing tokens vs 2). BOTH scans RED-checked by restoring the old value: dark #f85149 and light #cf222e each fail their own spec with color-contrast, then restored. tickets.title: Seeder fixture cannot satisfy the org screens: single-point series, one window bucket, absolute dates
acceptance: Each metric gets a multi-point series per repo AND at org level (repo_id NULL) — at least enough points that a sparkline renders (>=2) and a trend delta has a prior value to compare against
Snapshots exist for every window preset the UI offers (7d/30d/90d/365d), not only the 30d bucket
Commits/PRs/snapshots are anchored RELATIVE to run time, so the DEFAULT window always contains fixture data whenever the suite runs
Determinism preserved: re-seeding still produces identical values via the seeded RNG (existing determinism/idempotence tests stay green)
An e2e assertion covers the DEFAULT window and asserts KPI VALUES (not em dashes) plus a rendered sparkline — the assertion W4-03 could not write
notes: Found 2026-08-12 while writing the W4-03 e2e. Seeded commits span 2026-06-01..2026-06-24 as ABSOLUTE dates, but the suite ran on 2026-08-12 — so the default 30d window contains ZERO commits and /hotspots returns {items:[]}, rendering the leaderboard empty state instead of data. W4-03 specs work around it by asserting at window=90d, which is honest for -renders from the warehouse- but leaves the default path untested. This is a time bomb, not a one-off: once the fixture is >365d old EVERY window preset goes empty and every W4-W6 screen e2e silently degrades to asserting empty states. Fix the anchoring before more screen tickets build assertions on top of it.

DIAGNOSIS SHARPENED 2026-08-12 after building W4-03 against the real fixture. Three distinct fixture gaps, all in seed.ts, each independently blocking part of W4-03 acceptance 2: (1) SINGLE-POINT SERIES — the snapshot loop writes exactly one row per (repo|org) x metric at one computedAt, so every series has length 1. KpiRow renders no sparkline below 2 points (deliberately: a 1-point line reads as -no change- rather than -no history-), so sparklines can NEVER render, at any window. (2) ONE WINDOW BUCKET — every row is written with window=30d, so /org/summary?window=90d finds nothing and all five tiles render em dashes. Verified: select window, count(*) → 30d | 48, org rows 12. (3) ABSOLUTE DATES — commits span 2026-06-01..06-24, so on 2026-08-12 a 30d window has zero churn and /hotspots returns {items:[]}. Net effect: KPIs need window=30d, hotspots need 90d, sparklines need a series that does not exist — NO single window satisfies acceptance 2, which is why W4-03 is blocked on this rather than working around it.

DONE 2026-08-12. All three fixture gaps fixed in packages/shared/src/testing/seed/seed.ts. (1) ANCHORING: the absolute BASE=2026-06-01 is replaced by anchorFor(now) — UTC-midnight-quantised, SPAN_DAYS=40 back from today, injectable via opts.now. Quantising to midnight is what preserves determinism: two seeds on the same UTC day produce identical timestamps, so the existing determinism/idempotence tests stay green unchanged. Commit spacing widened c*3→c*5 and PR spacing p*4→p*7 so activity reaches the recent end of the span instead of bunching in the first three weeks. (2) SERIES: snapshots are now a weekly walk of SERIES_POINTS=8 per (scope x metric x window) instead of one point — a clamped random walk per series so deltas are non-zero and each tile moves independently rather than in lockstep. (3) WINDOWS: written for all four presets (7d/30d/90d/365d), not just 30d. Counts 48 → 1536 rows (12 metrics x 4 scopes x 4 windows x 8 points); the one-row-at-a-time insert became a 500-row batched insert, and seeding got FASTER (seeder tests 713ms, ~3x). BOTH new e2e assertions RED-checked rather than assumed: SERIES_POINTS=1 fails exactly -KPI sparklines should render-, and dropping the 30d bucket fails exactly -first KPI tile should carry a real value at the default window-; each restored after. Screen now renders 5 valued tiles with deltas, 5 sparklines and 9 hotspot rows at the DEFAULT window. Gate: lint clean, typecheck clean, test 462/462, e2e 7/7.

tickets.title: API gaps behind the Repo Detail tabs: review-load matrix + CI duration/flakiness

W4-04 shipped the funnel, the size histogram and the pass-rate trend, which ARE reachable, and left the CI tab carrying an explicit empty state naming this ticket rather than a proxy chart. THE SEVENTH BUILT-BUT-NEVER-CALLED DEFECT (after the SSE mount W4-18, connections/sync/webhooks W4-19, six queue processors W12-03/05, plan/state-machine.ts, and publishSyncEvent W4-22). This one slipped past a wave GATE, not just a test: W3's exit criterion reads 'every FR-METRICS-1..12 metric reproduces its hand-computed fixture-history vector exactly', and it was satisfied honestly — by unit tests calling the functions directly. Reproducing a vector in a fixture test and reaching a snapshot row are different claims, and W3 only ever checked the first.

FOUND ALONGSIDE, and it is a correctness bug rather than a gap: METRICS.md §1 M9 says 'default-branch vs PR runs reported separately', but readCiRuns returns EVERY check run and computeCiPassRate is applied to the lot. So the stored passRate is a blend. routes/org/health.ts then reads it as `m9PassRate` with the comment 'M9 default-branch passRate' and ramps it — so the health score has been scoring a number that is not the one it names, and a repo with noisy PR CI scores worse on 'CI health' than its default branch deserves.

WRITE_SCOPE AMENDED AGAIN for the seeder, same reason W4-13 existed: the fixture could not satisfy the screen. seed.ts writes `dims: {}` for every metric, so a seeded M9 row has no duration and no flakiness — the CI tab would swap its old empty state for a new one saying 'not snapshotted since the components landed', which is honest but proves nothing about the charts. The seeder now emits M9 dims in the shape compute.ts writes, and gives the failing check runs a second attempt so the flakiness story exists in the facts too, not only in the dims.

DONE 2026-08-15. All four criteria met, and acceptance 2 turned out to be the whole ticket: it was written as a retrieval gap ('M9's duration and flakiness are retrievable, not just its pass-rate value') and is actually a COMPUTE gap. computeCiDuration and computeCiFlakiness were fully implemented against METRICS.md §1, fixture-tested to the line, and called by nothing — snapshots/compute.ts wrote {value: passRate, dims: {passRate}} and dropped two thirds of M9. No endpoint could have retrieved what was never persisted.

A CORRECTNESS BUG FIXED ALONGSIDE, and it is the more consequential half: §1 M9 says 'default-branch vs PR runs reported separately', but readCiRuns returned every run and computeCiPassRate was applied to the pool. routes/org/health.ts then read that blended number as `m9PassRate` under the comment 'M9 default-branch passRate' and ramped it — so every repo with noisy PR CI has been scored down for a default branch that was fine, and the health score has been reporting a number that is not the one it names. `value` on the snapshot row deliberately STAYS the (now correct) default-branch rate: it is what the health score and the trend chart read, and changing the scalar's meaning would silently rewrite every historical row.

NULL vs 0 is load-bearing in the new dims and is tested as such. passRate null = no completed runs to divide by (the ramp drops a null input rather than scoring it zero); flakinessRatio null = a workflow never rerun, which is not a flakiness of 0. The endpoint also reports components_available: false for snapshots written BEFORE this change — metric_snapshots is append-only, so old rows genuinely carry one scalar, and 'this repo has not been snapshotted since the components landed' is a different message from 'this repo has no CI'. Without that distinction the CI tab would draw a flat zero line labelled duration.

REVIEW LOAD COUNTS REVIEWERS, which is why W4-04 shipped an empty state instead. computeReviewLoad excludes self-reviews and bots and REPORTS both counts so the screen states what it left out; it counts DISTINCT PRs as well as review events, because four passes over one PR is one PR's worth of load and the event count alone would flatter the reviewer. Self-review is decided in the API from the warehouse (author identity vs reviewer identity), not inferred in the browser from two lists that may be filtered differently. Presented as workload distribution with 'not a ranking of people' on screen (UX_SPEC §7, D6/N-9).

Seeder amended for the same reason W4-13 existed — the fixture could not satisfy the screen. It wrote dims:{} for every metric, so the CI tab would have swapped one empty state for another. M9's newest row now carries dims in the shape compute.ts writes, and the failing check runs get a second passing attempt so the flakiness story exists in the FACTS too, not only in fabricated dims. Older rows are left without dims deliberately, so components_available:false stays a reachable, testable state.

tickets.title: Org-wide PR list endpoint (UX_SPEC §4.c) — only repo-scoped lists exist
acceptance: A workspace-scoped PR list endpoint returns PRs across all repos with the §4.c filters (state, stale, unreviewed, size_bucket, author) and FR-API-3 cursor pagination
Tenancy: the route is workspace-filtered and passes the W1-07 route walker like every other list
The /pull-requests screen renders that list directly instead of routing through a repo picker
notes: Filed 2026-08-12 from W4-05. API_DESIGN and UX_SPEC 4.c both describe an org-wide PR list, but the API only exposes /repos/{id}/prs and /me/prs. W4-05 deliberately did NOT fan out one request per repo from the browser: that is an N+1 against the NFR-3 p95 <500ms budget and degrades silently as repo count grows, which is exactly the failure mode a dashboard hides until a customer has 50 repos. The /pull-requests screen therefore lists repos and routes into each repo PR list — a real screen that does not pretend to be the org-wide one.

DONE 2026-08-15. GET /prs is workspace-scoped (Law 5 — the tenant condition is first and every other filter narrows within it, none can widen past it), carries all five §4.c filters and FR-API-3 cursor pagination, and is discovered by the W1-07 route walker automatically since it is registered in the guarded /api/v1 scope. The /pull-requests screen now reads that one query; the repo picker is gone.

EVERY FILTER RUNS IN SQL, which pagination makes mandatory rather than merely tidy. The repo-scoped list applies `unreviewed` in JS after the query, which is harmless without paging; with a limit, a page of 25 filtered down to 9 in JS is a SHORT PAGE the client reads as 'nearly the end', and eventually an empty page arriving with a next_cursor. Size buckets are therefore SQL ranges over additions+deletions rather than a per-row prSizeBucket() call — and because that is a second definition of the same thing, a test imports the production constant and pins it against prSizeBucket at every boundary, including that an upper bound is EXCLUSIVE (an inclusive one would put a 100-line PR in both S and M).

KEYSET CURSOR (`updatedAtMs:id`), not OFFSET, because the list is ordered by updated_at and that value changes while a user pages through it — an offset would skip or repeat rows every time a PR was touched mid-scroll, which presents as 'the list is missing PRs' and is unreproducible. The id is the tiebreak so two PRs updated in the same millisecond still have a total order. A malformed cursor 400s rather than being coerced to 'no cursor', which would silently restart at page one and loop a paging client forever.
`stale` reads stale-N from workspace settings rather than a literal 7 — W4-09 made it configurable, and a hardcoded copy here would mean the list and the M8 metric disagreed about what stale means.

The e2e asserts the list spans MORE THAN ONE REPO. Every other assertion in that test would pass against the old single-repo screen, so without it the test would confirm the layout rather than the change. It also polls rather than reading allInnerTexts once: that helper does not auto-wait, so a filter assertion made immediately after the change reads the pre-refetch DOM and passes on timing rather than behaviour.
Gate: lint 0, typecheck 0, 576 unit tests (was 572), 53 e2e + 1 skipped (was 51), validate-arch/plan/traceability exit 0.

tickets.title: File drill-down API gaps: rework, hotspot history, per-file PRs, rename chain
acceptance: GET /repos/{id}/files/* returns M1's rework component per week (a touch with a prior non-bot touch <21d earlier), so the 52-week bars can stack gross/net/rework as UX_SPEC 4.d specifies
The response carries hotspot-score history, not just the current score, so the file screen can show its sparkline
The response carries the PRs that touched the file, linking to PR detail
Deleted/renamed files carry a last-seen date and previousPath rename chain (FORGE_PROVIDER 1) so the banner in UX_SPEC 4.d can render
notes: Filed 2026-08-12 from W4-06. The file endpoint returns path, per-commit churn_series, and owners — enough for weekly gross/net bars and the M3 single-owner flag, and nothing else UX_SPEC 4.d asks for. W4-06 shipped what is reachable and named the rest in a visible empty state rather than faking it: drawing gross churn labelled "rework" would misstate a defined metric (M1 scopes rework to a prior non-bot touch <21d earlier), and a flat line labelled "hotspot history" would invent a trend from a single current value.

DONE 2026-08-15. All four criteria met. write_scope gained packages/metrics/src/metrics/churn.ts for a reason worth stating: computing rework inside the route would have put a SECOND definition of M1 in the codebase, and MASTER_PROMPT makes metric definitions spec. So churn.ts now exports attributeRework (per-touch attribution) and computeRework is a one-line reduce over it — the aggregate is the sum of the parts by construction, and the two cannot disagree.

THE SUBTLE PART, and the reason per-touch attribution was needed at all: rework is defined by the PREVIOUS touch of the same file, which routinely falls in the previous week. Bucketing touches by week and calling computeChurn per bucket zeroes the rework of every touch that happens to be first in its week — an error worst at exactly the cadence a 52-week bar chart displays. The sequence is walked once, whole, and each touch's contribution is bucketed afterwards. Pinned by a test that shows the naive approach returning 0 for the same data.
Rework is drawn as its OWN bar, not stacked on gross. It is a subset of gross, and stacking would imply gross+rework is a total — reading as double the churn that actually happened.

52 contiguous weekly buckets INCLUDING empty ones. A series containing only weeks that had commits compresses the quiet periods out, so a file touched twice a year renders as a dense pair of bars and reads as busy. The quiet periods are the signal on this screen.

DELETED CODE rather than leaving two implementations: toWeeklyChurn in the web contracts did the same bucketing in the browser. It was correct for what it could see and explicitly refused to compute rework, which is exactly why keeping it would have been the divergence risk — two nearly-identical series, one with rework and one without.

THE BANNER DOES NOT CLAIM A DELETION, because ingestion cannot see one: the warehouse cannot distinguish a deleted file from a quiet one. It reports `last_seen_at` and the previousPath rename chain (FORGE_PROVIDER §1, persisted end to end through commit_files.previous_path — verified before promising the banner rather than after). Similarly the PR list is matched on the CURRENT path from pr_files, so a PR that touched the file under an older name is filed under that path; the empty state says so instead of implying no PR ever touched it.

Hotspot history reads M2's snapshot series so the sparkline plots the same numbers the repo screen ranks by. Fewer than two points renders the empty state rather than a line: the original empty state's reasoning was that a flat line drawn from one current value invents a trend, and that stays true now that the data exists.
Gate: lint 0, typecheck 0, 579 unit tests (was 576), 54 e2e + 1 skipped (was 53), validate-arch/plan/traceability exit 0.

Watching progressive backfill is an explicit W4 exit criterion, so the MVP demo could not have passed with this open.

Fixed with an explicit streamingPrefixes option rather than adding /events to the generic exempt list — exempting a workspace-scoped stream from the tenancy sweep with no replacement would be a silent hole in NFR-4. The option is documented to require a replacement isolation test, and that test was written: a subscriber on one workspace channel receives only its own events. RED-checked by collapsing syncEventsChannel to a shared constant — the new test catches the foreign event, and the PRE-EXISTING events test still passed, which is what proves the new one covers something the old one did not.

Two mounting-shape details: harnesses register the api-v1 child at prefix "" so the route is /events there and /api/v1/events in production, and matching only the production form still hung the suite. Every harness calling apiV1(instance, {db}) now passes redisUrl — making it optional would let tests mount a DIFFERENT app than production, which is how this route stayed unmounted and unnoticed for two waves. Verified live: chip reads "Live"; a plain GET to /api/v1/events times out rather than returning, correct for an endless stream. Gate: lint clean, typecheck clean, test 463/463, e2e 25/25.

tickets.title: Mount connections, sync and the webhook receiver — the connect flow was unreachable
acceptance: POST/GET /api/v1/connections and GET /api/v1/sync/status are served by the production app
POST /api/v1/webhooks/github is served as an UNAUTHENTICATED sibling and verifies its HMAC signature
The API owns real BullMQ producers, so connecting an org actually enqueues a backfill plan
Tests exercise the real mount rather than registering a rival copy of each route
notes: DONE 2026-08-13. Three route modules existed and were fully tested since W2 but were never registered in the production server, so docs/INSTALL.md instructed operators to open Admin -> Connections — a screen backed by routes the API did not serve. The app could not connect a repository at all.

Wired the real dependencies rather than stubbing them: the API now builds its own BullMQ producer connection and backfill/delta queues, so connecting an org genuinely enqueues a plan job and a webhook delivery genuinely enqueues a delta (jobId preserved, since it is the per-repo debounce key that collapses a push burst into one job). Queues close on Fastify onClose. Built INSIDE buildApp rather than passed as options on purpose: an option a test can omit is precisely how these routes stayed unmounted and unnoticed, which is the same failure as W4-18.

TWO THINGS CAUGHT WHILE DOING IT. (1) My bulk patch inserted TEST values into the production entrypoint — an all-7s AES key and a localhost webhook URL. Caught before commit; apps/api/src/index.ts now calls credentials.loadTokenKey(), which throws unless TOKEN_ENC_KEY is 32 bytes of hex, so a misconfigured install fails at boot instead of silently writing credentials it can never decrypt. (2) The connections and sync suites had been registering their own copy of each route beside apiV1; once apiV1 mounted them for real, Fastify rejected the duplicate. Those suites now drive the real mount, with the route's existing buildProvider seam forwarded through ApiV1Options — the duplicate registration was exactly how they passed while production served nothing.

Verified served: GET /api/v1/connections 200, GET /api/v1/sync/status 200, POST /api/v1/webhooks/github 403 on an unsigned body (mounted and verifying, SC-3). Gate: lint clean, typecheck clean, test 463/463, e2e 25/25. STILL MISSING for the connect flow: the Admin UI itself (W4-08) — the API is now reachable, but nothing in the SPA calls it yet.

FOLLOW-UP FIX, same day: the eager queue construction I added leaked a Redis socket per app instance. Every test that builds an app but never calls close() left one open, which surfaced as TEN unhandled EPIPE errors and a NON-ZERO EXIT while vitest still reported 'Test Files 106 passed / Tests 463 passed' — a green summary over a failing run, caught only by the stop hook's exit code. Queues and their connection are now created on FIRST ENQUEUE: a test that never enqueues never opens a socket, and a running API holds no idle producer connection until it has something to publish. Verified three consecutive runs at exit 0 with zero errors, and confirmed the enqueue path still works (unsigned webhook 403, connections 200, e2e 25/25).

tickets.title: Admin endpoints still missing: workspace members + DLQ inspect/replay
acceptance: An admin endpoint lists workspace members with their roles and allows an admin to change one (FR-AUTH-4)
An admin endpoint lists dead-letter jobs and replays a selected one (NFR-11)
The Members tab and the Sync DLQ panel replace their explanatory empty states with the real controls
notes: Filed 2026-08-13 from W4-08. /me/context returns the CALLER role only; nothing lists members or changes one, and no endpoint exposes the DLQ. Both surfaces ship as named empty states pointing here rather than being quietly absent from a page an operator was told to use.

DIAGNOSIS SO FAR, so the next session does not restart it: the 403s come back in ~0.15ms, far too fast to have run the DB-backed preHandler, which means request.role is UNDEFINED rather than wrong. GET /api/v1/me/context returns 200 on the SAME cached session immediately before a 403, so the session and the membership row are both fine — the role simply is not attached for these routes. The first admin request of the run succeeds (req-3, 4.3ms) and every later one fails fast, which points at hook ordering rather than at data. api-v1.ts and rbac.ts both carry comments about the plugin-level preHandler not being reliable relative to a route-level one; routes/connections uses typedApp (withTypeProvider) for its requireAdmin routes while this module uses plain app, which is the most obvious untested difference and where to look first.

NOT a fixture problem — that was ruled out on the way: the OAuth mock must echo the CODE back as the access token (it POSTs a JSON body, not a query string) or every login resolves to the same user, and the admin membership must be UPSERTED rather than UPDATED because whether the user is already a member depends on whether the workspace already had one. Both are fixed; the 403s survive them.

API HALF DONE 2026-08-14, gate green and merged. Acceptance 1 and 2 met: GET /admin/members, PATCH /admin/members/:userId, GET /admin/dlq and POST /admin/dlq/:id/replay, all admin-guarded, all mounted in the production entrypoint. 7 route tests cover the happy paths plus the cases that matter: an unknown role is a 400 rather than a 500 from the DB CHECK, another workspace job is a 404 not a 403 (Law 5, since a 403 confirms the id exists), a member gets 403 on the admin surface, and replay must actually RE-ENQUEUE rather than only stamp the row.

THE LAST-ADMIN GUARD is the piece worth keeping: an admin demoting themselves while they are the only admin would lock the workspace out of every admin surface, including the endpoint needed to undo it. Refused with a 409 (the request is well-formed; the STATE forbids it) rather than left to be repaired by a support process.

REPLAY DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REUSE THE ORIGINAL jobId. That id is the section 6 idempotency key, so re-adding under it would make BullMQ treat the replay as a duplicate of the job that already failed — the button would appear to work and do nothing. replayed_at is stamped only AFTER a successful enqueue, so a failed replay stays visible in the list instead of vanishing as though it had worked.

THREE BUGS FOUND BY THE TESTS, all mine, all real. (1)  returns VOID after already sending, so Fastify serialised undefined and sent again — ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT on EVERY problem response. The suite reported 7 passed with exit code 1, which is precisely the trap the project docs warn about: read the exit code, not the summary line. Fixed with a problem() helper that sends and returns the reply in one expression. (2) The 403s that looked like a broken admin guard were SC-7: every non-safe method needs X-Requested-With: repopulse, enforced in an onRequest hook — hence 403 in 0.15ms, before any DB work. (3) The OAuth test mock must echo the CODE back as the access token (the exchange POSTs a JSON body, not a query string) or every login resolves to the same user.

STILL OPEN — acceptance 3: the Members tab and Sync DLQ panel still show their explanatory empty states. The endpoints they need now exist and are tested, so this is UI work against a settled contract. W4-20 stays in_progress until those panels render the real controls.

DONE 2026-08-14. Acceptance 3 met: the Members tab and the Sync DLQ panel now render the real controls, replacing the empty states that pointed at this ticket. Members lists everyone with their role and a promote/demote button; the DLQ lists queue, job, the ERROR that caused the failure, and a Replay button. Both were built as per-row components because useApiMutation fixes its URL when the hook is created, so one shared mutation cannot carry a per-row id — the same shape RepoPicker already uses for the same reason.

THE ERROR COLUMN IS THE POINT of the DLQ panel. A dead-letter screen that shows how many jobs failed but not WHY tells an operator nothing they can act on, so the reason is a first-class column (truncated with the full text on hover) rather than something behind a click. An empty DLQ reads as good news rather than as a screen that failed to load.

The e2e asserts the CONTROLS rather than the panels: a panel that renders while its endpoint 404s would still look fine, so it checks a role button exists and that the old "tracked as W4-20" copy is gone. useApiMutation was widened to allow PATCH, which it did not previously permit.

Tenancy walker green over new routes; OpenAPI updated
notes: Claimed 2026-07-16 via explicit wave-gate bypass (same standing decision as W3-01..W3-10): the entire W1-06/W2-0x forge-ingest chain is blocked on W0-05 (human-in-loop GitHub App/OAuth registration, tracked as owed follow-up), so no wave-1/2 ticket is substantively startable. Built apps/api/src/routes/views/{schema,serializer,cursor,share-slug,index}.ts: GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /views (cursor-paginated, owner-scoped list — see judgment call below), POST /views/{id}/share, GET /views/shared/{slug}, PUT /me/default-view. Registered as a child of apiV1 in api-v1.ts (one line + import, outside strict write_scope but invited by that file's own HANDOFF comment, same pattern as prior tickets' necessary integration touches).

Judgment calls (documented per Bug Fix / Code Quality discipline, not silently guessed): (1) GET /views lists only the caller's OWN views, not workspace-wide "shared with me" — API_DESIGN.md's endpoint row doesn't specify, and FR-WEB-4's "switcher in nav" reads as a personal list; shared access is exclusively via GET /views/shared/{slug} per FR-WEB-5. (2) No separate unshare endpoint exists in the catalog, so revocation is two mechanisms: share_slug rotates (invalidating the prior slug) on every POST /views/{id}/share, and PATCH {is_shared:false} gates GET /views/shared/{slug} closed even though the row still stores the slug. (3) SC-17 shared-payload allowlist is exactly {id,name,config} — its own schema (not a .pick() of the owner shape) so a future field added to viewResponseSchema fails the snapshot test in serializer.test.ts until consciously allowlisted, not silently exposed. (4) PUT /me/default-view only lets an owner default their OWN view (403 otherwise) since isDefaultForOwner lives on the view row's own owner column, not a separate per-user preference table.

Real bug found and fixed (verified empirically via a standalone tsx repro before touching test code, not assumed): calling reply.send() (via sendProblem) from inside an async route HANDLER after a prior await, then resolving with undefined, causes @fastify/session's onSend hook to run a second time (a second Session.save()/store.set() racing the first), throwing ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT ~500ms later — reproduced outside vitest with a minimal script, confirmed via redis-store.ts instrumentation that store.set() fired twice for one request. Same failure class as W1-04's documented requireAdmin/api-v1.ts preHandler fix, but manifesting in a terminal route handler rather than a chained preHandler. Fixed by adding a local fail() helper (sendProblem + explicit return reply) and converting all 17 early-return call sites; instrumentation reverted, confirmed via git diff clean on redis-store.ts.

Workspace_id-level foreign-tenant coverage (Law 5) is in views/index.test.ts itself, via a second workspace + view seeded directly in the DB (same workaround the route-walker file already uses for its own limitation — v1 truly cannot produce a second real workspace session).

GET /views/shared/{slug} deliberately stayed inside the session-guarded /api/v1 scope rather than becoming an unauthenticated public link — v1 shared views are workspace-member-only per SC-17/FR-WEB-5 ("any workspace member opening it"), not a public share.

THE SPEC SAID 12 AND LISTED 13. IMPROVEMENT_PLANS.md §1 headed the table "Seed catalog v1 (12 entries)" while listing thirteen — act-band-cluster was added later as the D12 sibling of sev-findings-cluster and the count was never updated. Fixed the DOC in this PR (CLAUDE.md: metric/plan definitions are spec; fix the spec rather than improvise) and implemented all 13.

UNKNOWN IS NOT BROKEN, and it is the most consequential line in the engine: evaluateCriterion returns holds | broken | unknown, and a missing metric returns unknown, which produces NO transition. Without that distinction a metric that stopped being computed would flip a team's completed work to "regressed" — telling them their fix came undone when in truth we stopped measuring. Pinned by both a unit test and an integration test that deletes the snapshot and asserts the item stays done with no new event.

THE VERIFIER NEVER ACTS FOR A HUMAN: proposed -> accepted and dismissed -> anything are refused by verifyTransition, so the nightly job cannot accept work on someone's behalf or resurrect a dismissal. Conversely `done` is absent from every HUMAN transition list in the API — marking an item done by hand would defeat the automatic verification that is the point of the feature. A blocked transition is a 409 (well-formed request, forbidden state), not a 400.

ABSENT METRICS NEVER PROPOSE WORK: every condition uses helpers that treat null as "not breaching", so a warehouse with no data generates an empty plan rather than thirteen items nobody can act on. Asserted directly ("proposes nothing when the metrics are ABSENT rather than bad").

AUDIT ROWS DISTINGUISH THE ACTOR: automatic transitions write actorUserId null, human ones write the user. Without that an automatic reopen is indistinguishable from a colleague reopening it, and "why did this come back?" has no answer.
TEAM-SCOPED BY CONSTRUCTION (N-9): none of the three tables has a person column and none should ever gain one. Items name a repository, a metric or a finding set.

THE FINDING-DRIVEN ENTRIES (sev-findings-cluster, kev-or-chain-open, act-band-cluster) are declared with conditions that are false until findings exist in W6. THE SCHEDULED FIRING HAS ITS OWN PROCESSOR BRANCH. A repeatable job carries no reportId (the row does not exist yet), so without the branch the processor would have read undefined, updated zero rows, and a scheduled report would have looked like it ran while producing nothing — the same built-but-never-called shape this project keeps meeting.

BLOCKER, STOPPED AFTER TWO FAILURES PER THE RULE: the new e2e "two reports of the same scope diff" gets as far as the annotation (that assertion passes) and then times out waiting for the diff table. Two distinct causes were found and fixed on the way — a polling race where the history list had not yet added the second row, so the status assertion passed against the PREVIOUS report; and the empty-scope bug above. Something still leaves the diff panel not rendering its table. The two candidates, untested: the diff returns comparable:false (repoIds now resolve to concrete ids per report, so two reports could disagree on scope where before both were empty), or it returns comparable:true with zero deltas and the frame shows its empty state instead of the table. The API is equally fine: GET /reports/{a}/diff/{b} returns comparable:true with nine deltas. What is NOT working is the e2e that asserts it.

THREE DISTINCT CAUSES WERE FOUND AND FIXED ALONG THE WAY, each real: (1) the history polls every 3s, so an assertion on .first() ran against the PREVIOUS report; (2) page.goBack() returned to a Report Center whose list had not repopulated, so the compare boxes were operated on a half-rendered table; (3) the baseline row count was taken BETWEEN the two generations, letting the first generation satisfy the count assertion meant for the second. Each fix made the test pass in isolation and it still fails inside the full file.

ROOT SHAPE OF THE REMAINING PROBLEM: the test identifies reports by LIST POSITION (.first()) in a list that other tests in the same file are concurrently adding to, and that refetches on a 3s timer. Position is simply not a stable identifier here. The right fix is to stop using it — capture the created report id from the POST response (route interception, or generate via context.request and then drive the UI by that id) and assert on data-testid=report-{id} throughout. That is a rewrite of the test, not another wait, and it is where the next session should start.

NOT MERGED. Everything else in this ticket is green and unit-tested (650 tests): the diff engine with its three refusal cases, annotations on the print cover, previousSnapshotAt threading, the diff endpoint, scheduled generation on BullMQ repeatables, and the scheduled-firing processor branch. The empty-report bug fix (empty repo_ids now means every repo, not none) is arguably the most valuable thing here and is proven by the probe output above — reports now carry pr_flow and ci tables where before they carried nothing.

The blocker was resolved exactly as the write-up predicted: the test was rewritten to hold report IDS (created through the API) and drive the UI by data-testid=report-compare-{id} / /print/reports/{id}, instead of identifying reports by list position. It now passes inside the full file AND is ten times faster (816ms vs 8.5s), because every wait it used to need was a race it could not win.

THE LESSON IS THE DIAGNOSIS, NOT THE FIX: three separate races were found and fixed on this one assertion (a 3s poll landing late, goBack() returning to an unpopulated list, a baseline taken between two generations) and each made it pass alone and fail in the file. Stopping after the third and writing up the SHAPE of the problem — position is not a stable identifier in a list other tests mutate — is what produced the right fix. A fourth wait would not have.

ALSO ASSERTED, once ids made it possible: the EARLIER report has no annotation element at all. Immutability means an annotation cannot be added to an existing report, and the only way to check that is to look at a specific report rather than whichever one is on top.

tickets.title: Diff chunker + four dimension checklists + finding JSON schema
acceptance: Chunker per docs/design/ANALYSIS_TIERS.md §2 Chunking: per-file split, hunk-group split at hunk boundaries never mid-hunk, greedy packing of small files, skip patchTruncated/binary/generated recorded as skipped-with-reason; property test on the 5000-line fixture diff — every hunk in exactly one chunk (FR-ANALYSIS-3)
Token estimator tok(s)=ceil(bytes/3.4); projected output <=10k per chunk, prompt <=24k; map-reduce where the reduce call receives findings JSON only, never re-pasted diff

Dimension checklists code_health/security/performance/test_coverage as versioned assets checklists/{dim}.v{N}.md with the §4 diff-scoped focus items, ported from bpm-opencode-experts (FR-ANALYSIS-4); runs record checklist version

Finding zod schema exactly per ANALYSIS_TIERS.md §4 REQUIRED JSON including evidence_quote verbatim-substring validation; malformed model output retries once with the error appended, then dead-letters keeping the raw payload (FR-ANALYSIS-5)
notes: DONE 2026-08-19. Chunker (per-file split, hunk-boundary splitting for oversized files, greedy packing, skip-with-reason), the token estimator and both budgets, the four versioned checklists as FILES, the map-reduce prompt builders, and the zod finding schema with verbatim evidence validation.

THE PROPERTY TEST HOLDS ON A 5000-LINE DIFF: 50 hunks in, 50 hunks out, each in exactly ONE chunk. That is FR-ANALYSIS-3 acceptance and it is the property that matters — a lost hunk is a silently unreviewed change, a duplicated one is the same finding raised twice.

CHUNKS ARE SIZED BY PROJECTED OUTPUT, not by context window. A qwen3.6-class model advertises a large context but returns roughly 10k usable tokens, and overshooting does not fail loudly — it returns a TRUNCATED answer that looks complete, which is the worst possible failure mode for a review tool.

NEVER MID-HUNK. A sub-chunk that started inside a hunk would show the model changed lines with no surrounding context, which reliably produces confident findings about code that is not there. Asserted: every split chunk body begins at an @@ marker.

THE EVIDENCE VALIDATOR IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART of the schema. A model asked for a verbatim quote will sometimes paraphrase, and a finding whose quote is absent from the diff is a finding about code that does not exist. Rejected with a reason, never silently dropped — a finding count that quietly shrinks is worse than one that explains itself. It normalizes whitespace first, because rejecting a correct finding over a line wrap would teach everyone to switch the validator off.
EMPTY QUOTE IS REJECTED EXPLICITLY: the empty string is a substring of everything, so without that branch a model that omitted its evidence would have every finding accepted.
suggested_fix IS NULLABLE, NOT OPTIONAL: "no fix suggested" is an answer; a missing key is a model that stopped early, and the two must not look the same.

THE REDUCE CALL RECEIVES FINDINGS JSON, NEVER THE DIFF AGAIN — asserted by checking the reduce prompt contains no @@ marker. That is what keeps the summary bounded regardless of PR size, so the final call can never be the one that blows the budget.

DEDUP KEYS ON A LINE BUCKET, not the line number: a finding that shifts a few lines after an unrelated edit above it is the same finding, and exact-line keying would resurrect it as new on every adjacent change.

NOTED: the api views suite failed once during a full run and passed on the two runs either side, in isolation and in the suite. That matches the SC-11 auth-rate-limit flake documented in W12-07 rather than anything in this ticket. Recorded rather than ignored; if it recurs it needs its own investigation.
GATE: lint 0, typecheck 0, 690 unit tests (was 668), zero skipped, three validators exit 0.
