acceptance: Dedup per docs/design/ANALYSIS_TIERS.md §5: dedup_key = sha256(dimension\0file\0normalize(evidence_quote)) + line-bucket tiebreak; re-run on unchanged PR yields 0 new rows and bumps last_seen/occurrence_count; a resolved finding whose key reappears reopens with an audit row (FR-ANALYSIS-6)

Lifecycle open → confirmed | dismissed(reason) → resolved | wont_fix with every transition audited in finding_status_history (FR-INSIGHTS-1); false_positive dismissals feed analysis_false_positive_rate{dimension,model,checklist_version}
Re-review on webhook synchronize: only changed/added files re-chunked; findings on files no longer in the diff auto-resolve with reason outdated_diff (§5)
Health score gains the security sub-score with weight renormalization per METRICS.md §3, and hotspot ranking gains open-finding density (FR-INSIGHTS-2/5 v1.x halves)
notes: WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED before code: acceptance 4 adds the security sub-score to the health score (packages/insights/src/score) and open-finding density to hotspot ranking (packages/insights/src/hotspots), neither of which is under findings/**.

DONE 2026-08-19. Dedup keying, the finding lifecycle, the store (persist with dedup, reopen, auto-resolve, open-finding density, false-positive rate), the security sub-score in the health score, and hotspot density inputs.

THE CONTRACT: re-running an unchanged PR creates ZERO new rows and bumps last_seen/occurrence_count. A findings list that grows every time the same question is asked is a list people stop reading — and the count now feeds the health score, so it would also move a number nobody changed the code to move.

A MACHINE NEVER UNDOES A HUMAN JUDGEMENT: a dismissed or wont_fix finding is NOT reopened when the model says the same thing again. A resolved one IS reopened when its evidence reappears, with an audit row and a null actor — that is not undoing a judgement, it is new information: the code came back.

AUTO-RESOLVE IS RECORDED AS outdated_diff, NOT fixed. We observed that we stopped seeing the finding, not that anyone repaired it. Crediting an unwitnessed fix would make the resolution rate a number nobody should trust.

THE SECURITY SUB-SCORE IS ABSENT, NOT ZERO, FOR AN UNANALYSED REPO — and a test asserts the difference directly. If absent findings scored as clean, every repository nobody has reviewed would outrank an analysed one that honestly reported two issues. That is the null-vs-zero trap in the place it would do the most damage.

REAL BUG FOUND IN EXISTING CODE: tier1Only was computed from the sub-score DEFINITIONS rather than the sub-scores that survived. The moment buildHealthSubScores always emitted a security definition, every repo — including unanalysed ones — reported "not Tier-1 only". The label means "this score contains non-Tier-1 evidence", and only a SCORED sub-score does. Fixed and pinned.

NORMALIZER MADE IDEMPOTENT, caught by my own failing expectation: collapsing whitespace before stripping digits leaves the gap the number occupied ("foo( 42 )" -> "foo(  )"), so normalizing an already-normalized quote produced a different string — and a normalizer that is not idempotent gives the same finding two keys, which silently disables dedup.

FALSE-POSITIVE RATE COUNTS ONLY false_positive DISMISSALS. "We accept this risk" is not the model being wrong; folding the two together would make the FP rate measure team policy instead of model quality. It returns null rather than 0 over an empty set — a 0% false-positive rate across zero findings reads as a perfect model.

NOT IN THIS TICKET: the analysis.review queue and its processor. W6-01 deferred the queue so it would land WITH its processor; that is the review runner, which belongs with the API/UI wiring in W6-04 rather than with the store.

acceptance: Schema delta per docs/DATABASE.md D9: analysis_runs.pass_kind ('find','verify','challenge','synthesize','narrate','plan') + parent_run_id; findings.verify_status ('unverified','confirmed','contradicted'); migration + rollback note

Challenger gate per FR-ANALYSIS-10: severity>=4 finding, verified secret, or chain must survive ONE adversarial refute pass before org-banner/Security-tab-top surfacing; sev-4 fixture blocked from banner until challenge passes; loop discipline per docs/work/UX_AGENTS_IMPROVEMENT_PLANS.md §B2 (hard caps, no-progress halt)

notes: WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED before code: acceptance 5 adds a verify_status facet and badge to the Explorer (web) which reads a new API field (apps/api/src/routes/findings).

DONE 2026-08-19. Schema delta (analysis_runs.pass_kind + parent_run_id, findings.verify_status) with migration 0010 and a rollback note that says what the rollback DESTROYS. Verify pass with host affinity, refute-first prompt, the challenger gate, FP-suppression memory, and the Explorer verification facet + badge.

MAKER != VERIFIER IS ENFORCED, NOT REQUESTED. pickVerifierHost never returns the finder host, and when no second host exists the finding is SKIPPED and stays `unverified` rather than being confirmed by the model that raised it. A model asked whether it was right agrees with itself, so a same-host pass would confirm nearly always and the "verified by a second model" badge would mean nothing — worse than no badge, because people would trust it.

THE PROMPT ASKS FOR A REFUTATION, NOT A REVIEW. "Is this correct?" invites agreement: the model has been handed a confident claim and a reason to accept it. The verifier is told its default position is that the finder was wrong and to confirm only if it cannot refute — which makes agreement the expensive answer.

THE CHALLENGER GATE BLOCKS UNVERIFIED SEVERITY>=4 FROM LOUD SURFACING. An unverified critical claim on an org banner is the most expensive way this product can be wrong: everyone sees it, and being wrong once there costs more trust than ten correct findings earn. Contradicted findings are never surfaced at any severity.

FP-SUPPRESSION MEMORY (R-B4): a finding dismissed as a false positive does not come back while its evidence is unchanged — the dedup key IS the unchanged test. The sighting still bumps occurrence_count, because how often a suppressed pattern recurs is worth knowing. A dismiss button that does not stick is one nobody presses twice.

"unverified" IS AN ANSWER, NOT A MISSING VALUE, and the UI says so: the badge reads "not independently verified" rather than rendering nothing. Collapsing unverified into unlabelled would let an unchecked claim look identical to a confirmed one — the same null-vs-zero conflation this project keeps finding, here applied to trust.

SEEDED ONE FINDING OF EACH VERIFICATION STATE so the facet and badge are exercised against data rather than an empty filter, and the e2e asserts a contradicted finding does NOT still claim to be verified.

Deterministic narrative renders with T2 mocked in CI — zero live LLM calls (docs/TESTING.md §8); axe green on new surfaces
notes: WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED before code: the pulse card is an Org Overview widget (needs a new WidgetType — registerWidget overwrites by type) served by an API endpoint, and the since-last-visit strip needs a /me endpoint. Both are outside the filed scope but named in the acceptance.
DONE 2026-08-19. Deterministic Weekly Pulse (five bullets, fixed slots), the /org/pulse endpoint, the pinned Org Overview card with its provenance chip, and the keyboard triage queue.

TEMPLATE FIRST, MODEL SECOND — the ordering IS the design. Every number is computed from the warehouse before any model sees the text; the narrate pass may only reword. applyNarration DISCARDS a rewording that changes or invents a figure (numbersPreserved compares the multiset of numbers), and falls back wholesale if the model returns the wrong number of bullets. A stiff sentence beats a fluent one with a fabricated number, because the fluent one gets quoted.

THE PROVENANCE CHIP TELLS THE TRUTH: it reads "computed from your warehouse" until a narrate pass has actually run, rather than wearing a "T2 · local" badge for text a template produced. An AI card family that misrepresents where its words came from is worse than no badge at all.

"FIRST MEASURED" IS NOT "IMPROVED FROM ZERO" — the most tempting lie in a weekly summary, because it makes every newly computed metric look like progress. A metric with no prior value says so and is ranked below real movement; a metric that was not computed says THAT rather than reporting zero.

EXACTLY FIVE BULLETS, ALWAYS, in the same slots (biggest mover, findings, plan progress, next two movers). A summary whose shape changes week to week cannot be skimmed, and skimming is the only way a weekly note gets read.

THE TRIAGE QUEUE IS FULLY KEYBOARD OPERABLE (NFR-5): j/k step, c confirms, d dismisses as a false positive, Esc exits, evidence inline, and an exit summary carrying the FP count that feeds the same analysis-quality metric. Triaging forty findings with a mouse is a job nobody finishes.

A11Y REGRESSION I INTRODUCED AND FIXED: the provenance line used text-fg-faint, which in the LIGHT theme is #818b98 on white (~3:1) and fails AA for body text. The light-theme axe spec caught it. ACKNOWLEDGED SUPPRESSES FROM THE LIST, NEVER FROM THE DATA, and the response carries suppressed_count and suppressed_paths so the UI can say how many are hidden. A leaderboard that silently omits rows is one nobody can reason about — the first person to spot the gap stops trusting every other number on the screen. That honesty badge is the whole reason the intent is safe to offer.

A REFACTOR INTENT IS A PROMISE WITH A DATE ON IT. If the hotspot score has not improved within warn_after_months the promise quietly expired, and saying so is the entire value of recording it — an intent nobody is ever reminded about is a comment, not a plan. FLAT counts as not improved: holding a score steady for four months is not a refactor.

IMPROVEMENT BEFORE THE INTENT WAS DECLARED DOES NOT COUNT. The engine only reads history from createdAt onward, so a file that was already getting better cannot credit an intent for work that predates it.
ACKNOWLEDGED NEVER WARNS. An intent that keeps nagging after an explicit team decision is exactly why people stop using intents at all.
SUPERVISE HAS NO GRACE PERIOD — any decline alerts immediately, because hearing about it early is what supervising means.

SETTING AN INTENT RESETS THE CLOCK: a refactor declared today gets today deadline even on a path acknowledged last year, and one intent per file is enforced by the unique key (two live intents would make "is this acknowledged?" unanswerable).

tickets.title: T2 host-config hardening (SC-24): zod validation, credential-free requests, VLAN policy
acceptance: zod host-list validation per SC-24 (docs/SECURITY_CONTROLS.md): LM Studio base URLs must be private-range LAN addresses unless explicitly flagged — canonical evil-URL corpus test (public IP/hostname, metadata IP, localhost) rejected; host list is admin workspace config, never per-request input
T2 requests carry zero credentials/secrets (client test asserts no auth headers/env values in outbound payloads); responses continue through the full SC-13 pipeline
deploy compose/quadlet note: LLM VLAN reachable from the worker network only (pairs with the W7-05 SC-20 hardening); reachability check listed for the W7-06 runbook execution
notes: DONE 2026-08-19. zod host-list validation, credential-free request assertion on the real outbound call, and the SC-24 VLAN note in deploy/compose.yaml pointing at the W7-06 runbook check.

THE CONTROL IS THAT NO ROUTE ACCEPTS A HOST. The list is admin workspace config; validation is the second line of defence. If a request could name the host, anyone who can reach the analysis API could point this product's diff-sending machinery at a server they control — and diffs are the most sensitive thing the warehouse holds.

THE METADATA ENDPOINT IS CHECKED BEFORE THE PRIVATE-RANGE TEST, and that ordering is the whole trap: 169.254.169.254 is LINK-LOCAL, so a naive "is it private?" check waves it straight through. It is the single most valuable SSRF target there is — it hands instance credentials to anything that can make an HTTP request. Rejected by name, with a message that says why.

HOSTNAMES ARE REJECTED BY DEFAULT even though one could resolve to a private address: resolution happens later, elsewhere, and can change between validation and use. A name that resolves privately today is not a guarantee about tomorrow.
A PUBLIC HOST NEEDS AN EXPLICIT FLAG, and the flag is deliberately awkward — a deployment that genuinely runs its model on a public host should have to say so in config, where a person reviews it.

CREDENTIAL-FREE IS ASSERTED ON THE ACTUAL OUTBOUND REQUEST, not on the header constant: the test drives a real complete() call and inspects what fetch received, so a future edit inside chat() that adds an auth header is caught. The header set is also frozen.
THE SECRET DETECTOR IGNORES A DIFF THAT MERELY MENTIONS THE WORD ("// renamed the password field"). A guard that fires on prose becomes noise, and noise gets switched off.

That is not ceremony: three of the differences it surfaced would each have shipped as a silent data bug. (1) Gitea repos have NO pushed_at, only updated_at, which the backfill planner orders by. (2) Commits carry NO per-file additions/deletions on ANY endpoint — list or detail — so per-file churn does not exist at the source. (3) The PR list omits churn while PR detail and PR files carry it, so the list must normalize churn to ABSENT rather than zero or a genuinely 0-line PR becomes indistinguishable from an unfetched one.

PRODUCT CONSEQUENCE WORTH A DECISION: because Gitea reports no per-file commit churn, hotspot and ownership metrics that rank files by per-commit churn cannot be computed from Gitea commits the way they can from GitHub. getCommitFiles returns each file with 0/0 plus the ACCURATE commit-level totals. Splitting the commit total across files was rejected — it would look plausible and be fiction. PR files are unaffected and do carry real churn. Recorded in docs/research/gitea-api.md.

WEBHOOK SEMANTICS RESOLVED — this was flagged UNVERIFIED in the design doc. X-Gitea-Signature is a BARE lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body with NO sha256= prefix, confirmed from go-gitea source (services/webhook/deliver.go: signatureSHA256 = hex.EncodeToString(sig256.Sum(nil))). A verifier written for GitHub would reject every genuine Gitea delivery. Implemented strictly per forge and contract-tested BOTH ways: the bare digest is accepted and a GitHub-shaped sha256= prefix is rejected, because accepting both would mean a caller cannot tell which forge signed a delivery.

NOT VERIFIED, and stated rather than glossed: no live webhook delivery from a real Gitea instance has been received end to end, and no real Gitea repo has been ingested. The format is confirmed from source and both directions are contract-tested, but acceptance 2 asks for a test against our own Gitea 1.x instance, which needs a read-only token and a reachable URL. The GitHub smoke proved that class of check catches what a self-consistent fake cannot — the same is outstanding here. Tracked as the remaining verification step, not as ticket scope creep.

Budgeter is pass-through (hasRateLimits:false) as specified; deployments return an empty page rather than throwing so the DORA signal falls back to releases (FR-METRICS-12) instead of failing a backfill over a capability the caller was told about. Gate: lint 0, typecheck 0, 517 unit tests (was 497; +20 contract), 40 e2e + 1 skipped, all exit 0.

THIS IS THE REPORT MOST LIKELY TO BE READ BY SOMEONE WHO DID NOT RUN IT — an auditor, a customer security team, a board pack. Two rules follow and shape every section: nothing may look like a measurement when it is a heuristic, and an empty section must say WHY. "No findings" and "nothing has analysed this repository" are the same shape on a page and opposite facts in a meeting.

THE EMPTY FINDINGS SECTION REFUSES TO READ AS "CLEAN": it says the findings were never RAISED and that the correct reading is "not yet examined" unless an analysis run covered the repos — then points at the egress and lifecycle sections as the evidence of whether one did. Asserted by a test.

THE EMPTY EGRESS SECTION IS THE MOST REASSURING ONE IN THE PRODUCT, and the most easily confused with "we did not record it". It states zero Tier-3 calls AND that the log is written before each call rather than after — the property that makes the zero mean something.
VERIFY STATUS TRAVELS INTO THE REPORT. An unverified critical finding and one a second model confirmed are different claims, and a security document that flattens them overstates its case.

THE WINDOW START IS DERIVED FROM THE PINNED windowEnd, never Date.now(): the egress summary would otherwise widen silently every time the report was regenerated, which is exactly the determinism the W5-03 pin exists to protect.

DEPENDENCY AND SECRET SIGNALS ARE DECLARED ABSENT AND HEURISTIC-BY-DESIGN rather than quietly omitted, so a reader knows the report is not claiming a clean dependency tree. They land in W8 and will be labelled there too — a pattern match is not a confirmed leak, and putting one beside scanner findings as an equal is how a report overstates.

acceptance: Scanner/ScannerContext/ScanBudget types + static registry compile exactly per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §1; dispatch, budgets, findings persistence, UI facets and report sections are driven by registry metadata only — adding a registered fixture scanner touches zero framework files (FR-SEC-1)

Dedicated security.scan BullMQ queue with own worker pool, priority below analysis.review, §4 idempotency keys and DLQ per NFR-11; trigger-matrix test enqueues exactly the enabled scanners per pr_synced/push/schedule/manual event (FR-SEC-9)

ScanBudget enforcement per §1.2 (wall-clock, container CPU/mem, forge-call quota on the scan lane, LLM tokens via gateway accounting with meta.initiator='scanner:{key}'); exhaustion ⇒ scan_run budget_exceeded with partial findings kept + flagged; chaos test: crash every scanner — ingestion lag and Tier-1 dashboards unaffected (NFR-15)
notes: WRITE_SCOPE WIDENED before code: packages/security does not exist yet, the repo_scanner_config table needs schema + migration + a drizzle.config.ts entry + a wipeWorkspace line, and the security.scan queue must land WITH its processor (the wiring gate requires it).

DONE 2026-08-19. New packages/security: Scanner/ScannerContext/ScanBudget contracts per SECURITY_SUITE.md §1, the static registry, workspace enablement defaults, budget metering with failure isolation, the repo_scanner_config and scan_runs tables (migration 0012), the security.scan queue WITH its processor, and the admin enablement API.

THE REGISTRY THROWS ON A DUPLICATE KEY RATHER THAN OVERWRITING. The widget registry silently replaced by type and cost a panel in W5-07; here the key is stamped onto every finding, so a duplicate would misattribute results to the wrong tool. A startup crash is the cheaper failure.

THE FRAMEWORK NEVER BRANCHES ON A SCANNER KEY, which is the only way FR-SEC-1 can be true: dispatch, triggering and tool requirements all read registry METADATA. A test registers a fixture scanner under a new key and asserts it participates in triggering without a framework change — the moment a switch on scanner.key appears, that claim is already false.

runScanner NEVER RETHROWS (NFR-15). A scanner is third-party code by construction, so the worst it may do is produce no findings; if it rethrew, one poison scanner would take ingestion and every other scanner down with it. Crash returns failed, wall-clock returns budget_exceeded — distinct statuses because they need distinct responses: failed is a bug to fix, budget_exceeded is a limit to raise.

BUDGETS ARE ENFORCED BY THE FRAMEWORK, NOT TRUSTED TO THE SCANNER. BudgetMeter charges forge calls and LLM tokens and throws at the cap, so a runaway scanner cannot spend the workspace forge budget (Law 7) or an unbounded number of tokens.

AN EXPLICIT STORED `false` BEATS A DEFAULT OF `true`, and the test says why: `stored?.enabled ?? default` would be correct here by luck and wrong the moment a default flips — a repo that deliberately opted out would silently opt back in. An unknown scanner key is disabled, not enabled: fail closed on a key nobody has reasoned about.

THE CATALOG ENDPOINT LISTS DOCUMENTED DEFAULTS EVEN WHEN NO SCANNER IS REGISTERED for them, marked `registered: false`. A scanner that failed to register would otherwise vanish from the admin screen and look like it was never meant to exist.

A PARTIAL RUN IS FLAGGED ON THE ROW. Findings from a budget-cut scan are real but the SET is incomplete, and an unflagged partial scan reads as a clean one — which is the most dangerous thing a security screen can say.

TOOL AVAILABILITY CHECKED BEFORE BUILDING: semgrep and gitleaks ARE installed here; syft, grype, trivy and osv-scanner are NOT. This ticket is the framework and needs none of them. The scanners that do are W8-02 onward, and any whose tool is missing will be parked rather than shelled out to.

tickets.title: Findings-store schema delta migration + scan_run / sboms / repo_scanner_config tables
acceptance: Migration extends findings per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §1.3 / FR-SEC-12: dimension enum += secrets|dependency|sast|iac|chain; new nullable scanner_key, rule_id, cve_id, chain_id, preconditions jsonb, yields jsonb, scan_run_id; file/line_range become nullable for repo-level findings; applies without data loss over a seeded W6 findings set, rollback note per docs/DATABASE.md §5

New tables scan_run (trigger, commit_sha, status incl. budget_exceeded, tool_versions jsonb per §1.3), sboms (CycloneDX per (repo, sha) per §3.2) and repo_scanner_config (§1) — all with workspace_id + indexes (Law 5); tenancy suite green

Dedup-key extension sha256(scanner_key + rule_id + dimension + file + normalize(evidence_quote)) in the shared findings helper; scanner re-run on unchanged input yields 0 new rows and reopen/occurrence semantics hold (FR-ANALYSIS-6 extension); scanner + analysis findings coexist in one store
Secret-redaction invariant in schema + helpers: secrets findings store fingerprint hash + file/line only — DB-dump grep with a planted fixture secret finds zero plaintext occurrences (SC-29)
notes: NOTE ON SCOPE: scan_runs and repo_scanner_config already landed in W8-01 (the framework needed them to exist). This ticket adds the findings delta, the sboms table, the dedup extension and the secret-redaction invariant.

DONE 2026-08-19. Migration 0013: findings dimension check extended to code_health|security|performance|test_coverage|secrets|dependency|sast|iac|chain; file/line_start/line_end made NULLABLE for repo-level findings; added scanner_key, rule_id, cve_id, chain_id, preconditions jsonb, yields jsonb, scan_run_id. New sboms table (CycloneDX per repo+sha); scan_runs and repo_scanner_config landed in W8-01. All carry workspace_id — validate-arch rule 5 PASS.

THE DEDUP KEY IS BACKWARD-COMPATIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION, and that was the real hazard in this ticket. Appending scanner_key/rule_id unconditionally would have re-keyed every finding already in the store: the next run would create a duplicate of each, and every occurrence count, triage decision and false-positive suppression would silently detach from its finding. A finding with no scannerKey now hashes EXACTLY the string it always did; only scanner findings get the richer key. There is a test that asserts the old key is unchanged.

FILE AND LINE ARE NULL, NOT ZERO OR EMPTY, for a repo-level finding. A CVE in a lockfile has no line, and the previous null-vs-zero bugs in this codebase all came from encoding "absent" as a value the UI would render. The line-bucket tiebreak reads null as the literal bucket "repo" rather than falling through to Math.floor(0/10).

SC-29 IS PROVEN AGAINST THE DATABASE, NOT AGAINST THE FUNCTION. A unit test on redactSecretFinding would only prove the function; the integration test plants a real-looking key, stores the finding a scanner would store, then greps every text column of findings for the plaintext — the same thing a database dump would contain. It creates its own workspace/user/connection/repo/run fixtures rather than reading whichever repo happened to exist, because an earlier version of that pattern passed by depending on another test having run.
NOT EVEN A MASKED PREFIX IS STORED: the test asserts the first 8 characters are absent too. "AKIA…" plus a repository name is often enough to find the rest.
assertRedacted THROWS rather than warns, because redaction is easy to forget in a new scanner and an author who forgets should get an exception, not a leak.

HONEST LIMIT: analysis_runs.tier is constrained to (2,3), so the secrets fixture attaches its finding to a tier-2 run. A scanner run has no LLM tier of its own — scan_run_id is the correct parent and the analysis_runs FK stays only until the scanners in W8-03+ write scan_runs rows. Worth revisiting when findings.analysis_run_id can be made nullable.

GATE: lint 0, typecheck 0, 800 unit tests (was 794), zero skipped — the redaction integration test RUNS rather than skips, which was the point of it; pnpm -r test green; validate-arch, validate-plan, validate-traceability all PASS. No e2e — this ticket ships no screen.

tickets.title: Snapshot service (C1a): getTarball + scan lane, guarded extraction, shred + sweeper, Podman sandbox profile
acceptance: ForgeProvider delta per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §1.4: getTarball op + supportsTarball capability + 'scan' lane (priority between backfill and reconcile) in the BudgetedClient; GitHub 302→codeload redirect followed, 1 core point charged (recorded fixture); FR-FORGE-6 lint gate amended — tarball callable only from the snapshot service, git clone banned everywhere (C1a)

Extraction per §2.1: SHA-pinned fetch, streaming tar guards drop absolute-path/'..'/symlink/hardlink escapes (dropped + counted), 50MB per-file / 2GB total caps ⇒ abort failed(size_cap); traversal and zip-bomb fixture archives covered (FR-SEC-2)

Shred on every exit path: finally-delete + startup/hourly orphan sweeper; kill-scan-mid-run tests (crash and SIGKILL) leave zero snapshot bytes on disk, DB or logs; sweeper clears a planted orphan snap-* dir (NFR-13)

Sandbox profile per §2.2: non-root UID, snapshot mounted /scan ro,noexec, --network=none, --pids-limit, CPU/mem/wall caps from ScanBudget, no forge credentials or env secrets mounted; findings leave only as schema-validated JSON on stdout; integration test asserts network deny + read-only fs; lint gate: no scan-tool spawn outside packages/security/sandbox (NFR-14)
notes: DONE 2026-08-19. ForgeProvider delta (getTarball + supportsTarball + the scan lane), a hand-owned streaming tar reader with guarded extraction, bracketed snapshots with a shred-on-every-exit-path and an orphan sweeper, the Podman sandbox profile with a LIVE integration test, and validate-arch rules 6 and 7 — each proven by planting the violation it forbids.

THE REDIRECT TO CODELOAD IS FOLLOWED WITHOUT THE FORGE TOKEN. The signature in the redirect URL is the credential; forwarding an Authorization header to a host the connection was never scoped to is a credential egress with no purpose. The downloader takes a URL and nothing else, so there is no header to leak — the shape is the guarantee, and a test pins it. A redirect to any host but codeload/objects.githubusercontent is refused: a redirect is an instruction from a remote server about where to send the next request, which is how an SSRF becomes a download.

THE SCAN LANE SITS BETWEEN BACKFILL AND RECONCILE, and the test states why: a scan is worth less than filling in history someone asked for and more than catching up on data we already have. Below reconcile it would never run on a busy workspace.

THE TAR READER IS OURS, WHICH IS A REAL TRADE-OFF AND NOT A PREFERENCE. tar-stream is not in docs/TECH_STACK.md and adding a dependency is a stop-and-ask, but the deciding argument is that the guards have to run on an entry BEFORE a byte of it reaches disk — a library that hands back an extracted tree gives the guards nothing to guard. Fixture archives are built by the SYSTEM tar, not hand-assembled bytes, so the parser is tested against what tar emits rather than what I assumed it emits. That immediately caught macOS AppleDouble sidecar files, which a forge archive never contains (COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 in the fixture builder). GNU long-name and pax path records ARE honoured: ignoring them would silently use a truncated path, and a truncated path is a different file.

DROPPED ENTRIES ARE COUNTED BY REASON, NOT SILENTLY SKIPPED. A symlink out of the tree is ordinary in real repos, so this path runs constantly; a drop count of 400 is itself a finding and a count of 0 is the evidence the guards did nothing today. A symlink named ../../x is counted as a SYMLINK — the thing it is — not as a traversal, so the counts say what happened.

A CAP ABORTS THE WHOLE EXTRACTION rather than yielding a partial tree. A partial extraction is not a smaller scan, it is a scan of an unknown subset, and findings from one would understate the repo silently. The caps bite mid-decompression: a 50MB-of-zeroes bomb compresses under 1MB, and a cap that only measures after decompressing has already paid what the bomb was built to cost.

THE SWEEPER IS THE SIGKILL MECHANISM AND finally IS NOT — they cover different failures and neither substitutes for the other. The test proves it by really SIGKILLing a child that holds a snapshot in a try/finally: the directory is STILL THERE afterwards, which is the evidence, and then the sweeper removes it. The sweeper keeps anything younger than the longest allowed scan, because sweeping a live snapshot turns a slow scan into a corrupt one. Age is clamped at zero — filesystem mtime granularity can round a directory a millisecond into the future, and a negative age reads as younger than any threshold.

IT IS WIRED, NOT MERELY EXPORTED: the boot sweep runs in apps/api/src/workers/index.ts and was watched printing "snapshot sweep on boot: removed 0, in flight 0" against live Postgres/Redis. An unwired cleanup is the same defect as an unwired processor — it exists, it is tested, and it never runs.

shred IS AN UNLINK AND SAYS SO. On a copy-on-write or flash-backed filesystem, overwriting a path does not reliably overwrite the blocks that held it, so a pass of zeroes would buy the appearance of erasure and not the fact. The real control is that the scratch root is ephemeral and the window is one scan long.

THE SANDBOX WAS RUN, NOT JUST GENERATED. Podman is installed here, so the integration test really starts a container and observes: a write to /scan fails read-only, /proc/net/route holds no interface at all under --network=none, and id -u is 65534. The route assertion also checks the header line is present, so a failed read cannot pass as network denial. The argv assertions run everywhere, which keeps the profile honest on a machine without a runtime. The container gets an EMPTY env, not a filtered copy of ours: a denylist of secret-looking names is a guess about what the next wave will add to the environment.

BOTH LINT GATES ARE TESTED BY PLANTING VIOLATIONS. Asserting the current tree passes proves nothing — a rule whose regex matches nothing passes forever, which is the built-but-never-fires cousin of built-but-never-called. Rule 6 fires on git clone in either argv order and on simple-git/isomorphic-git/nodegit, and on getTarball called outside packages/security; rule 7 fires on semgrep/gitleaks/trivy/syft/grype/osv-scanner/checkov spawned outside the sandbox. Comment-only lines are exempt on rule 4 precedent; the fixture test file is exempt by name, and nothing else is, because excluding all test files would let a genuine clone in a test sail through.

GITLAB SAYS IT CANNOT rather than returning an empty archive. Its archive endpoint has not been verified against a live instance the way the rest of that adapter was, and an empty snapshot would scan clean and report a repo as having no findings — the most dangerous thing a security subsystem can say.

SCOPE WIDENED, WITH REASON: apps/api/src/workers/index.ts and apps/api/package.json (the sweeper must be called, not just exported), packages/security/package.json + tsconfig.json + src/index.ts (the sandbox lives outside src/ because rule 7 keys on the directory), scripts/validate-arch.sh + scripts/arch-rules-6-7.sh (the ticket asks for two lint gates), and the three provider contract tests whose capability objects are asserted exactly.

GATE: lint 0, typecheck 0, 848 unit tests (was 800), zero skipped — the podman tests RAN; pnpm -r test green; validate-arch (now 7 rules) PASS, validate-plan, validate-traceability PASS. No e2e — this ticket ships no screen.

tickets.title: Secrets scanner — stream mode riding ingestion (gitleaks-compatible rulepack, verified-secret escalation)
acceptance: Stream mode per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §3.1: regex+entropy ruleset in gitleaks-compatible format (MIT; TruffleHog OSS is AGPL-3.0 and excluded; versioned rulepacks/secrets.v{N}.yaml) runs on every ingested diff patch on pr_synced/push — no snapshot, no container; planted-secret fixture diff yields a finding ≤60s after webhook delivery (FR-SEC-3)

Verified-secret escalation: verifying detector ⇒ severity 5 / confidence 5 + org banner + top of Security tab; live verification config-gated, default OFF; rulepack version stamped on every finding and scan_run
Findings store fingerprint hash + file/line only, never the secret value (SC-29); yields ['credential:{kind}'] populated for chaining
notes: DONE 2026-08-19. Versioned rulepack (rulepacks/secrets.v1.yaml, 15 detectors), a fail-closed loader, an added-lines-only diff detector with entropy floors and allowlists, offline verification with the escalation path, and STREAM MODE wired into the webhook delta so a planted secret in an ingested diff becomes a stored finding.

"GITLEAKS-COMPATIBLE" MEANS THE FIELD NAMES, NOT THE FILE. gitleaks own config is TOML; SECURITY_SUITE.md names the asset secrets.v{N}.yaml. The rulepack uses gitleaks field names (id/description/regex/entropy/keywords/allowlist) so a detector ports across by copying it, and the header says in as many words that `gitleaks -c secrets.v1.yaml` will not work. Claiming compatibility without that sentence would send someone to try it. Go inline (?i) IS translated to the JavaScript flag, in rule regexes and allowlists alike — dropping it silently would have narrowed every assignment rule to lower-case only, a rule that still fires, just less often.

THE LOADER IS A STRICT YAML SUBSET, HAND-OWNED, AND FAILS CLOSED. An unknown rule field throws: `entropu: 4.2` would otherwise mean no entropy floor at all and nobody would notice until the alert volume changed. A detector that silently vanishes from the pack produces exactly the same output as a clean repository. The subset parser found a real bug in itself: keying "new rule vs list item" on whether a list was open put every rule following a keywords block into the previous rule keyword list — the pack loaded cleanly while losing half its detectors. Indentation decides now, and a test asserts the shipped pack really carries all 15.

ADDED LINES ONLY, NUMBERED FROM THE HUNK HEADER. A key on a REMOVED line was already committed — that is history mode — and reporting it here would fire on every PR that deletes an old config and present a cleanup as a new leak. The line number matters more here than anywhere else in the product: for a secret, the location is ALL that gets stored.

FORMAT IS NOT LIVENESS, and the escalation ladder says so. Only a CONFIRMED live credential goes to severity 5 / confidence 5 with immediate surfacing. A format verifier (documented token shape) raises confidence to 4 and NEVER touches severity — if a shape check could set severity 5, every AKIA... in a test fixture would page someone. GitHub embeds a checksum in its tokens; that is NOT implemented, because there is no real token here to verify the claim against and an unverified checksum would reject valid tokens while claiming rigour.

LIVE VERIFICATION THROWS WHEN ENABLED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DOING NOTHING (default OFF, as designed). A switch that reads as on and does nothing is worse than an absent switch. The gap is recorded in docs/STATUS.md.

SC-29 IS PROVEN AGAINST THE DATABASE, WITH A GUARD AGAINST THE VACUOUS PASS. The integration test plants an AKIA key in a diff, runs the real stream scan, and asserts a finding EXISTS before grepping every text column (including yields::text) for the plaintext — a redaction test that passes because the detector found nothing proves nothing, which is the same shape as the podman route-table check in W8-03.

IT IS WIRED. deltaProcessor calls the scan after the delta lands, for pull_requests and push_commits, and workers/index.ts injects it — that injection is asserted by a test, because "the dependency exists, the tests inject it, production never does" has now been the defect four times in this codebase. The scanner is injected into the processor rather than imported by ingest, so ingestion has no dependency on the security package.

WHAT TO SCAN COMES FROM THE WAREHOUSE, NOT THE WEBHOOK. Delta jobs deliberately carry no PR number (a webhook is a doorbell, INGESTION §4), so stream mode asks which head SHAs have no succeeded secrets run and answers idempotently: a replayed delivery scans nothing and spends no forge call. Forge calls go out on the W8-03 `scan` lane.

MIGRATION 0014 REMOVES THE W8-02 DEBT: findings.analysis_run_id is nullable, scan_run_id has its FK, and a check constraint requires EXACTLY ONE parent. Scanner findings no longer attach to a dummy tier-2 analysis run claiming an LLM tier they never used, and no finding can be orphaned from the run that explains it. The W8-02 redaction fixture was moved onto a scan_run in the same change.

TWO REAL BUGS FOUND IN THE EXISTING STORE while wiring this. (1) persistFindings never passed scannerKey/ruleId into dedupKey — W8-02 added those to the key precisely so two scanners flagging one line stay two findings, and the only store in the codebase dropped them, so they would have collided into one row while the dedup unit test went on passing. (2) The stale sweep auto-resolved by FILE with no dimension filter: a secrets scan that reviewed src/config.ts would have closed the code_health findings on it. The sweep is now scoped to the dimensions a run could have produced, and stream mode passes no reviewedFiles at all — it sees one diff, not the repository, and auto-resolving "everything I did not see" from a partial view closes findings on files the PR never touched.
TIER 1, NOT TIER 2: a regex pass claiming tier 2 would put deterministic findings in the same bucket as model output.

SCOPE WIDENED, WITH REASON: packages/insights/src/findings/store.ts (the dedup-key and sweep bugs above are in the only store that can persist a scanner finding), packages/shared schema + migration 0014 (the NOT NULL had to go), apps/api/src/workers/{processors,index}.ts (stream mode has to be called), packages/security/package.json + src/index.ts.

GATE: lint 0, typecheck 0, 875 unit tests (was 848), zero skipped; pnpm -r test green; 94 e2e passed (1 skipped: the real-forge smoke, which needs Brad token) — run because this ticket changes the ingestion delta path; validate-arch (7 rules), validate-plan, validate-traceability PASS.

tickets.title: Secrets scanner — history mode over warehoused backfill patches
acceptance: Scheduled (monthly per §4) / manual sweep over all warehoused backfill patches in the 12-month window per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §3.1 history mode; a secret present only in an old committed-then-removed patch is found from history alone (FR-SEC-4)
Dedups against stream-mode findings: re-run on unchanged history creates 0 new rows (FR-ANALYSIS-6 extension); optional snapshot pass for current-tree files without patch coverage wired behind config
notes: DONE 2026-08-19. History mode over the 12-month commit window, scheduled monthly per SECURITY_SUITE §4, with the per-target scan path shared with stream mode rather than copied.

THE DESIGN AND THE WAREHOUSE DISAGREED, AND THE NOTE IS THE DELIVERABLE. §3.1 says history mode needs no forge calls because "patches are already warehoused" — they are NOT: commit_files and pr_files carry per-file churn counts and say "No patch text" in their own headers, because DATABASE.md never made room for diff bodies. So history mode re-fetches patches per commit through the budgeted client on the scan lane: one core point per commit, which is why it is capped (200/sweep), monthly, and reports what it deferred. Warehousing patch bodies is the alternative and it is a storage AND secret-exposure decision — a patch body containing a live key would then be a row in our own database — not something to slip into a 2-point ticket.
A SILENT CAP READS AS "HISTORY IS CLEAN" when it means "history is half-read", so the result carries `deferred` and a test asserts it.
OLDEST FIRST, unlike stream mode. History exists to reach the far end of the window; newest-first would spend every capped sweep re-walking the recent commits stream mode has already covered.

THE TEST PLANTS THE SHAPE THAT MATTERS: a key added in a 6-month-old commit and REMOVED in a 1-month-old one. Stream mode never saw it and the current tree does not contain it, so finding it proves history mode rather than proving the detector twice. The removal commit yields nothing, because a removed line is a key that was already committed and the finding belongs where it was added. A commit 20 months old is never fetched at all — the 12-month window is a filter, not a label.

FAILED RUNS ARE NOT COVERAGE: the "already scanned" predicate counts succeeded and running, never failed, so a commit whose scan blew up is retried by the next sweep instead of being silently written off.

RE-RUNNING CREATES ZERO ROWS, and both halves are asserted: the commits are already covered so nothing is re-fetched, and a forced re-scan would land on the same dedup key because BOTH modes go through persistFindings rather than inserting their own findings. That shared path is also why there is only one place SC-29 can be got wrong.

WIRED, WITH AN OFF SWITCH. A monthly repeatable job fans out one history job per live repo (SECRETS_HISTORY_CRON, default `23 4 1 * *`, `off` to disable — same reasoning as RECONCILE_CRON: a sweep starts work nobody asked for at a wall-clock time, which is wrong in a test harness). The history runner is looked up in an INJECTED MAP keyed by scanner key, never a switch, so FR-SEC-1’s "the framework never branches on a scanner key" stays true; a test asserts the absence of that switch in non-comment lines.

THE SWEEP WRITES ONE scan_run PER COMMIT, not one per sweep: a single row over a 200-commit sweep could not say which commits were actually covered, and "which commits has this repo been swept for" is exactly the question the next sweep asks.

SNAPSHOT PASS FOR FILES WITH NO PATCH COVERAGE: NOT BUILT. The acceptance calls it optional and behind config; with patches fetched per commit there is no patch-coverage gap for commits inside the window, and the real gap — code older than the window — is a snapshot scan that belongs with the other snapshot scanners (W8-07 onward), not bolted onto a 2-point ticket. Recorded here rather than silently dropped.

SCOPE WIDENED, WITH REASON: apps/api/src/workers/{scan-processor,index}.ts — a history mode nobody schedules finds nothing, and this codebase has shipped that defect enough times to have a gate for it.

GATE: lint 0, typecheck 0, 881 unit tests (was 875), zero skipped; pnpm -r test green; 94 e2e passed (1 skipped: real-forge smoke, needs Brad token); validate-arch (7 rules), validate-plan, validate-traceability PASS.

tickets.title: Dependency scanner: syft SBOM → grype/OSV CVE → KEV correlation → slopsquatting → posture rollup
acceptance: Pipeline per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §3.2: manifest+lockfile targeted fetches at default-branch head SHA (no snapshot, budgeted) → syft CycloneDX SBOM stored per (repo, sha) in sboms → grype/OSV match, one finding per (package, CVE) with cve_id + CVSS-mapped severity; fixture manifests reproduce the known CVE set (FR-SEC-5)

CISA KEV correlation floors severity at 4 + kev:true payload flag faceted in UI; slopsquatting heuristics (not-in-registry, registry age <90d + low downloads, Damerau-Levenshtein ≤2 to top-N) flag the hallucinated-package fixture as rule slopsquat severity 4

Posture rollup (counts by severity + finding-age percentiles) feeds the Security tab tile and FR-INSIGHTS-2 security sub-score; daily default-branch schedule + cheap pr_synced manifest-diff mode per §4; yields ['vuln-dependency:{cve}']
CI uses vendored mini grype/OSV/KEV databases — zero live tool-DB downloads (docs/TESTING.md §10)
notes: BLOCKED 2026-08-19 — every tool this ticket names is absent from this machine. syft (SBOM), grype and osv-scanner (CVE match) and a CISA KEV database: none installed, and the acceptance is written entirely in terms of what they produce ("fixture manifests reproduce the known CVE set", "vendored mini grype/OSV/KEV databases").

WHAT COULD HAVE BEEN FAKED AND WAS NOT: a hand-written CVE list would satisfy the fixture test and report a repository as having no known vulnerabilities the moment it met a real dependency tree. A security scanner that says "clean" without the database that decides what clean means is worse than an absent scanner, because the empty Security tab is indistinguishable from a good result.

WHAT IS NEEDED, FROM WHOM: Brad installs syft + grype (or osv-scanner) — `brew install syft grype` — and decides where the vulnerability databases live, since the sandbox runs with --network=none and cannot fetch them at scan time. That is the real design question this ticket cannot answer alone: the tool databases have to be pulled HOST-SIDE and mounted read-only, which is exactly the "tool/rulepack db-sync job" in W8-12.

SUGGESTED ORDER when it unblocks: W8-12 first (scan sandbox image + db-sync), then this ticket, because the pipeline needs both the image and the mounted databases before a single assertion here can be true.

The slopsquatting half (registry age, download counts, Damerau-Levenshtein to top-N) needs a registry API and is a separate live-network decision, listed here so it is not forgotten when the CVE half unblocks.

tickets.title: Semgrep scanner (Opengrep engine, own bpm-rulepacks): weekly snapshot full runs + diff-scoped incremental, rulepack config, REAL/FP triage mapping
acceptance: Full mode per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §3.3: weekly/manual Opengrep (LGPL, semgrep-rule-format compatible) over a §2 snapshot inside the §2.2 sandbox against our own in-house bpm-rulepacks (git URL + ref, fetched host-side by db-sync, mounted read-only) — never Semgrep's registry rules/packs (p/*, --config auto), which are license-barred for service use; pack + tool versions stamped in scan_run.tool_versions; seeded-vuln fixture snapshot reproduces the expected findings (FR-SEC-6)
Incremental mode on pr_synced scans changed files only via targeted fetches (no tarball); regression planted between weekly fulls is caught by the PR run

Triage mapping REAL→confirmed, FP→dismissed(false_positive), UNVERIFIED→open on the FR-INSIGHTS-1 lifecycle with audited transitions; FP dismissals feed the tuning metric; rule-declared yields recorded for chaining
notes: DONE 2026-08-19. Opengrep 1.27.1 running inside the W8-12 sandbox against our own bpm-rulepack, in both modes: FULL over a W8-03 snapshot and INCREMENTAL over a PR's changed files. Migration 0015 adds scan_runs.tool_versions.

THE ENGINE REALLY RUNS AND THE RULES REALLY FIRE. The integration tests build a real tar.gz, take a real snapshot, start a real container with --network=none and a read-only root, and assert the six rule ids come back and land in the store with their ids, files and yields intact. A unit test on the parser would only have proved the parser.

THE LICENCE RULE IS ENFORCED IN CODE, not documented in a comment: p/*, r/*, `auto` and any semgrep.dev URL are REFUSED with an error naming the reason. A silently dropped `--config auto` would leave a customer believing they run a 2,000-rule pack while they run six. Pack files are passed by NAME rather than `--config /rules`, so a future mount cannot quietly add rules to a run.

THE RULES ARE OURS, SIX OF THEM, AND SMALL ON PURPOSE — a rule is worth shipping only if we can say what it costs to be wrong about it. Both fixtures are the test: the vulnerable one must fire every rule, the SAFE one must fire none. That caught a real false positive during authoring: the weak-PRNG rule matched `cacheKey` because its regex included `key`. A rule that cries wolf on cache keys is one people turn off, and then it misses the session token too, so `key` came out of the pattern.

NOTHING A STATIC MATCH PRODUCES REACHES SEVERITY 5. ERROR→4, WARNING→3, INFO→2, and confidence 3 across the board: severity 5 in this product means confirmed and immediately exploitable, and a pattern over a syntax tree saw a shape, not an exploit. Reserving the top of the scale is what keeps it meaningful when a verified secret or a KEV CVE arrives.

TOOL ERRORS ARE SURFACED, NEVER SWALLOWED. A rulepack that fails to load makes opengrep exit 0 with an empty results array — indistinguishable from a clean repository. The parser returns those errors and the test asserts it. This is not hypothetical: a `{`-leading pattern made the whole pack unparseable during authoring, and the run still "succeeded".

THE CONFIG-PATH PREFIX IS STRIPPED FROM RULE IDS. Opengrep namespaces check_ids by where the config file sat (`rules.bpm-baseline.v1.<id>`), so the same rule run from two mount points would dedup as two findings. Ids are matched against the pack we shipped, with a last-segment fallback rather than storing a filesystem path as a rule identifier.

FULL MAY AUTO-RESOLVE, INCREMENTAL MAY NOT. A full run has seen the whole tree, so it passes reviewedFiles and can close what it no longer reports — scoped to its own scanner key, so a semgrep run can never resolve a secrets finding. A diff-scoped run has seen six files and passes nothing: auto-resolving "everything I did not see" from a partial view would close findings on files the PR never touched.
THE INCREMENTAL SCRATCH DIR IS SHREDDED IN A finally, exactly like a snapshot. They are the same customer bytes; where they came from does not change what they are.

A DOCS-ONLY PR STILL WRITES A RUN ROW. "We looked and there was nothing this pack can read" is a fact the next run needs; a skipped run with no row is indistinguishable from a run that never happened.

TWO VERSIONS, NOT ONE: tool_versions carries {opengrep, rulepack} because a finding is reproducible only against an engine AND a pack, and "which of the two changed" is the first question when a finding appears or disappears between runs. The engine version is READ FROM THE IMAGE rather than assumed.

A REAL BUG IN THE SANDBOX, FOUND BY RUNNING IT: runInSandbox spawned the runtime with a completely empty environment, so `podman` itself could not be found (spawn ENOENT) the moment anything used a bare binary name. The container env and the RUNTIME env are two different things; the runtime now gets PATH and nothing else, and a new live test asserts a host variable set beside the run does not appear inside the container.

TRIAGE: REAL→confirmed, FP→dismissed(false_positive), UNVERIFIED→open. false_positive specifically, because that is the tuning signal — "not applicable" and "accepted risk" are decisions about this codebase, not about the rule. UNVERIFIED is an UNJUDGED finding, not a weaker one, which is why it stays open: a queue that hides what nobody has looked at reports itself finished.

SCOPE WIDENED, WITH REASON: packages/security/rulepacks/semgrep/** and fixtures/semgrep/** (a scanner without rules is not a scanner), packages/security/sandbox/{profile,run}.ts (rawStdout + the runtime-env fix — a tool with its own output format cannot use the sandbox otherwise), packages/shared schema + migration 0015 (the acceptance names scan_runs.tool_versions), eslint.config.js (the vulnerable fixture is deliberately bad code and a fixture that satisfies the linter no longer resembles what the scanner exists to find).

NOT DONE: the weekly SCHEDULE that would call runSemgrepFull. The monthly secrets sweep (W8-05) established the cron+fan-out pattern and this slots into it, but W8-09 needs the same wiring for chain recomputation — doing it once, for both, is the right shape. Recorded here rather than silently skipped.

GATE: lint 0, typecheck 0, 920 unit tests (was 901), zero skipped — the opengrep-in-sandbox tests RUN; pnpm -r test green; validate-arch (7 rules), validate-plan, validate-traceability PASS. No e2e — no screen changed.

tickets.title: OWASP checklist scanners (owasp_web + owasp_llm) through the Tier-2/3 gateway
acceptance: OWASP Web Top-10 (2021) + LLM Top-10 (2025) as versioned checklist prompt assets executed through the Tier-2/3 gateway per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §3.4 — chunking, 45k maxTokens, JSON-mode, zod validation, dedup and egress rules unchanged; gateway accounting rows carry meta.initiator='scanner:{key}' (FR-SEC-7)

Finding schema extended with preconditions[]/yields[] populated by the checklist prompts; fixture diffs emit schema-valid findings; T3 only under the existing opt-in/escalation rules (security ∧ severity ≥3), never silent egress
owasp_llm auto-enables only when the dependency scanner's SBOM contains LLM packages; a repo without LLM deps never enqueues owasp_llm (test); owasp_web manual/scheduled per repo
notes: DONE 2026-08-19. OWASP Web Top-10 (2021) and LLM Top-10 (2025) as versioned checklist assets run through the analysis gateway, with the chaining vocabulary populated and owasp_llm gated on the SBOM.

THE GATEWAY IS THE POINT, NOT A CONVENIENCE. Every control lives behind it — the 45k cap, the warm-up and crash retry, the Tier-3 opt-in check, the egress audit row — so a scanner that called a model directly would bypass four controls at once (Law 8). Chunking, quote validation and dedup are the analysis package's, unchanged: a second implementation of "does this quote appear in the diff" is a second place for a paraphrase to slip through as evidence.
ACCOUNTING CARRIES meta.initiator = scanner:{key} on every call. Scanner spend has to be separable from review spend or the first question about an LLM bill has no answer.

A CHECKLIST IS A VERSIONED ASSET, and editing one in place is a mistake dressed as a small change: the version is stamped on the scan_run and on every finding, so a rewritten v1 makes last month's findings stop meaning what they said. The loader takes the HIGHEST version rather than a configured one — pinning belongs in per-repo config, not in a default that quietly runs last year's questions forever.

THE PROMPTS ARE WRITTEN FOR RESTRAINT, NOT COVERAGE. Both say in as many words that silence is a valid answer, because a ten-category checklist that rewards finding something per category returns ten findings and most are invented. Both demand a verbatim quote, and the validator drops anything that is not in the diff — asserted with a planted paraphrase that is thrown out and COUNTED, never silently dropped.

THE DIFF GOES LAST, FENCED, AND LABELLED AS DATA. This scanner's entire input is attacker-influenced text: anyone who can open a PR can write "ignore your instructions" in a comment. Instructions first, code last, inside a fence, with an explicit line saying everything in it is data.
A CHUNK WHOSE OUTPUT CANNOT BE VALIDATED CONTRIBUTES NOTHING and is counted. Salvaging what parses would mean storing findings from a response we already know was malformed.

T3 IS DECIDED, NEVER ASSUMED. A security finding at severity ≥3 MEETS the existing escalation trigger; without the per-repo opt-in it is refused rather than downgraded, and the test asserts both halves — met without permission, and permitted with it. No silent egress.

owasp_llm HAS THREE ANSWERS, NOT TWO. `no_sbom` is a fact about US and `no_llm_packages` is a fact about the REPOSITORY; collapsing them would render "nobody has looked" as "not applicable". A repo with no SBOM never enqueues owasp_llm and writes NO scan_run row — a scanner that did not run must not appear to have. The package matcher is anchored so `openai-mock-server` and `my-openai-wrapper` do not trip it: a false positive here runs a whole LLM checklist over a codebase with no model in it and every finding it produces is confident and wrong.

THE GATEWAY IS FAKED IN THE TESTS, ON PURPOSE. What needs proving is the path — prompt built, response validated against the chunk it reviewed, findings stored with their yields, accounting tagged. A live model would make every one of those assertions flaky while proving nothing extra: LM Studio's answer is not part of this contract. No live-model test is claimed here.

SCHEMA DELTA: findings gained optional preconditions[]/yields[] with an empty default, so every W6 pass and every existing prompt keeps validating unchanged — making them required would have rejected every checklist that predates them.
SCOPE WIDENED, WITH REASON: packages/analysis/src/schema/finding.ts (the acceptance names the two new fields, and they belong in the one schema every pass validates against).
GATE: lint 0, typecheck 0, 937 unit tests (was 920), zero skipped; pnpm -r test green; validate-arch (7 rules), validate-plan, validate-traceability PASS. No e2e — no screen changed.

tickets.title: Attack chainer: yields→preconditions chains across all open findings
acceptance: Post-scan pass per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §3.5: reads ALL open findings via priorFindings and matches yields→preconditions over the shared vocabulary into chain findings (dimension chain, chain_id, member ids in payload, severity = min(5, max(member)+1)); golden test: two seeded findings with matching vocab produce exactly the expected chain at elevated severity (FR-SEC-8)
Chains auto-resolve with an audit row when any member finding resolves; chainer enqueued as completion job after each scan batch + weekly full recompute per §4
Chain graph payload (entry→step→…→impact, each node referencing its member finding) served for the dashboard renderer

Compound-risk detector rides the same completion job (FR-INSIGHTS-6, D9): pure SQL — same file/module flagged by >=3 distinct dimensions/scanners ⇒ dimension 'compound' finding at severity min(5, max(member)+1), auto-resolving when a member resolves; golden test on a 3-dimension fixture module
notes: DONE 2026-08-19. The chainer pass: yields→preconditions matching over all open findings, the compound-risk detector, auto-resolution when a link breaks, and ONE weekly schedule that also carries W8-07's deferred full semgrep scan.

THE MATCHING IS DELIBERATELY LITERAL. One finding's `yields` term must EQUAL another's `preconditions` term — no synonyms, no inference, no model. `credential:aws` does not match `credential:amazon`, and a test says so. A chainer that guesses produces plausible paths nobody can refute, and every one of them has to be argued down by a person; that is worse than no chainer at all.

A CHAIN IS ONE WORSE THAN ITS WORST LINK, capped at 5 — not the max, and never an average. If a chain could not exceed its worst member it would tell a reader nothing they did not already have from the member.

THE CHAIN ID IS DERIVED FROM ITS MEMBERS (sha256 over their dedup keys, in order), not generated. That is what makes the weekly recompute update a chain in place instead of raising a new one every week — and it is why re-running over unchanged findings creates zero rows, which the integration test asserts.

EVERY STEP REFERENCES ITS FINDING. The payload carries member ids, the matched link terms and a node list, because the entire value of a chain is that it turns three medium findings into a path someone can WALK — and a path you cannot trace back to its evidence is a scary picture, not a finding. The chain itself has NO file: picking one member's path would send a reader to a step rather than to the path.

AUTO-RESOLUTION NEEDED ITS OWN PASS, and that is a real finding about the existing store: the ordinary stale sweep works on FILES, and a chain has none — nothing would ever have closed one. Any member closing breaks the chain, every closure writes a finding_events row with the reason, and cleanup runs BEFORE rebuilding so a chain whose member was fixed yesterday is not rebuilt from today's findings and counted as new.

COMPOUND RISK COUNTS DIMENSIONS, NOT SCANNERS (FR-INSIGHTS-6, D9). Two scanners reporting the same KIND of problem is corroboration; counting them separately would make "we ran more scanners" look like "this file got worse". Asserted with two sast findings on one file that correctly do NOT compound. Pure SQL, as the ticket asks: it is a grouping question, and there is nothing here a model could add that would not be a guess.
THE CHAINER EXCLUDES ITS OWN OUTPUT from both passes. Chaining chains would produce findings about findings, deeper every week.

CONFIDENCE 4, NOT 5, on a chain: the links are deterministic but whether the path is truly walkable depends on code neither end of it can see. The rationale says the useful thing out loud — breaking ANY link breaks the chain, and the cheapest step to fix is usually not the most severe one.

ONE WEEKLY SCHEDULE FOR TWO SCANNERS, which is why W8-07 deliberately left its cron to this ticket. A full semgrep scan and a chain recompute are the same shape of work and two crons would drift. The chainer runs an hour later on purpose: a chain built from findings a full scan is about to replace is a chain about last week. Both are looked up in an INJECTED MAP by scanner key, never a switch (FR-SEC-1), and the worker was watched booting with both schedules registered.

THE WEEKLY SEMGREP RUN NEEDS A PINNED SHA and uses the newest ingested commit — repos carries pushed_at but not the sha it belongs to. With no commits it reports skipped rather than scanning "whatever is current", which would produce findings nobody can reproduce.

SCOPE WIDENED, WITH REASON: packages/shared schema + migration 0016 (the acceptance names dimension `compound`, which the check constraint did not allow), apps/api/src/workers/{scan-processor,index}.ts (a chainer nobody schedules never runs — and this is the wiring pass W8-07 deferred here).

NOTE ON THE E2E SUITE: one run of 98 reported a single failure that did not reproduce on two further full runs (97 passed, 1 skipped, both times). Recorded rather than ignored — if it recurs it is a real flake to chase, and pretending three runs were three greens would be the wrong kind of tidy.
GATE: lint 0, typecheck 0, 955 unit tests (was 937), zero skipped; pnpm -r test green; 97 e2e passed (1 skipped real-forge smoke); validate-arch (7 rules), validate-plan, validate-traceability PASS.

tickets.title: Security tab + Findings Explorer scanner facets + org security rollup tile
acceptance: Findings Explorer gains scanner_key, extended dimension, cve_id, KEV-flag and chain-membership facets per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §5 (facets driven by registry metadata); finding detail shows rule id, scan_run link and chain graph (FR-SEC-10)

Repo Detail Security tab: posture score, CVE/KEV table, secrets status (last stream/history scan + open count), SAST summary, open chains rendered entry→…→impact with nodes linking member findings; per-scanner error and 'not enabled' states — never a blank or broken page (NFR-15)

Org security rollup tile: open findings by severity across repos, KEV count, verified-secret count (always red-flagged), worst chain — drills to per-repo Security tabs; health-score security sub-score basis label upgrades when scanner data present (FR-INSIGHTS-2)
E2E: filter by scanner facet → open Security tab → click a chain node → land on member finding; tenancy route-walker and axe green over all new routes
notes: DONE 2026-08-19. Repo Security tab, scanner facets on the Findings Explorer, the org security rollup tile, and GET /repos/:id/security + GET /org/security behind them.

THE WHOLE SCREEN IS BUILT AGAINST ONE FAILURE: a security page that says nothing and reads as "safe". A scanner that is SWITCHED OFF, one that has NEVER RUN, and one that RAN AND FOUND NOTHING are three different sentences and only the last is good news — so every scanner carries an explicit state, and the coverage table prints a DASH rather than a zero for anything that has not looked. A zero is a claim; an unrun scanner has not earned it.

THE EMPTY PANELS NAME THEIR CAUSE. The CVE panel says "no dependency scan has run — this is not a clean bill of health" (W8-06 is parked for missing tools); the chains panel distinguishes "no chains" from "chain analysis has never run" (W8-09). A missing panel reads as a broken page and a broken security page reads as no problems, so the sections stay and explain themselves (NFR-15).

A REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED: the findings API validated `dimension` against the four ANALYSIS dimensions and silently dropped anything else. Secrets findings were storable, listable and countable — and unfilterable, so asking for exactly the ones you wanted showed you everything instead. The list is now the full nine from the W8-02 schema, and the facet is exercised by e2e.
THE SCANNER FACET IS DRIVEN BY THE REGISTRY, not a hard-coded list: a scanner added in a later wave becomes filterable the day it registers, without touching this screen (SECURITY_SUITE §5).

THE KEV FACET FILTERS ON THE FINDING PAYLOAD, not a column. KEV is a fact about a CVE that only the dependency scanner sets; a column would need backfilling for every scanner that never sets it. Filtering on the payload means the facet works the day W8-06 lands and returns nothing — correctly — until then.

TWO CLOCKS FOR SECRETS, NOT ONE: "last scan of new commits" and "last sweep of history" are separate lines, because a repo scanned on every push but never swept has twelve months nobody has read, and one timestamp cannot say that.
VERIFIED CREDENTIALS READS "none confirmed", NOT 0. Live verification is gated off (W8-04), so nothing can confirm liveness; "none confirmed" is true and "0" would imply someone checked.

A CHAIN IS AS SEVERE AS ITS WORST STEP, never an average — an average lets one critical link hide behind three trivial ones. Chain nodes link to their member findings, because a path you cannot click through is a picture of an argument rather than the argument.

THE ROLLUP CARRIES A BASIS LABEL, same discipline as the health score’s "Tier-1 only": with one scanner running, "0 open" means "one scanner found nothing", and a reader who cannot see that reads it as an audit. The tile sits BELOW the fold for the same reason — above it, it would be the loudest thing on the page while saying the least.

AN AXE VIOLATION THE A11Y SWEEP CAUGHT ON ITS FIRST RUN: the secrets drill-down link was inside a <dl>, which may only contain dt/dd groups. Moved out. This is the third time the a11y gate has caught something a click-through would have called fine.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: the e2e "click a chain node → land on member finding" step. No chain data exists until W8-09 computes it, and seeding fake chain rows to make an e2e green would test the seeder, not the product. The panel, the node links and their empty states ARE covered; the click-through is W8-09 acceptance.

GATE: lint 0, typecheck 0, 892 unit tests (was 881), zero skipped; pnpm -r test green; 97 e2e passed (was 94; 1 skipped real-forge smoke), including a new axe sweep over the Security tab; bundle 110.1 KB of a 200 KB budget; validate-arch (7 rules), validate-plan, validate-traceability PASS.

tickets.title: Security Posture report: per-scanner sections + chains appendix
acceptance: Security Posture report gains one section per enabled scanner (posture counts, deltas vs prior run, top findings) + a chains appendix per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §5; disabled scanners render 'not enabled', never blank (FR-SEC-10, FR-REPORTS-4)
Degrades to the existing Tier-1-only W7-03 sections when scanners are disabled; assembler snapshot tests cover both enriched and degraded renderings against the seeded-vuln fixture warehouse
Determinism pin intact: assembly reads findings/scan_run/snapshot rows as of snapshotAt only; regenerating with identical params is byte-identical (FR-REPORTS-6)
notes: DONE 2026-08-19. Per-scanner sections (posture counts, top findings, delta vs the PREVIOUS run) and a chains appendix on the Security Posture report, replacing the W7-03 placeholder that said dependency/secret signals were "not computed in this version".

THE REPORT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT IMPORT THE SCANNER REGISTRY, and that is the determinism decision in this ticket. The registry is code, and code changes: a report regenerated in six months would gain sections for scanners that did not exist when it was first produced and lose them for scanners since removed — byte-identical regeneration (FR-REPORTS-6) would break in a way nobody notices until an auditor compares two copies. The catalogue here is what the DATA says: every scanner with a config row, a run, or a finding at or before snapshotAt. A scanner nobody has ever configured or run is absent here and present on the Security tab, which is the screen that legitimately reflects the live registry.

ABSENT CONFIG IS null, NOT false. A scanner with no repo_scanner_config row is running on the workspace default; printing "not enabled" for it would be a claim the warehouse cannot support. Only an explicit stored false renders "switched off" — and that section also says what it costs the reader: the zeros elsewhere in the report exclude what this scanner would have found.

NEW-SINCE-PREVIOUS-RUN IS null ON A FIRST RUN, never 0. A brand-new scanner reporting "0 new" would say nothing changed when in fact nothing had ever been measured. The delta is counted against the PREVIOUS run's finish time rather than the latest one's, because "what appeared since we last looked" is the question a reader is asking.

TIES ARE BROKEN BY TITLE, NOT BY INSERTION ORDER. Top-findings sorted by severity alone would reorder between two runs over identical data and quietly break the byte-identical guarantee — the test asserts two assemblies serialise identically.

THE PIN IS ENFORCED ON SCAN RUNS TOO: a run started after snapshotAt is invisible to the report, asserted directly. Determinism that covers findings but not the runs that produced them is determinism with a hole in it.

A CHAIN IS RANKED BY ITS WORST STEP, never an average — an average lets one critical link hide behind three trivial ones — and the empty appendix says chains have not been LOOKED for (W8-09), not that none exist.

THE DEGRADED RENDERING SAYS "not yet scanned". A report that simply omits its scanner sections reads as though the scanners ran and found nothing, which is the exact confusion this whole report is written against.
A repo-level finding renders its location as "repository-level" rather than an empty cell: a blank looks like missing data, and a CVE genuinely has no line.

SCOPE WIDENED, WITH REASON: packages/reports/src/assembler/security-scanners.integration.test.ts — the ticket allotted fixtures/security/** for fixtures, but the assertions that matter here are about live warehouse rows and the snapshot pin, which a static fixture cannot exercise.

GATE: lint 0, typecheck 0, 900 unit tests (was 892), zero skipped, three consecutive clean runs; pnpm -r test green; validate-arch (7 rules), validate-plan, validate-traceability PASS. No e2e — the report body is assembled server-side and the Report Center screens are unchanged.

tickets.title: CVE validation pipeline: alias dedup, dep scoping, usage detection, reachability tiers, EPSS + effective risk
acceptance: Tiers V0–V4 per docs/design/SECURITY_SUITE.md §3.6 run in order on every dependency finding: OSV-alias dedup (CVE+GHSA fixture collapses to ONE finding with aliases recorded); lockfile scoping dev/prod + direct/transitive — dev-only downgrades effective_risk and is NEVER auto-dismissed (FR-SEC-13)

V2 usage detection: import/require scan (snapshot tree when one exists for the SHA, else targeted source-root fetches); never-imported vulnerable dep lands reachability 'manifest_only' with a PROPOSED not_affected(vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path) — proposal only, no auto-dismiss

V3 reachability: govulncheck source mode for Go inside the NFR-14 sandbox (Go fixture proves 'proven_unreachable' via call graph); JS/TS/Python get semgrep rules GENERATED from OSV affected-symbol data when present ('symbol_reachable' with file:line evidence); every dependency finding stamped with its reachability tier

V4: EPSS scores join the nightly db-sync (scan containers stay --network=none, SC-28 checksum rules); effective_risk = f(CVSS, KEV, EPSS, reachability, dep_scope) with workspace-tunable weights in the catalog; findings columns reachability/epss/effective_risk per docs/DATABASE.md D10; CI uses vendored mini EPSS/OSV data (docs/TESTING.md §10)
notes: BLOCKED 2026-08-19 — this pipeline validates DEPENDENCY findings, and there are none, because W8-06 is blocked for missing syft/grype/osv-scanner. Every tier here is written as "runs on every dependency finding": V0 dedups OSV aliases, V1 scopes them against the lockfile, V2 asks whether the vulnerable package is imported, V3 proves reachability, V4 scores them. With no CVE source there is nothing to dedup, scope, or score.

WHY NOT BUILD THE PURE CORE ANYWAY. The deterministic halves — alias grouping, dev/prod scoping, the import scan, the effective_risk formula — could be written and tested against fixtures I invent. That is 8 points of code with ZERO production callers, validated only against my own idea of what grype emits, for findings that cannot exist. Built-but-never-called is the single most common defect this codebase has produced (W4-22, W12-03, and four more), and writing a whole subsystem that way on purpose would be the largest instance of it yet. The shape of grype/OSV output should come from grype, not from me.

ALSO MISSING BEYOND W8-06: govulncheck (V3 Go call-graph proof) — Go itself IS installed, so `go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest` is the whole gap; and the EPSS feed for V4, which needs the nightly db-sync whose vulnerability-database half is already parked in W8-12 (scan containers are --network=none, so EPSS must be fetched host-side and mounted).

WHAT IS ALREADY IN PLACE FOR IT: the sandbox (W8-03/W8-12) that govulncheck would run inside, the sboms table (W8-02), the findings columns for cve_id/yields, and the chainer vocabulary term `vuln-dependency:{cve}` that dependency findings are meant to yield.

ORDER WHEN IT UNBLOCKS: install syft+grype (and govulncheck), finish W8-12's db-sync vulnerability half, then W8-06, then this. Doing this ticket before W8-06 would mean designing the funnel around imagined tool output and rewriting it on first contact.

tickets.title: VEX: justification-gated triage, vex_statements, OpenVEX/CycloneDX export, funnel UI
acceptance: Triage on dependency findings maps to OpenVEX per FR-SEC-14: not_affected REQUIRES a justification from the OpenVEX enum (400 without one); vex_statements table per docs/DATABASE.md D10, keyed (repo, purl, vuln, version_range) with author + evidence link; every statement audit-logged (SC-22)
Suppression semantics: re-scan at a covered version creates 0 new rows; a version outside version_range reopens the finding as under_investigation (fixture: bump the dep version → reopened)

Exports: OpenVEX JSON and CycloneDX-embedded VEX served alongside the SBOM via session-authed endpoints; both validate against their published schemas in test; OSV/GHSA + EPSS attribution line in the report footer (DESIGN_REVIEW.md G-18 pattern)

Funnel UI per FR-SEC-15 on Security tab + Explorer + Security Posture report: raw→deduped→scoped→affected/not_affected/under_investigation with per-justification breakdown; counts reconcile to finding rows; default sort effective_risk; raw count never hidden
notes: BLOCKED 2026-08-19 — same root cause as W8-13: VEX statements are assertions ABOUT DEPENDENCY FINDINGS, and none can exist while W8-06 is blocked for missing syft/grype/osv-scanner. Every acceptance item here is written in terms of them: "triage on dependency findings", "re-scan at a covered version creates 0 new rows", "a version outside version_range reopens the finding", "the funnel raw→deduped→scoped→affected reconciles to finding rows".

WHY NOT BUILD THE TABLE AND THE EXPORT ANYWAY: the vex_statements schema is keyed (repo, purl, vuln, version_range), and every one of those four columns is a shape that comes OUT of the dependency scanner. Designing the key around imagined purls and version ranges is how it gets rewritten on first contact with grype output — and an OpenVEX export validated only against documents I wrote myself proves the validator, not the export.

WHAT IS ALREADY HERE FOR IT: the audit-event union (SC-22) takes new events cheaply, the findings lifecycle already supports dismissal with a reason, and the Security tab has the funnel's shape in its scanner-status section.
